knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logical implication structure of constraint qualifications
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix a problem class \(\mathcal P\). Each constraint qualification \(Q\) is a predicate on feasible-point pairs \((P,\bar x)\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise logical comparison of constraint-qualification predicates on a fixed problem class, distinct from comparing only their downstream consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the implication relation on constraint qualifications by
\[
Q_1\succeq_{\mathrm{imp}}Q_2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\forall(P,\bar x)\in\mathcal P,\ Q_1(P,\bar x)\Rightarrow Q_2(P,\bar x).
\]
The constraint-qualification implication structure is the resulting preorder. Qualifications \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) are implication-equivalent when both \(Q_1\succeq_{\mathrm{imp}}Q_2\) and \(Q_2\succeq_{\mathrm{imp}}Q_1\) hold. They are incomparable when neither universal implication holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a fixed class of constrained problems, qualification \(Q_1\) implies qualification \(Q_2\) when every feasible point satisfying \(Q_1\) also satisfies \(Q_2\). This universal implication defines a preorder. Mutual implication gives equivalence, while failure of both implications gives incomparability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q_1\succeq_{\mathrm{imp}}Q_2\iff\forall(P,\bar x)\in\mathcal P,\ Q_1(P,\bar x)\Rightarrow Q_2(P,\bar x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(S_Q=\{(P,\bar x)\in\mathcal P:Q(P,\bar x)\}\), then \(Q_1\succeq_{\mathrm{imp}}Q_2\) is equivalent to \(S_{Q_1}\subseteq S_{Q_2}\).
special_cases_latex: An implication may hold on convex programs but fail on the larger class of smooth nonconvex programs; hence \(\mathcal P\) is part of the definition.
immediate_consequences_latex: The quotient by mutual implication is partially ordered.
A strict implication requires \(Q_1\succeq_{\mathrm{imp}}Q_2\) together with a counterexample to \(Q_2\succeq_{\mathrm{imp}}Q_1\).
boundary_notes: This record defines how implications are represented, but it asserts no specific classical implication chain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and boundedness regimes of the KKT multiplier set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a feasible point \(\bar x\) of \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\), \(h_j(x)=0\), and \(x\in X_0\), define the KKT multiplier set \(\Lambda(\bar x)\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\times\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional continuously differentiable nonlinear programming with a closed convex set constraint and the normal-cone form of stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The multiplier set at \( ar x\) is
\[
\Lambda( ar x)=\{(\lambda,\mu):\lambda\geq0,\ \lambda_i g_i( ar x)=0,\ 0\in
abla f( ar x)+	extstyle\sum_i\lambda_i
abla g_i( ar x)+\sum_j\mu_j
abla h_j( ar x)+N_{X_0}( ar x)\}.
\]
The existence regime is \(\Lambda( ar x)
eq\varnothing\). The bounded-multiplier regime is \(\Lambda( ar x)
eq\varnothing\) and \(\sup\{\|(\lambda,\mu)\|:(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda( ar x)\}<\infty\). The unbounded regime has a nonempty but unbounded multiplier set; the failure regime has \(\Lambda( ar x)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT multiplier set \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) contains all nonnegative inequality multipliers and free equality multipliers satisfying stationarity and complementary slackness at \(\bar x\). Multiplier existence means this set is nonempty. Boundedness means it is nonempty and bounded in the finite-dimensional multiplier space. Nonempty-unbounded and empty sets define the other two regimes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Lambda(\bar x)=\varnothing,\quad \Lambda(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\ \text{unbounded},\quad\text{or}\quad \varnothing\neq\Lambda(\bar x)\ \text{bounded}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because the cited multiplier set is closed, a nonempty bounded \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is compact in finite dimensions.
special_cases_latex: Under Robinson regularity at a local minimizer, the cited result gives a nonempty bounded multiplier set.
With \(X_0=\mathbb R^n\), the normal-cone term vanishes.
immediate_consequences_latex: Boundedness rules out sequences of KKT multipliers whose norms diverge while the primal point remains fixed.
boundary_notes: Boundedness does not imply uniqueness.
Existence at an arbitrary feasible nonminimizer is not guaranteed by a constraint qualification alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Existence Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT multiplier existence under Guignard's constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing a differentiable function \(f\) subject to \(h_j(x)=0\) and \(g_i(x)\le0\). Let \( ar x\) be a local minimizer and suppose Guignard's constraint qualification holds there, namely the polar of the tangent cone equals the polar of the linearized cone. Then there exist equality multipliers \(\lambda_j\in\mathbb R\) and inequality multipliers \(\mu_i\ge0\) such that \[
abla f( ar x)+\sum_j\lambda_j
abla h_j( ar x)+\sum_i\mu_i
abla g_i( ar x)=0,\qquad \mu_i g_i( ar x)=0.\] Hence every stronger qualification implying GCQ also guarantees existence of a KKT multiplier vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a differentiable local minimum, GCQ yields equality and nonnegative inequality multipliers satisfying stationarity and complementarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Multiplier Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness of the KKT multiplier set under MFCQ at a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer of a continuously differentiable nonlinear program, and assume MFCQ at \(\bar x\). Define the KKT multiplier set \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) by stationarity, nonnegativity of inequality multipliers, and complementarity. Then \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) is nonempty and compact. In particular, there is a constant \(M<\infty\) such that \[\|\lambda\|+\|\mu\|\le M\qquad\text{for every }(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x).\] MFCQ excludes a nonzero abnormal multiplier direction, so no unbounded recession direction can occur in the closed multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a smooth local minimum satisfying MFCQ, the KKT multiplier set is nonempty, closed, and bounded, hence compact.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Multiplier Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Opposing affine inequalities give an unbounded KKT multiplier ray when MFCQ fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the problem of minimizing \(f(x)=0\) over \(x\in\mathbb R\) subject to \(g_1(x)=x\le0\) and \(g_2(x)=-x\le0\). Its feasible set is \(\{0\}\), and \(\bar x=0\) is a global minimizer. At \(\bar x\), the KKT multiplier set is \[\Lambda(0)=\{(\mu_1,\mu_2)\in\mathbb R_+^2:\mu_1-mu_2=0\}=\{(t,t):t\ge0\}.\] Thus \(\Lambda(0)\) is nonempty and unbounded, while MFCQ fails at \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the constant objective with the opposing constraints x less than or equal to zero and negative x less than or equal to zero, the unique feasible point is globally optimal, MFCQ fails, and the KKT multiplier set is the unbounded ray consisting of all pairs (t,t) with t nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda(0)=\{(t,t):t\ge0\}\) is unbounded, and MFCQ fails at \(0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LICQ Is Sufficient but Not Necessary for Multiplier Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependent active gradients with a singleton nonnegative multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x^2\) subject to \(g_1(x)=x\le0\) and \(g_2(x)=2x\le0\). At the global minimizer \(\bar x=0\), both inequalities are active and their gradients are linearly dependent, so LICQ fails. Stationarity and dual feasibility require \[\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=0,	\qquad \lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0,\] whose unique solution is \((0,0)\). Thus LICQ failure does not imply multiplier nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent active gradients can still yield a unique multiplier when nonnegativity forces every multiplier to vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{LICQ}\) fails at \(0\), but \(\mathcal M(0)=\{(0,0)\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: LICQ Is Sufficient but Not Necessary for Multiplier Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Lambda(\bar x)\) be the KKT multiplier set for a differentiable nonlinear program at a fixed feasible point \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming; uniqueness is defined at a fixed primal point and is distinct from uniqueness of the primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The multiplier at \(\bar x\) is unique precisely when
\[
\Lambda(\bar x)=\{(\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\}
\]
for some multiplier pair. The multiple-multiplier regime is \(|\Lambda(\bar x)|>1\), while the no-multiplier regime is \(\Lambda(\bar x)=\varnothing\). For the standard mixed KKT system, linear independence of the equality gradients and active inequality gradients implies that any multiplier satisfying stationarity and complementarity is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier uniqueness means that the KKT multiplier set at the fixed primal point \(\bar x\) is a singleton. A nonempty set with more than one element is the multiple-multiplier regime, and an empty set is the no-multiplier regime. Under LICQ, the coefficients in the stationarity representation by equality and active-inequality gradients are unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{unique multiplier at }\bar x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |\Lambda(\bar x)|=1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If two multiplier pairs satisfy the KKT system, uniqueness is equivalent to their difference being zero.
Under LICQ, uniqueness follows from linear independence of the gradients carrying possibly nonzero multiplier coefficients.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, full column rank of the equality Jacobian makes the Lagrange multiplier unique whenever it exists.
Inactive inequality multipliers are fixed at zero by complementarity and do not create nonuniqueness.
immediate_consequences_latex: LICQ at a local minimizer gives existence and uniqueness of the KKT multiplier under the standard smooth hypotheses.
boundary_notes: MFCQ generally provides existence and boundedness, not uniqueness.
Strict complementarity alone does not imply multiplier uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Karush–Kuhn–Tucker system for a smooth nonlinear program
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and \(h_j(x)=0\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), where all functions are continuously differentiable. Define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i(x)+\sum_j\mu_jh_j(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming with the sign convention \(g_i\leq0\). This is a system definition, not an assertion that every local minimizer satisfies it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A triple \((x,\lambda,\mu)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^p\) is a KKT point when
\[
\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)=0,\qquad g(x)\leq0,\qquad h(x)=0,
\]
\[
\lambda\geq0,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
These are, respectively, stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness. The pair \((\lambda,\mu)\) is a KKT or Lagrange multiplier pair at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth problem with inequalities \(g_i(x)\leq0\) and equalities \(h_j(x)=0\), a KKT point is a primal–multiplier triple satisfying stationarity of the Lagrangian, primal feasibility, nonnegativity of inequality multipliers, and complementary slackness \(\lambda_i g_i(x)=0\). Equality multipliers are unrestricted in sign.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\nabla_xL=0,\quad g\leq0,\quad h=0,\quad\lambda\geq0,\quad\lambda\odot g=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Complementarity is equivalent to \(\lambda_i=0\) for every inactive inequality \(i\) with \(g_i(x)<0\).

Stationarity may be written \(-
abla f(x)=\sum_i\lambda_i
abla g_i(x)+\sum_j\mu_j
abla h_j(x)\).
special_cases_latex: With no inequalities, the system reduces to equality-constrained Lagrange stationarity and feasibility.
With no equalities, only nonnegative inequality multipliers and complementarity remain.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only active inequalities can carry positive multipliers.
Under an appropriate constraint qualification, every smooth local minimizer admits at least one multiplier pair satisfying this system.
boundary_notes: Without a constraint qualification, a local minimizer need not admit normalized KKT multipliers.
Reversing the inequality convention reverses the associated multiplier sign convention.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\), \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\), and \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_p)\) be continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A classification of the smooth finite-dimensional KKT system according to whether equality, inequality, or both types of scalar constraints are present.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The KKT system associated with \(\min f(x)\) is selected by the constraint regime: equality-only \((m=0)\), inequality-only \((p=0)\), or mixed \((m,p>0)\). Uniformly, it is
\[
\nabla f(x)+\nabla g(x)^T\lambda+\nabla h(x)^T\mu=0,\quad g(x)\leq0,\quad h(x)=0,
\]
\[
\lambda\geq0,\quad\lambda\odot g(x)=0,
\]
with every equation or multiplier block belonging to an absent constraint family deleted. Equality multipliers \(\mu\) are free; inequality multipliers \(\lambda\) are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT systems split into three regimes. Equality-only problems retain stationarity, equality feasibility, and free equality multipliers. Inequality-only problems retain stationarity, inequality feasibility, nonnegative multipliers, and complementarity. Mixed problems contain both blocks. The uniform displayed system specializes to each regime by deleting the absent constraint block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[m=0:\ \mathrm{KKT}_{=};\qquad p=0:\ \mathrm{KKT}_{\leq};\qquad m,p>0:\ \mathrm{KKT}_{\mathrm{mixed}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: All three regimes are instances of \(0\in\nabla f(x)+DG(x)^*y+N_K(G(x))\) for a suitable product constraint set \(K\), though this abstract form is not needed for the scalar definition.
special_cases_latex: The unconstrained regime \(m=p=0\) reduces to \(\nabla f(x)=0\).
Bound constraints are inequality constraints with coordinate gradients.
immediate_consequences_latex: Complementarity and multiplier sign restrictions appear only in regimes containing inequalities.
boundary_notes: Set constraints \(x\in X_0\) add a normal-cone term and are outside this scalar-only classification.
This definition does not claim necessity or sufficiency of any regime without further hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained KKT Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order KKT system for smooth equality-constrained minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), a feasible point \( ar x\) satisfies the equality-constrained KKT condition if there is \(
u\in\mathbb R^p\) such that \[h( ar x)=0,\qquad 
abla f( ar x)+Dh( ar x)^{\mathsf T}
u=0.\] The equality multipliers are unrestricted in sign. If \( ar x\) is a local minimizer and \(Dh( ar x)\) has full row rank, such a multiplier exists; the same rank condition also makes it unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality-constrained KKT consists of primal feasibility and Lagrangian stationarity with unrestricted equality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\exists
u\in\mathbb R^p:\ h( ar x)=0\ 	ext{and}\ 
abla f( ar x)+Dh( ar x)^{\mathsf T}
u=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality KKT Is Not Sufficient for a Minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of first-order equality KKT sufficiency without convexity or second-order information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2}-x^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad y=0,\] the point \((0,0)\) is feasible and satisfies KKT with \(\nu=0\). Nevertheless, \(f(t,0)=-t^2<f(0,0)=0\) for every \(t\ne0\), so \((0,0)\) is a strict local maximum along the feasible manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality KKT stationarity alone does not distinguish minima from maxima or saddles.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (0,0)\text{ satisfies KKT but is not a local minimizer}.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality KKT Is Not Sufficient for a Minimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent-Space Form of Equality KKT Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent geometric formulation at a regular equality-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(h( ar x)=0\) and \(Dh( ar x)\) has full row rank, then \[\exists
u:\ 
abla f( ar x)+Dh( ar x)^{\mathsf T}
u=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 
abla f( ar x)^{\mathsf T}d=0\ 	ext{for every }d\in\ker Dh( ar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular equality-feasible point, KKT stationarity is equivalent to objective-gradient orthogonality to the tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\nabla f(\bar x)\in\operatorname{range}Dh(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}\iff\nabla f(\bar x)\perp\ker Dh(\bar x).

notation.meaning: linearized tangent space of the equality constraints

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional equality-constrained optimization; there are no inequality multipliers or complementarity equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(L(x,\mu)=f(x)+\mu^Th(x)\). A pair \((x,\mu)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\) satisfies the equality-constrained KKT system when
\[
h(x)=0,\qquad \nabla_xL(x,\mu)=\nabla f(x)+\nabla h(x)^T\mu=0.
\]
The multiplier \(\mu\) is unrestricted in sign. If \(\nabla h(x)\) has full row rank, a multiplier satisfying stationarity is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equality-constrained problem, the KKT system consists of equality feasibility \(h(x)=0\) and stationarity of the equality Lagrangian \(\nabla f(x)+\nabla h(x)^T\mu=0\). Equality multipliers \(\mu\) have no sign restriction. Full row rank of the equality Jacobian makes the multiplier unique whenever it exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[h(x)=0,\qquad\nabla f(x)+\nabla h(x)^T\mu=0,\qquad\mu\in\mathbb R^p.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Stationarity is equivalent to \(-\nabla f(x)\in\operatorname{range}(\nabla h(x)^T)\).
special_cases_latex: For one equality \(h(x)=0\), stationarity is \(\nabla f(x)+\mu\nabla h(x)=0\).
For affine equalities \(h(x)=Ax-b\), the system is \(Ax=b\) and \(\nabla f(x)+A^T\mu=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: No complementary-slackness relation is present because equalities cannot be inactive.
boundary_notes: At a rank-deficient feasible point, multipliers may fail to be unique.
This system is a first-order stationarity definition, not by itself a sufficient condition for a local minimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Constrained KKT Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order KKT system using the convention \(g_i(x)\le 0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le 0\), a pair \((\bar x,\lambda)\) satisfies the inequality-constrained KKT system precisely when \[g_i(\bar x)\le0,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\quad(1\le i\le m),\] and \[\nabla f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\nabla g_i(\bar x)=0.\] At a local minimizer these conditions are necessary under an appropriate constraint qualification, such as LICQ or MFCQ; absent such a qualification, a KKT multiplier need not exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inequality KKT combines feasibility, nonnegative multipliers, complementary slackness, and Lagrangian stationarity.
assumptions_latex: For necessity at a local minimizer, a KKT constraint qualification holds at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0=\nabla f(\bar x)+\sum_i\lambda_i\nabla g_i(\bar x),\quad g(\bar x)\le0,\quad \lambda\ge0,\quad \lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inequality KKT Is Not Sufficient Without Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order KKT insufficiency in a smooth inequality-only problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}-x^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x^2-1\le0.\] The interior feasible point \(x^\star=0\) satisfies KKT with \(\lambda=0\), but \(f(t)=-t^2<f(0)=0\) for every sufficiently small \(t\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonconvex problem, satisfying inequality KKT does not guarantee local optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star=0\text{ satisfies KKT but is not a local minimizer}.
knowledge_statements.title: Inequality KKT Is Not Sufficient Without Convexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-Qualification Failure Can Destroy KKT Necessity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inequality-only optimum having no KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad x^2\le0,\] the unique feasible point \(x^\star=0\) is globally optimal. Since \(g'(0)=0\), stationarity would require \(1+\lambda g'(0)=1=0\), which is impossible. Both LICQ and MFCQ fail at \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a constraint qualification, a smooth inequality-constrained global minimizer may have no KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star=0\text{ is optimal but has no KKT multiplier}.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Qualification Failure Can Destroy KKT Necessity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Gradient Form of Inequality KKT Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of stationarity and complementarity to active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I( ar x)=\{i:g_i( ar x)=0\}\). At a feasible point, complementarity is equivalent to \(\lambda_i=0\) for \(i
otin I( ar x)\). Hence KKT stationarity is equivalently \[-
abla f( ar x)=\sum_{i\in I( ar x)}\lambda_i
abla g_i( ar x),\qquad \lambda_i\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only active inequalities appear in KKT stationarity, with nonnegative coefficients generating the negative objective gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\nabla f(\bar x)\in\operatorname{cone}\{\nabla g_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Gradient Form of Inequality KKT Stationarity

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), where \(f\) and all \(g_i\) are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional inequality-constrained optimization using the \(g_i\leq0\) sign convention and no equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x)\). A pair \((x,\lambda)\) satisfies the inequality-constrained KKT system when
\[
\nabla f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\nabla g_i(x)=0,\qquad g_i(x)\leq0,
\]
\[
\lambda_i\geq0,\qquad\lambda_i g_i(x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Thus an inactive inequality has zero multiplier, whereas an active inequality may have a zero or positive multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For inequalities \(g_i(x)\leq0\), the KKT system requires stationarity of \(f+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i\), primal feasibility, nonnegative multipliers, and componentwise complementary slackness. An inequality with \(g_i(x)<0\) must have \(\lambda_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\nabla f(x)+\nabla g(x)^T\lambda=0,\quad g(x)\leq0,\quad\lambda\geq0,\quad\lambda\odot g(x)=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing slack values \(s=-g(x)\geq0\), complementarity becomes \(\lambda\geq0\), \(s\geq0\), and \(\lambda\odot s=0\).
special_cases_latex: For one inequality, either \(g(x)<0\) and \(\lambda=0\), or \(g(x)=0\) and \(\lambda\geq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The stationarity sum may be restricted to the active index set \(I(x)=\{i:g_i(x)=0\}\).
boundary_notes: With the alternative convention \(c_i(x)\geq0\), the Lagrangian is commonly written with a minus sign.
KKT necessity at a local minimizer requires an appropriate constraint qualification.

\(\exists(\lambda,

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed KKT Necessity Can Fail Without a Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Genuinely mixed smooth optimum having no KKT multiplier pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad y=0,\quad x^2\le0.\] The unique feasible point \((0,0)\) is globally optimal. There, the equality gradient is \((0,1)\) and the inequality gradient is \((0,0)\), so stationarity would require \[(1,0)+\nu(0,1)+\lambda(0,0)=(0,0),\] which is impossible. LICQ and MFCQ fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-constraint optimum need not admit KKT multipliers when its active constraints fail a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (0,0)\text{ is globally optimal but has no mixed KKT multiplier pair}.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed KKT Necessity Can Fail Without a Constraint Qualification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set form of the mixed stationarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For feasible \( ar x\), let \(I( ar x)=\{i:g_i( ar x)=0\}\). Mixed KKT is equivalently \[-
abla f( ar x)=Dh( ar x)^{\mathsf T}
u+\sum_{i\in I( ar x)}\lambda_i
abla g_i( ar x),\qquad \lambda_i\ge0,\] with all inactive inequality multipliers zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed KKT combines an unrestricted equality-gradient span with a nonnegative cone of active inequality gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\nabla f(\bar x)\in\operatorname{range}Dh(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}+\operatorname{cone}\{\nabla g_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex KKT Optimality Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient KKT characterization under differentiable convexity and Slater regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) and \(g_i:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) for \(1\le i\le m\) be differentiable convex functions, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p	imes n}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(1\le i\le m\) and \(Ax=b\). Suppose there exists \(x^s\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(Ax^s=b\) and \(g_i(x^s)<0\) for every \(1\le i\le m\). Then a feasible point \(x^\star\in\mathbb R^n\) is a global minimizer if and only if there exist \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(
u\in\mathbb R^p\) such that \[
abla f(x^\star)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i
abla g_i(x^\star)+A^{\mathsf T}
u=0,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(x^\star)=0\quad(1\le i\le m).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable convex program with affine equalities and a Slater point, a feasible point is globally optimal exactly when it admits nonnegative inequality multipliers and unrestricted equality multipliers satisfying stationarity and complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) for \(1\le i\le m\) are differentiable and convex.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and the equality constraints are \(Ax=b\).
There exists \(x^s\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(Ax^s=b\) and \(g_i(x^s)<0\) for every \(1\le i\le m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):g_i(x)\le0\ (1\le i\le m),\ Ax=b\}\iff x^\star\) admits KKT multipliers \((\lambda,\nu)\in\mathbb R_+^m\times\mathbb R^p\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of KKT Necessity Without Slater Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex example showing that an optimum need not admit a KKT multiplier when strict feasibility fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad x^2\le0.\] The unique feasible point \(x^\star=0\) is globally optimal, but no Slater point exists. KKT stationarity would require \(1+2\lambda x^\star=1=0\), which is impossible for every \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex optimum can fail to admit a KKT multiplier when Slater regularity is absent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star=0\text{ is globally optimal, but no KKT multiplier exists}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex KKT Sufficiency Without a Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficiency half of convex KKT optimality, separated from multiplier existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable convex objective, differentiable convex inequalities, and affine equalities, any feasible point \(x^\star\) admitting multipliers that satisfy stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementarity is a global minimizer. This implication requires no Slater point or other constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex program, every feasible KKT point is globally optimal; regularity is needed for guaranteed multiplier existence, not sufficiency.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are differentiable and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):g(x)\le0,\ Ax=b\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex KKT Sufficiency Without a Constraint Qualification

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X_0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex. Let \(f\) and \(g_i\) be differentiable convex functions and let \(h_j\) be affine. Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(x\in X_0\), \(g(x)\leq0\), and \(h(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable finite-dimensional convex programming. The definition incorporates the standard global-sufficiency interpretation of a feasible KKT point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A convex KKT optimality certificate is a feasible triple \((x,\lambda,\mu)\) with \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfying
\[
0\in\nabla f(x)+\sum_i\lambda_i\nabla g_i(x)+\sum_j\mu_j\nabla h_j(x)+N_{X_0}(x),
\qquad \lambda_i g_i(x)=0.
\]
The convex KKT optimality family is the class of convex programs for which such a certificate is sufficient for \(x\) to be a global minimizer. Under an appropriate qualification such as Slater’s condition, it is also necessary at a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a differentiable convex program, a convex KKT certificate consists of primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, complementarity, and normal-cone stationarity. Any feasible point possessing such multipliers is globally optimal. A constraint qualification is used for the converse assertion that an optimizer possesses multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{convex data and KKT}(x,\lambda,\mu)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in X}f(z).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Stationarity is equivalent to \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in X_0}L(z,\lambda,\mu)\) for the convex Lagrangian.
special_cases_latex: For affine constraints and \(X_0=\mathbb R^n\), this includes linear and convex quadratic programs.
For inequality-only convex programs, the equality multiplier block is absent.
immediate_consequences_latex: Convexity upgrades KKT stationarity from a local first-order certificate to a global optimality certificate.
boundary_notes: Without convexity, KKT points may be nonoptimal stationary points.
Slater qualification is relevant to necessity and multiplier existence, not to the sufficiency direction once a feasible KKT certificate is given.

This is only the sufficiency direction; obtaining KKT multipliers from optimality can require a constraint qualification.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At a feasible KKT pair \((x,\lambda)\) for inequalities written as \(c_i(x)\geq0\), let \(I(x)=\{i:c_i(x)=0\}\), with \(\lambda_i\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional KKT complementarity at a fixed primal–dual pair, using the nonnegative-slack convention \(c_i(x)\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Weak complementarity holds when
\[
\lambda_i c_i(x)=0\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
Strict complementarity holds when exactly one member of each nonnegative pair \((\lambda_i,c_i(x))\) is zero, equivalently
\[
\lambda_i+c_i(x)>0\quad\text{for every }i,
\]
or, equivalently, \(\lambda_i>0\) for every active inequality \(i\in I(x)\). Degenerate complementarity is the weak-complementarity regime in which some active index satisfies \(c_i(x)=\lambda_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak complementarity requires each multiplier–slack product to vanish. Strict complementarity strengthens this by forbidding both entries of a complementary pair from being zero: every active inequality has positive multiplier, and every inactive inequality has positive slack and zero multiplier. If an active inequality also has zero multiplier, complementarity is degenerate at that index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{strict complementarity}\iff\forall i,\ \lambda_i c_i(x)=0\ \text{and}\ \lambda_i+c_i(x)>0\iff\forall i\in I(x),\ \lambda_i>0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under \(g_i(x)\leq0\), replace the slack by \(-g_i(x)\geq0\); strict complementarity becomes \(\lambda_i-g_i(x)>0\) together with \(\lambda_i g_i(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For a single inequality, strict complementarity means either the constraint is inactive with positive slack or it is active with a positive multiplier.
immediate_consequences_latex: Strict complementarity partitions indices unambiguously into positive-multiplier active indices and positive-slack inactive indices.
boundary_notes: Strict complementarity does not imply LICQ or multiplier uniqueness.
Weak complementarity permits both multiplier and slack to vanish.

notation.meaning: nonnegative primal slack for inequality i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KT Points, Complementarity, and Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the source convention that inequality slacks and multipliers are nonnegative; it also records the source's sufficient active-gradient independence condition for its cited regularity assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible point x^* admitting multipliers \lambda^* that satisfy the Kuhn--Tucker conditions is called a KT point. For each inequality i\in I, complementarity is \lambda_i^*c_i(x^*)=0; thus c_i(x^*)>0 implies \lambda_i^*=0. Strict complementarity holds when there is no i\in I for which \lambda_i^*=c_i(x^*)=0, equivalently, every active inequality has \lambda_i^*>0. In addition, linear independence of \{a_i^*:i\in\mathcal A^*\} implies the cited regularity assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point that admits multipliers satisfying the KT system is a KT point. Complementarity requires each inequality's multiplier or slack to be zero, so inactive inequalities have zero multipliers. Strict complementarity means every active inequality has a positive multiplier. Independence of the active constraint gradients implies the cited regularity assumption.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal A^*\text{ is the active-constraint index set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_i^*c_i(x^*)=0\ (i\in I),\qquad \text{strict complementarity}\iff \nexists i\in I:\lambda_i^*=c_i(x^*)=0,\qquad \{a_i^*:i\in\mathcal A^*\}\text{ linearly independent}\implies\text{the cited regularity assumption}.

children.title: Strict Complementarity Regime
children.top_down_role: KKT regimes with strictly positive multipliers on active inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Complementarity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict complementarity for inequalities written as \(g_i(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\bar x,\lambda)\) satisfy primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness for inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\). Strict complementarity holds when every active constraint has a positive multiplier: \[g_i(\bar x)=0\ \Longrightarrow\ \lambda_i>0.\] Because complementarity forces \(\lambda_i=0\) whenever \(g_i(\bar x)<0\), this is equivalently \[\lambda_i-g_i(\bar x)>0\quad\text{for every }i.\] Thus each inequality index belongs to exactly one of two regimes: active with positive multiplier, or inactive with zero multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity means each active inequality has a positive multiplier; every inactive inequality has zero multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(g(\bar x)\le0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_i(\bar x)=0\Rightarrow\lambda_i>0\), equivalently \(\lambda_i-g_i(\bar x)>0\) for all \(i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform separation implied by strict complementarity for finitely many inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finitely many complementary pairs, define \[\delta=\min_{1\le i\le m}\max\{-g_i(\bar x),\lambda_i\}.\] Then strict complementarity holds if and only if \(\delta>0\). In that case every inactive inequality has slack at least \(\delta\), and every active inequality has multiplier at least \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite inequality system, strict complementarity is equivalent to positive uniform separation from the scalar transition point.
assumptions_latex: \(g(\bar x)\le0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Strict complementarity}\iff\min_i\max\{-g_i(\bar x),\lambda_i\}>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Strict-Complementarity Margin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition relative to a local solution and a KKT multiplier vector, using inequalities of the form c_i(x)\ge 0.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*\) be a local solution and let \(\lambda^*\) satisfy the KKT conditions at \(x^*\). Strict complementarity holds if, for every \(i\in\mathcal I\), exactly one of \(\lambda_i^*\) and \(c_i(x^*)\) is zero. Equivalently,
\[
\lambda_i^*>0\qquad\text{for every }i\in\mathcal I\cap\mathcal A(x^*).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity means that every active inequality has a strictly positive multiplier. Under the KKT conditions, inactive inequalities have zero multipliers, so exactly one of each inequality's multiplier and slack is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall i\in\mathcal I,\ \bigl[(\lambda_i^*=0)\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}(c_i(x^*)=0)\bigr]\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \lambda_i^*>0\ \forall i\in\mathcal I\cap\mathcal A(x^*)

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Complementarity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementarity allowing active inequalities with zero multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\bar x,\lambda)\) satisfy \(g(\bar x)\le0\) and \(\lambda\ge0\). Weak complementarity is the componentwise condition \[\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\quad\text{for every }i,\] without requiring positive multipliers on active constraints. Hence the degenerate index set \[D(\bar x,\lambda)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0,\ \lambda_i=0\}\] may be nonempty. Strict complementarity is precisely the special weak-complementarity regime in which \(D(\bar x,\lambda)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak complementarity permits an active constraint to have zero multiplier, unlike strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\) for every \(i\), while possibly \(D(\bar x,\lambda)\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-relative partition of a complementary inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[I^-(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)<0\},\quad I^+(\bar x,\lambda)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0,\lambda_i>0\},\quad I^0(\bar x,\lambda)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0,\lambda_i=0\}.\] Under complementarity these sets are pairwise disjoint and partition \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\); moreover \(\lambda_i=0\) on \(I^-\), and weak activity occurs exactly on \(I^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity partitions indices into inactive, positive-multiplier active, and zero-multiplier active classes.
assumptions_latex: \(g(\bar x)\le0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{1,\ldots,m\}=I^-(\bar x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}I^+(\bar x,\lambda)\mathbin{\dot\cup}I^0(\bar x,\lambda).

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Transition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating the two branches of each scalar complementarity pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce the primal slack \(s_i=-g_i(x)\). The scalar complementarity set is \[\mathcal C_i=\{(s_i,\lambda_i)\in\mathbb R_+^2:s_i\lambda_i=0\}.\] Its two relatively open branches, \(s_i>0,\lambda_i=0\) and \(s_i=0,\lambda_i>0\), represent inactive and strictly complementary active constraints. Their common transition boundary is \((s_i,\lambda_i)=(0,0)\), equivalently \(g_i(x)=0\) and \(\lambda_i=0\). At this boundary strict complementarity fails, and arbitrarily small perturbations may switch the identified activity branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complementarity branches meet where a constraint is active and its multiplier is zero; strict complementarity fails there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_{\mathrm{transition}}\mathcal C_i=\{(0,0)\}\), corresponding to \(g_i(x)=0\) and \(\lambda_i=0\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative primal slack of the ith inequality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Geometry at the Complementarity Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bouligand tangent geometry of one scalar complementarity pair at its branch intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal C=\{(s,\lambda)\in\mathbb R_+^2:s\lambda=0\}\), \[T_{\mathcal C}(0,0)=(\mathbb R_+\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb R_+).\] Thus the tangent cone is nonconvex: a complementary first-order perturbation may enter either coordinate branch but cannot have both components positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the zero-slack, zero-multiplier transition, the tangent cone is the union of the two nonnegative coordinate rays.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathcal C}(0,0)=(\mathbb R_+\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb R_+).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth mixed nonlinear program over a closed convex set \(X_0\), let \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Tg(x)+\mu^Th(x)\), with \(g(x)\leq0\), \(h(x)=0\), and \(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth KKT systems represented as a coupled normal-cone stationarity inclusion and a componentwise complementarity relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The complementarity–stationarity representation at \((x,\lambda,\mu)\) is
\[
-\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)\in N_{X_0}(x),
\]
together with
\[
g(x)\leq0,\quad\lambda\geq0,\quad\lambda\odot g(x)=0,\quad h(x)=0.
\]
Equivalently, using the slack \(s=-g(x)\), the complementarity block is \(0\leq\lambda\perp s\geq0\), while the stationarity block remains the normal-cone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The representation couples two components. Stationarity says that the negative Lagrangian gradient lies in the normal cone of the set constraint. Complementarity says that the nonnegative inequality multiplier is orthogonal componentwise to the nonnegative primal slack, along with primal feasibility. Equality feasibility is imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[-\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)\in N_{X_0}(x),\qquad0\leq\lambda\perp-g(x)\geq0,\qquad h(x)=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The stationarity inclusion is equivalent to \(0\in\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)+N_{X_0}(x)\).
If \(X_0=\mathbb R^n\), then \(N_{X_0}(x)=\{0\}\) and stationarity becomes an equation.
special_cases_latex: With no equality constraints, the \(\mu\) and \(h\) blocks disappear.
For scalar inequalities, \(0\leq\lambda\perp-g(x)\geq0\) means \(\lambda_i\geq0\), \(g_i(x)\leq0\), and \(\lambda_i g_i(x)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The representation isolates geometric stationarity from the algebraic complementarity block.
boundary_notes: The normal cone is the convex normal cone because \(X_0\) is assumed closed and convex.
This is an exact KKT representation, not a relaxed residual condition.

notation.meaning: componentwise nonnegative vectors with zero inner product, equivalently zero componentwise products
normal cone to the set constraint

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inequality \(g_i(x)\le0\), set \(s_i=-g_i(x)\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative primal and dual variables are complementary exactly when their minimum, or their Fischer–Burmeister residual, vanishes componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le s_i\perp\lambda_i\ge0\iff\min\{s_i,\lambda_i\}=0\iff\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(s_i,\lambda_i)=0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(s\in\mathbb R^m\) be the nonnegative primal slack associated with inequality feasibility and let \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) be the corresponding nonnegative dual multiplier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional componentwise complementarity for primal slacks and dual multipliers, independent of a particular algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A primal–dual pair \((s,\lambda)\) is complementary when
\[
s\geq0,\qquad\lambda\geq0,\qquad s_i\lambda_i=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
0\leq s\perp\lambda\geq0,\qquad S\lambda=0,\qquad\text{or}\qquad s^T\lambda=0,
\]
where \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\); the last equivalence uses nonnegativity. For inequalities \(g(x)\leq0\), the primal slack is \(s=-g(x)\), so complementarity is \(0\leq-g(x)\perp\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal–dual complementarity pairs each nonnegative primal slack \(s_i\) with a nonnegative dual multiplier \(\lambda_i\) and requires their product to vanish. Because all terms are nonnegative, componentwise zero products, the diagonal equation \(S\lambda=0\), and the scalar orthogonality equation \(s^T\lambda=0\) are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\leq s\perp\lambda\geq0\iff s\geq0,\ \lambda\geq0,\ S\lambda=0\iff s\geq0,\ \lambda\geq0,\ s^T\lambda=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For constraints written \(c(x)\geq0\), take \(s=c(x)\); for constraints written \(g(x)\leq0\), take \(s=-g(x)\).
special_cases_latex: For one pair, the complementarity set is \((\mathbb R_+\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb R_+)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive primal slack forces zero dual multiplier, and positive dual multiplier forces an active primal constraint.
boundary_notes: The equation \(s^T\lambda=0\) is equivalent to componentwise complementarity only when both vectors are componentwise nonnegative.
Perturbed relations such as \(S\lambda=\tau e\) with \(\tau>0\) are central-path conditions, not exact complementarity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality Conditions for the Weighted L1 Linear Penalty Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient primal-dual conditions for the convex, bound-constrained piecewise-linear problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r=A^Tx-b\), with \(\rho\leq\sigma\), and let \(x\) satisfy \(l\leq x\leq u\). Then \(x\) solves the weighted \(L_1\) linear penalty problem if and only if there exist \(\pi\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[
c=A\lambda+\pi,\qquad \rho\leq\lambda\leq\sigma,
\]
\[
\pi_i>0\Rightarrow x_i=l_i,\qquad \pi_i<0\Rightarrow x_i=u_i,
\]
and
\[
r_j>0\Rightarrow\lambda_j=\rho_j,\qquad r_j<0\Rightarrow\lambda_j=\sigma_j.
\]
The conditions are sufficient as well as necessary because the objective and bound-feasible set are convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-feasible point is optimal exactly when stationarity holds with a signed bound-normal vector, each residual multiplier lies between its two penalty weights, and the signs of the bound normals and residuals impose the stated endpoint complementarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists\pi\in\mathbb R^n,\lambda\in\mathbb R^m:\ c=A\lambda+\pi,\ \rho\leq\lambda\leq\sigma,\ \pi_i>0\Rightarrow x_i=l_i,\ \pi_i<0\Rightarrow x_i=u_i,\ r_j>0\Rightarrow\lambda_j=\rho_j,\ r_j<0\Rightarrow\lambda_j=\sigma_j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality representation using unrestricted squared slacks and its KKT limitation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each scalar inequality \(g_i(x)\le0\), \[g_i(x)\le0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y_i\in\mathbb R:\ g_i(x)+y_i^2=0.\] The representation is sign-redundant because \(y_i\) and \(-y_i\) yield the same slack. In the equality formulation, stationarity in \(y_i\) requires \(2y_i\lambda_i=0\). At an active inequality, \(y_i=0\), this condition imposes no sign restriction on \(\lambda_i\). Thus the squared-slack equality system is not equivalent to the inequality KKT system unless dual feasibility \(\lambda_i\ge0\) is imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality can be represented by an unrestricted squared slack, but this introduces sign redundancy and does not enforce nonnegative KKT multipliers at an active constraint.
assumptions_latex: Equality multipliers use the same Lagrangian sign convention as \(g_i(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_i(x)\le0\iff\exists y_i:g_i(x)+y_i^2=0\), but \(2y_i\lambda_i=0\) does not imply \(\lambda_i\ge0\) when \(y_i=0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\). Consider the componentwise inequality system \(g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact reformulations of scalar inequalities using either nonnegative linear slacks or unrestricted squared slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The nonnegative slack representation introduces \(s\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and replaces
\[
g(x)\leq0
\]
by the equality system
\[
g(x)+s=0,\qquad s\geq0.
\]
Equivalently, a squared-slack representation introduces \(z\in\mathbb R^m\) and uses
\[
g_i(x)+z_i^2=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
For every feasible \(x\), the linear slack is uniquely \(s=-g(x)\); squared slacks exist with \(z_i=\pm\sqrt{-g_i(x)}\), and conversely either equality representation implies \(g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality \(g(x)\leq0\) can be represented exactly by adding a nonnegative slack \(s\) and imposing \(g(x)+s=0\). The slack is then uniquely \(s=-g(x)\). Alternatively, one may use unrestricted squared slacks and impose \(g_i(x)+z_i^2=0\). Squared slacks are generally nonunique in sign but project onto the same feasible \(x\)-set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[g(x)\leq0\iff\exists s\geq0:\ g(x)+s=0\iff\exists z\in\mathbb R^m:\ g_i(x)+z_i^2=0\ \forall i.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the nonnegative-slack form, \(s=-g(x)\) is forced by the equality.
For the squared form, \(|z_i|=\sqrt{-g_i(x)}\).
special_cases_latex: An active inequality has \(s_i=0\); an inactive inequality has \(s_i>0\).
For bounds \(x_i\geq\ell_i\), the slack equation is \(x_i-\ell_i-s_i=0\) with \(s_i\geq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: KKT complementarity \(\lambda_i g_i(x)=0\) becomes \(\lambda_i s_i=0\) in the nonnegative-slack representation.
boundary_notes: The squared-slack formulation changes derivative structure at \(z_i=0\) and should not be treated as regularity-neutral.
Linear nonnegative slacks add inequality bounds on \(s\); squared slacks replace those bounds by nonlinear equalities.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\bar x\in\Omega\), and let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable at \(\bar x\). The contingent tangent cone is \(T_\Omega(\bar x)\), and its polar normal cone is \(N_\Omega(\bar x):=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\langle v,d\rangle\leq0\ \forall d\in T_\Omega(\bar x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth optimization over a possibly nonconvex feasible set, using the contingent tangent cone and its polar normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The point \(\bar x\) is normal-cone stationary for \(\min\{f(x):x\in\Omega\}\) if and only if
\[
0\in \nabla f(\bar x)+N_\Omega(\bar x),
\]
equivalently, \(-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_\Omega(\bar x)\), or
\[
\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\geq0\qquad\forall d\in T_\Omega(\bar x).
\]
For \(\Omega=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\), if LICQ holds at \(\bar x\), this inclusion is equivalent to the existence of \((\bar\nu,\bar\lambda)\) such that
\[
\nabla f(\bar x)+\nabla h(\bar x)^T\bar\nu+\nabla g(\bar x)^T\bar\lambda=0,
\quad \bar\lambda\geq0,
\quad \bar\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point \(\bar x\) is normal-cone stationary when the negative objective gradient belongs to the normal cone of the feasible set at \(\bar x\). Equivalently, the objective has nonnegative directional derivative along every tangent direction. For a smooth equality-and-inequality description satisfying LICQ, the same condition has the usual KKT multiplier representation with stationarity, nonnegative inequality multipliers, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\nabla f(\bar x)+N_\Omega(\bar x)\), equivalently \(\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_\Omega(\bar x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_\Omega(\bar x)\).
\(\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\geq0\quad\forall d\in T_\Omega(\bar x)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}\Omega\), then \(N_\Omega(\bar x)=\{0\}\), so stationarity reduces to \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every differentiable local minimizer over \(\Omega\) is normal-cone stationary.
Under LICQ, the geometric inclusion admits the displayed KKT multiplier representation.
boundary_notes: For nonconvex sets, this record uses the polar of the contingent tangent cone; other variational normal cones need not coincide without regularity.
Normal-cone stationarity is generally necessary, not sufficient, for local minimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Smallness Does Not Imply a Distance Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between approximate stationarity certification and quantitative proximity to the stationary set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Small stationarity residuals need not provide a Lipschitz bound on distance to the stationary set. For \(f(x)=x^4\), let \(S=\{0\}\) and \(r(x)=|f'(x)|=4|x|^3\). Then \[\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)}{r(x)}=\frac{1}{4|x|^2}\to\infty\quad\text{as }x\to0,\ x\ne0.\] Consequently, no \(C,\delta>0\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le Cr(x)\) for every \(|x|<\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small stationarity residual certifies approximate equation satisfaction but need not bound distance to a solution without additional error-bound regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists C,\delta>0:\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le Cr(x)\ \text{for every }|x|<\delta\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a candidate triple \((x,\lambda,
u)\), define \[r_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x,\lambda,
u)=\left\|\left(
abla f(x)+Dg(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda+Dh(x)^{\mathsf T}
u,\ h(x),\ [g(x)]_+,\ [-\lambda]_+,\ \lambda\odot g(x)ight)ight\|_\infty.\] Here positive parts are componentwise. The displayed triple is an exact KKT certificate precisely when \(r_{\mathrm{KKT}}=0\). Given \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the verifiable inequality \(r_{\mathrm{KKT}}\le\varepsilon\) certifies simultaneous \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity, equality feasibility, inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity in the stated norm and scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single computable residual certifies exact KKT satisfaction at zero and componentwise approximate satisfaction below a chosen tolerance.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x,\lambda,\nu)=0\iff(x,\lambda,\nu)\ \text{satisfies the mixed KKT system}\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), with continuously differentiable \(f,h,g\). Let \(L(x,\lambda,\nu)=f(x)+\lambda^Tg(x)+\nu^Th(x)\), and write \([z]_+\) for the componentwise positive part.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming; the certificate measures primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementarity, and Lagrangian stationarity simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a primal-dual triple \(z=(x,\lambda,\nu)\), define the KKT residual
\[
R_{\mathrm{KKT}}(z):=
\begin{pmatrix}
\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\nu)\\
h(x)\\
[g(x)]_+\\
[-\lambda]_+\\
\lambda\odot g(x)
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\eta_{\mathrm{KKT}}(z):=\|R_{\mathrm{KKT}}(z)\|.
\]
The triple \(z\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity certificate if \(\eta_{\mathrm{KKT}}(z)\leq\varepsilon\). It is exact if \(\eta_{\mathrm{KKT}}(z)=0\). For any norm, exactness is equivalent to
\[
\nabla_xL=0,\quad h=0,\quad g\leq0,\quad\lambda\geq0,
\quad\lambda_i g_i=0\ \forall i,
\]
namely the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate is the norm of a vector collecting the Lagrangian-gradient residual, equality violation, positive inequality violation, negative-multiplier violation, and complementarity products. A triple is an \(\varepsilon\)-certificate when this norm is at most \(\varepsilon\). A zero residual is equivalent to satisfaction of every KKT condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x,\lambda,\nu)=0\) if and only if \((x,\lambda,\nu)\) satisfies the KKT equations and inequalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Any replacement of the displayed norm by another norm on the same finite-dimensional residual space has the same exact zero set.

The maximum-component certificate \(\max\{\|\nabla_xL\|,\|h\|,\|[g]_+\|,\|[-\lambda]_+\|,\|\lambda\odot g\|\}\leq\varepsilon\) is an equivalent finite-dimensional residual convention up to norm constants.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(R_{\mathrm{KKT}}=(\nabla_xL,h)\).
For unconstrained optimization, \(\eta_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A sequence with \(\eta_{\mathrm{KKT}}(z_k)\to0\) has asymptotically vanishing KKT violations componentwise.
The residual separates failure of stationarity from failure of primal feasibility, dual feasibility, or complementarity.
boundary_notes: The numerical value of an inexact certificate depends on norm and scaling, although its exact zero set does not.
A small residual alone does not imply proximity to a solution without an error bound or regularity condition.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be feasible for a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, let \(\bar y\) be a KKT multiplier, let \(C(\bar x,\bar y)\) be its critical cone, and set \(H(\bar x,\bar y)=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming at a KKT point; this definition organizes necessary curvature, sufficient curvature, and local growth predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The second-order optimality-growth system at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) consists of the predicates
\[
\mathrm{SONC}:\quad d^TH(\bar x,\bar y)d\geq0
\quad\forall d\in C(\bar x,\bar y),
\]
\[
\mathrm{SOSC}:\quad d^TH(\bar x,\bar y)d>0
\quad\forall d\in C(\bar x,\bar y)\setminus\{0\},
\]
and quadratic growth at \(\bar x\): there exist \(\alpha>0\) and \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+\alpha\|x-\bar x\|^2
\quad\forall x\in\Omega\cap B_\delta(\bar x).
\]
Under the standard hypotheses attached to the respective conditions, local minimality implies SONC, while SOSC implies quadratic growth and hence strict local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order optimality-growth theory classifies a KKT point by the sign of the Lagrangian Hessian on critical directions and by the resulting local objective growth. SONC requires nonnegative critical curvature. SOSC requires strictly positive critical curvature. Quadratic growth means that every sufficiently close feasible point has objective value at least a positive quadratic above the reference value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical predicates are critical-cone nonnegative curvature, critical-cone positive curvature, and local quadratic growth, with the standard chain \(\mathrm{SOSC}\Rightarrow\) quadratic growth \(\Rightarrow\) strict local minimality.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because the unit section of a finite-dimensional closed critical cone is compact, SOSC is equivalent to the existence of \(\sigma>0\) such that \(d^THd\geq\sigma\|d\|^2\) for every \(d\in C(\bar x,\bar y)\).
special_cases_latex: For unconstrained optimization, \(C(\bar x)=\mathbb R^n\), so SONC and SOSC reduce to positive semidefiniteness and positive definiteness of \(\nabla^2f(\bar x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Quadratic growth makes \(\bar x\) an isolated local minimizer relative to the feasible set.
SOSC excludes nonzero critical directions of zero or negative Lagrangian curvature.
boundary_notes: The constraint qualification required for SONC can differ from the hypotheses sufficient for SOSC.
Strict local minimality by itself need not imply quadratic growth or a positive-definite Hessian.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar x\in X\), and \(d\in T_X(\bar x)\). A parabolic displacement has the form \(\bar x+t d+\tfrac12t^2w\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional second-order feasible geometry for an arbitrary set, with a smooth-constraint formula available under metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The second-order tangent set to \(X\) at \(\bar x\) in direction \(d\) is
\[
T_X^2(\bar x;d):=
\left\{w:\exists\,t_k\downarrow0,\ x_k\in X,
\ \frac{x_k-\bar x-t_kd}{\tfrac12t_k^2}\to w\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(w\in T_X^2(\bar x;d)\) when
\[
\operatorname{dist}\!\left(\bar x+t_kd+\tfrac12t_k^2w,X\right)=o(t_k^2)
\]
for some \(t_k\downarrow0\). If \(X=\{x:g(x)\leq0,\ h(x)=0\}\), the data are twice continuously differentiable, and the stated regularity condition holds, then
\[
\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Tw+d^T\nabla^2g_i(\bar x)d\leq0
\]
for active indices satisfying \(\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td=0\), and
\[
\nabla h_j(\bar x)^Tw+d^T\nabla^2h_j(\bar x)d=0
\]
for every equality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order tangent set contains the acceleration vectors of feasible arcs whose first-order velocity is \(d\). Membership is defined through feasible sequences approximating a parabolic trajectory to order smaller than \(t^2\). For smooth constraints under regularity, the set is described by linear conditions on the acceleration plus the directional curvature of each constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_X^2(\bar x;d)\) is the set of all second-order feasible corrections accompanying the first-order tangent direction \(d\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(w\in T_X^2(\bar x;d)\) iff the parabolic path \(\bar x+t_kd+\tfrac12t_k^2w\) has distance \(o(t_k^2)\) from \(X\) along some \(t_k\downarrow0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(X\) is a convex polyhedron, then \(T_X^2(\bar x;d)=T_{T_X(\bar x)}(d)\).
The set is empty when \(d\notin T_X(\bar x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The scaling relation \(T_X^2(\bar x;\alpha d)=\alpha^2T_X^2(\bar x;d)\) holds for every \(\alpha>0\).
Second-order feasible geometry records constraint curvature that is invisible in the first-order tangent cone.
boundary_notes: For a general nonpolyhedral set, the second-order tangent set need not be convex or a cone.
The smooth algebraic formula requires the cited regularity hypothesis; the sequential definition does not.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Tangent Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parabolic second-order tangent sets, indexed by first-order feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar x\in F\), and \(d\in T_F(\bar x)\). The second-order tangent set to \(F\) at \(\bar x\) in direction \(d\) is
\[T_F^2(\bar x;d):=\left\{w\in\mathbb R^n:\ \exists\,t_k\downarrow0,\ w_k\to w\text{ with }\bar x+t_kd+\tfrac12t_k^2w_k\in F\ \forall k\right\}.\]
The second-order tangent family at \(\bar x\) is \(\{T_F^2(\bar x;d):d\in T_F(\bar x)\}\). Thus each member records the feasible second-order corrections associated with one first-order tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each feasible first-order direction, the second-order tangent set contains all limiting quadratic corrections that preserve feasibility along a suitable vanishing step sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F^2(\bar x;d)\) is the family member of feasible second-order corrections associated with \(d\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaling, Closedness, and the Zero-Direction Member
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic structural laws of parabolic second-order tangent families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar x\in F\), and \(d\in T_F(\bar x)\), the set \(T_F^2(\bar x;d)\) is closed, although it may be empty or nonconvex. For every \(\alpha>0\), \[T_F^2(\bar x;\alpha d)=\alpha^2T_F^2(\bar x;d),\] and \[T_F^2(\bar x;0)=T_F(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order tangent sets are closed, scale quadratically with the first-order direction, and reduce to the ordinary tangent cone in the zero direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F^2(\bar x;d)\) is closed, \(T_F^2(\bar x;\alpha d)=\alpha^2T_F^2(\bar x;d)\), and \(T_F^2(\bar x;0)=T_F(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\). Let \(\bar x\) be feasible, \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\), and let \((\bar\lambda,\bar\nu)\) satisfy the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming at a KKT point; inequality constraints use the convention \(g_i\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The linearized tangent cone is
\[
T_{\mathrm{lin}}(\bar x)=\{d:\nabla h(\bar x)d=0,\ \nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td\leq0\ \forall i\in I(\bar x)\}.
\]
A vector \(d\) is critical if
\[
d\in T_{\mathrm{lin}}(\bar x),\qquad \nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0.
\]
The critical-direction cone is therefore
\[
C(\bar x)=T_{\mathrm{lin}}(\bar x)\cap\nabla f(\bar x)^\perp.
\]
At a KKT pair this equals the multiplier representation
\[
C(\bar x,\bar\lambda)=\{d:\nabla h(\bar x)d=0,
\ \nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td=0\ \text{if }\bar\lambda_i>0,
\ \nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td\leq0\ \text{if }i\in I(\bar x),\bar\lambda_i=0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A critical direction is a linearized feasible direction along which the objective has zero first-order change. The set of all such directions is the intersection of the linearized tangent cone with the hyperplane orthogonal to the objective gradient. At a KKT pair, complementarity and stationarity give the equivalent description that active constraints with positive multipliers must remain tangent, while active constraints with zero multipliers need only satisfy their one-sided linearization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(\bar x)=T_{\mathrm{lin}}(\bar x)\cap\nabla f(\bar x)^\perp=C(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) at a KKT pair.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(d\in C(\bar x)\) iff \(d\) is linearized feasible and \(\nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\).

At a KKT pair, \(d\in C(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) iff every positive-multiplier active constraint has zero directional derivative and every zero-multiplier active inequality has nonpositive directional derivative.
special_cases_latex: Under strict complementarity, \(C(\bar x,\bar\lambda)=\ker[\nabla h(\bar x);\nabla g_{I(\bar x)}(\bar x)^T]\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Second-order conditions need be tested only on critical directions because other linearized feasible directions already have strictly positive first-order objective change.
The critical cone is a closed polyhedral cone when defined by finitely many smooth constraint gradients at a fixed point.
boundary_notes: Replacing the linearized cone by the actual tangent cone requires an appropriate constraint qualification.
The sign of inequality derivatives reverses under the alternative convention \(g_i\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized critical cones for smooth nonlinear programs, partitioned by first-order active-index patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) over \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m;\ h_j(x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,p\}\), and let \(\bar x\in F\) and \(I(\bar x):=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). Define the linearized cone
\[L_F(\bar x):=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td\leq0\ \text{for all }i\in I(\bar x),\ \nabla h_j(\bar x)^Td=0\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,p\}.\]
The critical cone is
\[C(\bar x):=\{d\in L_F(\bar x):\nabla f(\bar x)^Td\leq0\}.\]
If a KKT multiplier exists at \(\bar x\), stationarity implies
\[C(\bar x)=\{d\in L_F(\bar x):\nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\}.\]
For \(J\subseteq I(\bar x)\), define
\[C_J(\bar x):=\{d\in C(\bar x):\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td=0\iff i\in J\}.\]
The nonempty sets among \(\{C_J(\bar x):J\subseteq I(\bar x)\}\) partition \(C(\bar x)\) by first-order active-index pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The critical cone consists of linearized feasible directions that do not increase the objective to first order. At a KKT point their objective derivative is zero, and the cone can be partitioned according to which active inequalities have zero directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are differentiable at the feasible point \(\bar x\).
For the equality characterization, a KKT multiplier exists at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At a KKT point, \(C(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x)\cap\{d:\nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\}\), and the nonempty sets \(C_J(\bar x)\) partition \(C(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: indices of inequalities active at the reference point
critical-cone vectors having first-order active-index pattern J

abla h_j( ar x)^Td=0\  orall j,\ 
abla g_i( ar x)^Td=0\  orall i\in I^+( ar\lambda),\ 
abla g_i( ar x)^Td\leq0\  orall i\in I( ar x)\setminus I^+( ar\lambda)\}.\]

assumptions_latex: \((\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) satisfies KKT conditions under the convention \(g_i\leq0\), \(\bar\lambda_i\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical cone of a smooth nonlinear program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition by tangent-cone intersection and explicit linearized and multiplier-based representations under a suitable constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible stationary point \( ar x\), define \(\mathcal C( ar x;\mathcal F^{\mathrm{NLP}}):=\mathcal T( ar x;\mathcal F^{\mathrm{NLP}})\cap
abla f( ar x)^\perp\). Under a constraint qualification yielding the linearized tangent-cone representation, such as MFCQ, \(\mathcal C\) consists of the vectors \(d\) satisfying \(
abla f( ar x)^Td=0\), \(
abla g_i( ar x)^Td=0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,\ell\), and \(
abla g_i( ar x)^Td\le0\) for active inequalities. For any \(\pi\in M( ar x)\), if \(\mathcal A_+( ar x,\pi):=\{1,\ldots,\ell\}\cup\{i>\ell:\pi_i>0\}\), the same cone is \(\{d:
abla g_i( ar x)^Td=0\  orall i\in\mathcal A_+( ar x,\pi),\ 
abla g_i( ar x)^Td\le0\  orall i\in\mathcal A( ar x)\setminus\mathcal A_+( ar x,\pi)\}\).

Under an appropriate constraint qualification, it has a linearized description; equivalently, for any KKT multiplier, positive-multiplier active constraints impose equality and the remaining active inequalities impose nonpositivity.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\in\mathcal F^{\mathrm{NLP}}\text{ is stationary and satisfies the KKT conditions}
\text{A constraint qualification yielding the linearized tangent-cone representation, such as MFCQ, holds for the explicit formulas}
\pi\in M(\bar x)\text{ for the multiplier-based representation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\mathcal C( ar x;\mathcal F^{\mathrm{NLP}})=\mathcal T( ar x;\mathcal F^{\mathrm{NLP}})\cap
abla f( ar x)^\perp=\{d:
abla g_i( ar x)^Td=0\ (i\in\mathcal A_+( ar x,\pi)),\ 
abla g_i( ar x)^Td\le0\ (i\in\mathcal A( ar x)\setminus\mathcal A_+( ar x,\pi))\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical Direction–Cone Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality between geometric critical directions and the linearized critical cone under Abadie regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar x\) be feasible and suppose Abadie's constraint qualification holds, namely \(T_F(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x)\). Then the set of critical feasible directions, including the zero direction, satisfies
\[\{d\in T_F(\bar x):\nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\}=L_F(\bar x)\cap\nabla f(\bar x)^\perp.\]
If KKT stationarity holds, the right-hand side is exactly the critical cone \(C(\bar x)\). Consequently, nonzero critical directions are precisely the nonzero elements of \(C(\bar x)\); without tangent-linearization equality, the linearized cone can contain spurious critical vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Abadie regularity and KKT stationarity, geometric critical directions are exactly the nonzero vectors of the linearized critical cone.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are differentiable at the feasible point \(\bar x\).
KKT stationarity holds for the final identification with \(C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{d\neq0:d\in T_F(\bar x),\ \nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\}=C(\bar x)\setminus\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: vectors orthogonal to the objective gradient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spurious Linearized Critical Directions Without Abadie Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of the geometric direction–cone correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2\leq0\}=\{0\}\), \(\bar x=0\), and \(f\equiv0\). Then \(T_F(0)=\{0\}\), while the linearized cone is \(L_F(0)=\mathbb R\) because \(g'(0)=0\). Hence the geometric critical-direction set contains only zero, whereas the linearized critical cone is \(C(0)=\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate constraint can make every vector linearly critical even though the feasible set has no nonzero tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(0)\cap\nabla f(0)^\perp=\{0\}\subsetneq\mathbb R=C(0)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lifted critical cone and directional critical section
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-dependent critical geometry for a parameterized VI constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\lambda\in M(\bar z)\), define
\[\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda)=\left\{(d_x,d_y)\in\mathbb R^{n+m}:\begin{array}{ll}d_x^T\nabla_xg_i(\bar z)+d_y^T\nabla_yg_i(\bar z)\le 0,&i\in\mathcal I(\bar z),\ \lambda_i=0,\\d_x^T\nabla_xg_i(\bar z)+d_y^T\nabla_yg_i(\bar z)=0,&\lambda_i>0\end{array}\right\}.\]
For \(d_x\in\mathbb R^n\), define
\[\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda;d_x)=\{d_y\in\mathbb R^m:(d_x,d_y)\in\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda)\}.\]
The first set is a polyhedral cone, and each directional section is a possibly empty polyhedral set. If \(\nabla_xg_i(\bar z)=0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal I(\bar z)\), then
\[\operatorname{proj}_{d_y}\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda)=\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda;0)=T_{\mathrm{lin}}(\bar y;C(\bar x))\cap F(\bar x,\bar y)^\perp.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lifted critical cone imposes equality for positive-multiplier constraints and inequality for active zero-multiplier constraints. Fixing the parameter direction gives a possibly empty polyhedral section. If all active constraint gradients have zero parameter component, the projection and zero-direction section coincide with the usual VI critical cone.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I(\bar z)\text{ is the active index set}\)
\(\nabla_xg_i(\bar z)=0\text{ for every }i\in\mathcal I(\bar z)\text{ for the projection identity}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda)\text{ is a polyhedral cone and }\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda;d_x)\text{ is a possibly empty polyhedral set; under the stated zero-parameter-gradient condition, its projection is the VI critical cone}
