knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a parameterized NLP, let \(K(p)\) be the set of KKT triples \(z=(x,\lambda,\mu)\), and fix \((\bar p,\bar z)\) with \(\bar z\in K(\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-dimensional stability of a selected KKT solution, not global uniqueness of all optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reference KKT point \(\bar z\) is locally primal-dual stable if there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\) and \(V\) of \(\bar z\) such that the localized mapping \[K_V(p):=K(p)\cap V\] is nonempty for every \(p\in U\), remains close to \(\bar z\), and obeys a declared continuity modulus. It is locally single-valued Lipschitz stable if \(K_V(p)=\{z(p)\}\) and \[\|z(p_1)-z(p_2)\|\le L\|p_1-p_2\|\qquad\forall p_1,p_2\in U.\] It is differentiably stable when this selection is differentiable at \(\bar p\). The definition jointly controls primal variables and multipliers; stability of \(x(p)\) alone is only primal stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-dual stability means that nearby parameter values possess nearby KKT points and that the localized KKT mapping has a specified continuity property. The strongest classical smooth regime used here is a unique locally Lipschitz or differentiable branch of both primal variables and multipliers.
assumptions_latex: Localization is performed in a fixed neighborhood \(V\) of the reference primal-dual point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K(p)\cap V=\{z(p)\},\qquad \|z(p_1)-z(p_2)\|\le L\|p_1-p_2\|\] defines local single-valued Lipschitz primal-dual stability.
special_cases_latex: For smooth right-hand-side perturbations under active-gradient independence, strict complementarity, and second-order sufficiency, the branch is differentiable.
If only \(x(p)\) is unique while multipliers are multiple, primal-dual single-valued stability fails.
immediate_consequences_latex: Local Lipschitz stability implies continuity of the selected primal and multiplier components.
Differentiability supplies first-order expansions for both components.
boundary_notes: The definition is local and does not preclude remote KKT points.
Existence stability, set-valued Lipschitz stability, and single-valued Lipschitz stability are distinct.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Isolated Calmness Without a Single-Valued Localization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A multifunction with two nearby perturbed solutions but one isolated reference solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) by \(S(0)=\{0\}\) and \(S(p)=\{-p,p\}\) for \(p\ne0\). Its graph is closed, and every \(x\in S(p)\) satisfies \(|x|\le|p|\). Hence \(S\) is isolated calm at \((0,0)\) with modulus one, although every sufficiently small nonzero \(p\) has two localized solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Isolated calmness permits multiple perturbed branches: x=±p obey the same linear bound and meet at one isolated reference solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is isolated calm at }(0,0),\qquad |S(p)|=2\text{ for }p\ne0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Isolated Calmness of a Localized Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical graph-point definition of isolated solution stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) is isolated calm at \((\bar p,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\) if neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\) and \(V\) of \(\bar x\), and \(\kappa\ge0\), exist such that \[S(\bar p)\cap V=\{\bar x\},\qquad S(p)\cap V\subseteq \bar x+\kappa\|p-\bar p\|\mathbb B\quad(p\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reference solution is locally isolated at the reference parameter, and every localized perturbed solution remains linearly close to it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is isolated calm at }(\bar p,\bar x)\text{ exactly when the displayed localization and linear bound hold}.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Calmness of a Localized Solution
Isolated-Solution Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isolated calmness of a parameterized local solution mapping in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S:P\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) be a solution mapping and let \(\bar x\in S(\bar p)\). The solution \(\bar x\) is isolatedly stable, or equivalently \(S\) is isolated calm at \((\bar p,\bar x)\), if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\) and \(V\) of \(\bar x\), and a constant \(\kappa\ge0\), such that \(S(\bar p)\cap V=\{\bar x\}\) and
\[S(p)\cap V\subseteq \bar x+\kappa\lVert p-\bar p\rVert\mathbb B\qquad\text{for every }p\in U.\]
This condition permits multiple nearby solutions for perturbed parameters but bounds every localized branch linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reference solution is isolatedly stable when it is locally unique at the reference parameter and every nearby localized solution remains within a linear perturbation bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(\bar p)\cap V=\{\bar x\}\) and \(S(p)\cap V\subseteq\bar x+\kappa\lVert p-\bar p\rVert\mathbb B\) locally.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse formulation of a unique Lipschitz localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set-valued mapping \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\) if neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\) exist such that \(y\mapsto F^{-1}(y)\cap U\) is single-valued on \(V\) and Lipschitz continuous.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,V:\;F^{-1}(y)\cap U=\{s(y)\}\text{ with }s\text{ Lipschitz on }V.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) have locally closed graph at \((\bar p,\bar x)\). Then \(S\) has the Aubin property at \((\bar p,\bar x)\) with modulus \(\kappa\) if and only if \(S^{-1}:X\rightrightarrows P\) is metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar p)\); equivalently, for all nearby \((p,x)\), \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S(p))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(p,S^{-1}(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution mapping is locally Lipschitz-like exactly when its inverse satisfies the corresponding local error bound.
assumptions_latex: S:P\rightrightarrows X\text{ acts between finite-dimensional normed spaces}.
\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed at }(\bar p,\bar x).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional infinitesimal test for a Lipschitz-like solution mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) have locally closed graph at \((\bar p,\bar x)\). Then \(S\) has the Aubin property at \((\bar p,\bar x)\) if and only if \[D^*S(\bar p\mid\bar x)(0)=\{0\}.\] Equivalently, \(S^{-1}\) is metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar p)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of calmness from isolated calmness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S(p)=[-1,1]\) for every \(p\in\mathbb R\). At \((0,0)\), \(S\) is calm with modulus zero because \(S(p)\cap V\subseteq S(0)\). It is not isolated calm there, since \(S(0)\cap V\) contains points other than zero for every neighborhood \(V\) of zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant non-singleton solution set is calm but not isolated calm at an interior reference solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is calm at }(0,0)\text{ but not isolated calm there}.
knowledge_statements.title: Calmness Need Not Imply Isolation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric Regularity Need Not Be Strong Metric Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation caused by a multivalued localized inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) by \(F(x)=\{x,-x\}\). Then \(F^{-1}(y)=\{y,-y\}\). The inverse has the Aubin property at \((0,0)\), so \(F\) is metrically regular there. However, \(F^{-1}(y)\) has two localized values for every sufficiently small nonzero \(y\); hence \(F\) is not strongly metrically regular at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two-branch map is metrically regular but lacks the unique inverse branch required for strong metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is metrically regular but not strongly metrically regular at }(0,0).
knowledge_statements.title: Metric Regularity Need Not Be Strong Metric Regularity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-reference inverse equivalence corresponding to calmness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). The mapping \(F\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if locally \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x)).\] This holds if and only if \(F^{-1}\) is calm at \((\bar y,\bar x)\), with the same local modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity is the fixed-reference error bound dual to calmness of the inverse mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is metrically subregular at }(\bar x,\bar y)\iff F^{-1}\text{ is calm at }(\bar y,\bar x).

notation.meaning: solution set of the reference inclusion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Calmness Need Not Imply the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single-valued continuous map with a linear reference bound but no locally uniform Lipschitz bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) by \(S(0)=\{0\}\) and \(S(p)=\{p\sin(1/p)\}\) for \(p\ne0\). Since \(|p\sin(1/p)|\le|p|\), \(S\) is calm at \((0,0)\) with modulus one. Its single-valued representative is differentiable for \(p\ne0\), with derivative \(\sin(1/p)-(1/p)\cos(1/p)\), which is unbounded arbitrarily close to zero. A Lipschitz function has derivative bounded by its Lipschitz constant wherever differentiable, so this localization is not Lipschitz on any neighborhood of zero and \(S\) lacks the Aubin property at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oscillatory map is linearly bounded relative to the reference parameter and hence calm, but it is not Lipschitz-like between arbitrary nearby parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is calm at }(0,0)\text{ but does not have the Aubin property there}.

knowledge_statements.title: Calmness Need Not Imply the Aubin Property

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct graph-point definitions of the Aubin property, calmness, and isolated calmness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) and \((\bar p,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\), the Aubin property requires neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(\kappa\ge0\) such that \[S(p_1)\cap V\subseteq S(p_2)+\kappa\|p_1-p_2\|\mathbb B\quad(p_1,p_2\in U).\] Calmness requires \[S(p)\cap V\subseteq S(\bar p)+\kappa\|p-\bar p\|\mathbb B\quad(p\in U).\] Isolated calmness additionally localizes \(S(\bar p)\) to \(\{\bar x\}\) and replaces the reference set on the right by \(\{\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aubin regularity compares arbitrary nearby parameters, calmness compares only with the reference parameter, and isolated calmness also isolates the reference solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Aubin, calmness, and isolated calmness are distinguished by the displayed two-point, reference-point, and isolated-reference bounds}.

Solution-Mapping Regularity Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Localized Lipschitz regularity notions for set-valued solution mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) and \((\bar p,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\), the Aubin property holds if neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(\kappa\ge0\) satisfy \(S(p_1)\cap V\subseteq S(p_2)+\kappa\lVert p_1-p_2\rVert\mathbb B\) for all \(p_1,p_2\in U\). A single-valued localization that is Lipschitz implies all three properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aubin regularity compares any two nearby parameter values; calmness compares with the reference value; isolated calmness also isolates the reference solution.
assumptions_latex: \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) is a set-valued mapping between finite-dimensional normed spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A locally Lipschitz single-valued localization of \(S\) has the Aubin, calmness, and isolated-calmness properties.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MFCQ Gives Local Boundedness of KKT Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer stability of multiplier sets along convergent parametric KKT points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-dimensional smooth parametric NLP, let \((p_k,x_k)\to(\bar p,\bar x)\) be KKT points with associated multipliers \((\lambda_k,\mu_k)\). If MFCQ holds at \((\bar p,\bar x)\), then nearby multiplier sets are locally bounded. Every cluster point of \((\lambda_k,\mu_k)\) is a KKT multiplier at \((\bar p,\bar x)\). Thus the multiplier mapping is locally bounded and outer semicontinuous there, although it need not be single-valued or Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ prevents nearby KKT multipliers from diverging and makes their cluster points valid reference multipliers, without ensuring uniqueness or Lipschitz dependence.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint gradients are continuous in \((p,x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \limsup_{(p,x)\to(\bar p,\bar x)}M(p,x)\subseteq M(\bar p,\bar x),\quad M\text{ is locally bounded}.

knowledge_statements.title: MFCQ Gives Local Boundedness of KKT Multipliers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary of local multiplier boundedness under MFCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}-x\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_1(x)=x\le0,\qquad g_2(x)=2x\le0.\] At \(\bar x=0\), MFCQ holds because \(d=-1\) strictly decreases both active constraints. The KKT multiplier set is \[M(\bar x)=\{(\mu_1,\mu_2)\in\mathbb R_+^2:\mu_1+2\mu_2=1\},\] a nontrivial compact line segment. Thus MFCQ ensures boundedness here but not multiplier uniqueness or a single-valued localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant active inequalities can satisfy MFCQ while producing a bounded continuum of KKT multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The inequality convention is g_i(x)\le0 with multipliers \mu_i\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MFCQ}(\bar x)\text{ holds},\qquad M(\bar x)\text{ is bounded and non-singleton}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LICQ Gives a Unique Multiplier at a Fixed KKT Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise multiplier uniqueness from independence of equality and active-inequality gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a smooth NLP at a KKT point \(x\), suppose the equality gradients together with the active-inequality gradients are linearly independent. Then the stationarity equation has at most one multiplier vector supported on the active inequalities. Consequently, whenever a KKT multiplier exists, the multiplier set \(M(x)\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ makes the KKT multiplier unique at a fixed primal KKT point but does not alone establish Lipschitz dependence under perturbations.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint gradients exist at \(x\).
LICQ holds for the equality and active-inequality gradients at \(x\).
At least one KKT multiplier exists at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LICQ}(x)\Rightarrow |M(x)|=1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pair-Indexed KKT Multiplier Mapping and Calmness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier multifunction indexed consistently by the parameter and primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a smooth parametric NLP, let \[M(p,x):=\{(\lambda,\mu):x\text{ is primal feasible and }(x,\lambda,\mu)\text{ satisfies KKT stationarity, multiplier signs, and complementarity at }p\}.\] At \(((\bar p,\bar x),\bar m)\in\operatorname{gph}M\), the mapping is calm if neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(\kappa\ge0\) exist such that \[M(p,x)\cap V\subseteq M(\bar p,\bar x)+\kappa\|(p,x)-(\bar p,\bar x)\|\mathbb B\quad((p,x)\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mapping assigns all KKT multipliers to each feasible primal-parameter pair; calmness gives a one-sided local linear bound relative to the reference multiplier set.
assumptions_latex: The derivatives defining the KKT system exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is calm at }((\bar p,\bar x),\bar m)\text{ exactly when the displayed localized bound holds}.

knowledge_statements.title: Pair-Indexed KKT Multiplier Mapping and Calmness
Multiplier-Mapping Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calmness of the localized KKT multiplier mapping at a reference primal-parameter pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the parameterized program with a selected primal solution \(x(p)\), let \(M(p)\) be the set of multiplier pairs satisfying the KKT conditions at \(x(p)\). Given \((\bar p,\bar\mu)\in\operatorname{gph}M\), the multiplier mapping is calm at \((\bar p,\bar\mu)\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(\kappa\ge0\) such that
\[M(p)\cap V\subseteq M(\bar p)+\kappa\lVert p-\bar p\rVert\mathbb B\qquad(p\in U).\]
It is locally Lipschitz single-valued if \(M(p)\cap V=\{\mu(p)\}\) and \(\lVert\mu(p)-\mu(q)\rVert\le\kappa\lVert p-q\rVert\) locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier stability means nearby KKT multipliers remain linearly close to reference multipliers; the strongest local form is a unique Lipschitz multiplier branch.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Regularity of the KKT Generalized Equation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Write the KKT system as the generalized equation \(0\in F(z,p)+N_C(z)\), where \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), \(p\in\mathbb R^q\), \(F\) is differentiable in \(z\), \(C\) is a closed convex set encoding sign or complementarity structure, and \(N_C\) is its normal-cone mapping.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional generalized equations and their use as a local interface for NLP KKT stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The generalized equation is strongly regular at \((\bar z,\bar p)\) for \(0\) if \(0\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+N_C(\bar z)\) and there are neighborhoods \(V\) of \(\bar z\), \(W\) of \(0\), and a constant \(L\) such that, for every \(r\in W\), the partially linearized equation \[r\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+D_zF(\bar z,bar p)(z-\bar z)+N_C(z)\] has exactly one solution \(z(r)\in V\), and \[\|z(r_1)-z(r_2)\|\le L\|r_1-r_2\|.\] The Robinson interface consists of representing the NLP KKT conditions in this form so that strong regularity yields a locally unique Lipschitz primal-dual response to small residual or parameter perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong regularity requires the inverse of the linearized generalized equation to be locally single-valued and Lipschitz. The NLP interface is obtained by expressing stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity as one generalized equation in the primal-dual variables.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable with respect to \(z\) at \((\bar z,\bar p)\).
\(C\) is closed and convex, so \(N_C\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r\mapsto\{z\in V:r\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+D_zF(\bar z,\bar p)(z-\bar z)+N_C(z)\}\] is single-valued and Lipschitz near \(r=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Strong regularity is local single-valued Lipschitz invertibility of the partially linearized generalized equation.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, the normal-cone term disappears and strong regularity reduces to nonsingularity of the bordered KKT Jacobian.
For polyhedral \(C\), the linearized system is a piecewise-linear generalized equation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Small residual perturbations admit a unique nearby primal-dual solution.
With suitable parameter smoothness, parameter perturbations inherit a locally Lipschitz KKT selection.
boundary_notes: Metric regularity without single-valued localization is weaker than strong regularity.
The inspected local source states Robinson-type stability and metric regularity but not this exact strong-regularity definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LICQ Alone Does Not Give Strong Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of isolated Lipschitz stability when curvature is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\;\frac14x^4-px.\] LICQ is vacuous. Stationarity gives \(x^3=p\), hence the unique stationary solution is \(x(p)=\sqrt[3]{p}\). At \((p,x)=(0,0)\), the solution is isolated, but \(|x(p)|=|p|^{1/3}\) admits no local bound \(|x(p)|\le\kappa|p|\). Thus LICQ without nonsingular curvature does not imply strong regularity or Lipschitz solution stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quartic stationary problem has vacuous LICQ but only cube-root parameter dependence, showing that curvature nonsingularity is essential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LICQ}\not\Rightarrow\text{ strong regularity or local Lipschitz solution stability}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth primal-dual stability package under strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a twice continuously differentiable parametric NLP, let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) be a KKT point. Suppose LICQ holds, every active inequality multiplier is strictly positive, and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the null space of the active-constraint Jacobian. Then the fixed-active-set KKT Jacobian is nonsingular. Under sufficiently small smooth perturbations there is a unique nearby primal-dual KKT point with the same active set, depending continuously differentiably on the perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive reduced curvature yield a unique smooth primal-dual branch with persistent activity.
assumptions_latex: The NLP data are twice continuously differentiable in primal variables and continuously differentiable in parameters.
d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d>0\text{ for all }0\ne d\in\ker A(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a unique }C^1\text{ local KKT branch with constant active set}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature Without LICQ Does Not Stabilize Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of primal-dual uniqueness under redundant equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\frac12x^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad h_1(x)=x=0,\qquad h_2(x)=2x=0.\] The unique feasible primal solution is \(x=0\) and the objective has positive curvature, but LICQ fails. Stationarity is \(\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=0\), so the multiplier set is a line. Thus positive primal curvature without independent active gradients does not yield a unique localized primal-dual solution or strong regularity of the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant equalities preserve a unique primal minimizer but create infinitely many multipliers, so curvature alone cannot give primal-dual strong stability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla_{xx}^2L=1>0,\qquad\{\lambda:\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=0\}\text{ is non-singleton}.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Without LICQ Does Not Stabilize Multipliers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact smooth-equation package for an equality-constrained KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a twice continuously differentiable equality-constrained NLP, let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) satisfy KKT, let \(A=\nabla h(\bar x)\) have full row rank, and let \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\). The KKT Jacobian \[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular if and only if \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is nonsingular for a basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\). Under this condition, sufficiently small smooth canonical perturbations admit a unique \(C^1\) local primal-dual KKT branch. If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\), its primal points are strict local minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full equality-constraint rank plus a nonsingular reduced Hessian gives a unique smooth local KKT branch; positive reduced curvature additionally preserves strict local minimality.
assumptions_latex: The objective and equality constraints are twice continuously differentiable in x and smoothly parameterized.
A=\nabla h(\bar x)\text{ has full row rank}.
Z\text{ is a basis matrix for }\ker A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ nonsingular}\iff Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\text{ nonsingular};\qquad K\text{ nonsingular}\Rightarrow\text{a unique local }C^1\text{ KKT branch}.

notation.meaning: null-space basis of the equality Jacobian

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LICQ–Strong-SOSC Package for Robinson Strong Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth mixed-constraint KKT strong regularity without strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) be a KKT point of a twice continuously differentiable NLP. Assume LICQ and \[d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d>0\qquad(0\ne d\in C(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)),\] where \(C\) is the KKT critical cone: equality-linearized directions, zero derivative on positive-multiplier active inequalities, nonpositive derivative on zero-multiplier active inequalities, and zero first-order objective change. Then the canonically perturbed KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at the reference primal-dual point. It therefore has a unique localized Lipschitz primal-dual solution mapping. Strict complementarity is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ and positive Lagrangian curvature on the KKT critical cone give Robinson strong regularity and a unique local Lipschitz primal-dual branch, even with zero active multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The NLP data are twice continuously differentiable.
The displayed strong second-order sufficient condition holds on the multiplier-dependent KKT critical cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at }(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu).

Regularity Packages for Strong Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth NLP sufficient conditions for strong regularity of the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program with equalities and inequalities, and a KKT point \(( ar x, ar\lambda, ar
u)\). If the gradients of the equalities and active inequalities are linearly independent and
\[d^{\mathsf T}
abla_{xx}^2L( ar x, ar\lambda, ar
u)d>0\]
for every nonzero direction \(d\) in the KKT critical cone, then the KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at the reference primal-dual point. Consequently, sufficiently small canonical perturbations admit a unique localized primal-dual KKT solution depending Lipschitz continuously on the perturbation. Strict complementarity is not required for this strong second-order sufficient-condition formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ together with positive Lagrangian curvature on every nonzero critical direction yields a unique locally Lipschitz primal-dual KKT branch under canonical perturbations.
assumptions_latex: The NLP data are twice continuously differentiable.
The strong second-order sufficient condition holds on the KKT critical cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT generalized equation is strongly regular at \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\nu)\), hence has a unique Lipschitz localization under small canonical perturbations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical smooth NLP package ensuring a differentiable local branch under persistent activity; it is not asserted to be the weakest possible package.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical regularity package for strong local primal-dual stability is the conjunction of: \[(i)\ \operatorname{rank}A=\text{number of active constraints},\qquad (ii)\ \bar\lambda_i>0\ \text{for every active inequality},\qquad (iii)\ Z^THZ\succ0.\] These are respectively active-gradient linear independence, strict complementarity, and the strong second-order sufficient condition on the active tangent space. The package makes the active KKT Jacobian \[J=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\] nonsingular, separates active multipliers and inactive slacks from zero, and supports a locally unique differentiable primal-dual branch for sufficiently small right-hand-side perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard smooth package combines independent active gradients, positive multipliers on every active inequality, and positive-definite Lagrangian curvature on the null space of the active Jacobian. It gives a nonsingular active KKT Jacobian and separates the current activity pattern from transition boundaries.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{rank}A=m_a,\quad \bar\lambda_{\mathcal A_I}>0,\quad Z^THZ\succ0\] defines the classical smooth strong-stability package.

special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, strict complementarity is vacuous.
For an unconstrained problem, the package reduces to \(\nabla^2f(\bar x)\succ0\).

Active inequalities and inactive inequalities retain their sign classification under sufficiently small perturbations along the local branch.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Activity Persistence Along a Stable KKT Branch
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z(p)=(x(p),\lambda(p),\mu(p))\) be a locally unique continuous KKT branch near \(\bar p\). For inequalities \(g_i(x,p)\le0\), define \(\mathcal A(p)=\{i:g_i(x(p),p)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional NLPs; persistence is separated from strong regularity alone by explicit slack and multiplier separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The activity-persistence property at \(\bar p\) holds if there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar p\) such that \[\mathcal A(p)=\mathcal A(\bar p)\qquad\forall p\in U.\] A strong-regularity activity-persistence regime consists of a locally unique continuous primal-dual branch together with strict sign separation at the reference point: \[\lambda_i(\bar p)>0\quad(i\in\mathcal A(\bar p)),\qquad g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)<0\quad(i\notin\mathcal A(\bar p)).\] Continuity then preserves positivity of active multipliers and negativity of inactive slacks locally, while the KKT complementarity relations preserve equality for the positively multiplied constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activity persists when the same inequality indices remain binding throughout a neighborhood of the reference parameter. A stable continuous KKT branch yields this persistence when active multipliers are strictly positive and inactive constraints have strictly negative slack at the reference point.
assumptions_latex: A locally unique continuous KKT selection \(z(p)\) exists.
Active multipliers and inactive slacks are strictly separated from zero at \(\bar p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists U\ni\bar p\ \forall p\in U:\quad \mathcal A(p)=\mathcal A(\bar p).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The active-set indicator vector is locally constant along the selected KKT branch.
special_cases_latex: The smooth package of active-gradient independence, strict complementarity, and strong second-order sufficiency supplies a differentiable branch with persistent activity.
With equality constraints only, the activity statement is vacuous.
immediate_consequences_latex: The local KKT equations may be written using a fixed active set.
No inequality enters or leaves the active set inside the persistence neighborhood.
boundary_notes: Strong regularity without strict complementarity need not force a constant active set.
Weakly active constraints lie on activity-transition boundaries and are excluded from this persistence regime.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robinson strong regularity for a parameterized generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the KKT system be represented by the generalized equation \(0\in F(z,p)+N_C(z)\), and let \(0\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+N_C(\bar z)\). It is strongly regular at \((\bar z,\bar p)\) if the partially linearized equation
\[y\in F(\bar z,\bar p)+D_zF(\bar z,\bar p)(z-\bar z)+N_C(z)\]
has, for every sufficiently small \(y\), a unique solution \(z=s(y)\) near \(\bar z\), and the localization \(s\) is Lipschitz. For smooth NLP KKT systems, this property yields a unique Lipschitz-localized primal-dual response to small canonical data perturbations.

Activity-Persistence Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local active-set constancy under strong regularity plus strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a smooth parameterized NLP and a reference KKT point \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\nu)\). Suppose the KKT generalized equation is strongly regular, the constraint functions are continuous in the parameter, and strict complementarity holds: every active inequality satisfies \(\bar\lambda_i>0\). Then, on the unique localized primal-dual KKT branch \((x(p),\lambda(p),\nu(p))\), every reference-active inequality remains active and has positive multiplier for all sufficiently small perturbations. Every reference-inactive inequality remains strictly inactive by continuity. Hence
\[\mathcal A(x(p),p)=\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\]
throughout a sufficiently small parameter neighborhood.

Constraint data are continuous in the parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Only Weakly Active Indices Can Change on a Continuous KKT Branch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp local boundary for activity changes under continuous primal-dual stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\mapsto(x(p),\mu(p))\) be a continuous local KKT branch for \(g_i(x,p)\le0\). Every strictly inactive index at \(\bar p\) remains inactive nearby by continuity. Every active index with \(\mu_i(\bar p)>0\) remains active, because continuity gives \(\mu_i(p)>0\) and complementarity forces \(g_i(x(p),p)=0\). Therefore any local activity change can involve only indices satisfying \(g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)=0\) and \(\mu_i(\bar p)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a continuous KKT branch, strict inactivity and positive active multipliers persist; only weakly active constraints can switch status.
assumptions_latex: p\mapsto(x(p),\mu(p))\text{ is continuous and satisfies KKT complementarity locally}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A(x(p),p)\triangle A(x(\bar p),\bar p)\subseteq\{i:g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)=0,\ \mu_i(\bar p)=0\}\text{ locally}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong regularity does not preserve weakly active inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in\mathbb R^n\), consider \[\min_{x\ge0}\ \tfrac12\|x\|^2-p^\top x.\] Its KKT generalized equation is \(p\in x+N_{\mathbb R_+^n}(x)\). The inverse of \(x\mapsto x+N_{\mathbb R_+^n}(x)\) is the globally single-valued nonexpansive map \(p\mapsto P_{\mathbb R_+^n}(p)=p_+\); hence the generalized equation is strongly regular at \((x,p)=(0,0)\). With inequalities \(-x_i\le0\), \(\lambda(p)=(-p)_+\). At \(p=0\), every inequality is weakly active, while index \(i\) is inactive when \(p_i>0\) and active when \(p_i<0\). Thus strong regularity without strict complementarity does not imply local constancy of the active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthant projection is a strongly regular generalized equation whose weakly active inequalities change status across coordinate hyperplanes.
assumptions_latex: The normal cone is the convex-analysis normal cone to \(\mathbb R_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Strong regularity at }(0,0)\text{ holds, but the active set is not locally constant in }p.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthant-Projection Strong-Regularity Counterexample Family
Activity-Persistence Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong regularity alone does not preserve weakly active inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(p\in\mathbb R\), consider
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\ \tfrac12(x-p)^2\qquad\text{subject to }x\ge0.\]
The unique solution is \(x(p)=\max\{p,0\}\), and with the constraint written as \(-x\le0\), its multiplier is \(\lambda(p)=\max\{-p,0\}\). At \(p=0\), the constraint is active but weakly active because \(x(0)=\lambda(0)=0\). The primal-dual solution mapping is unique and Lipschitz near zero, yet the constraint is inactive for \(p>0\) and active for \(p<0\). Thus strong local primal-dual stability without strict complementarity does not imply activity persistence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-dimensional projection problem has a unique Lipschitz primal-dual solution, but its weakly active constraint switches status across zero.
assumptions_latex: The inequality is represented as \(-x\le0\) with multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local Lipschitz primal-dual stability holds at \(p=0\), but the active set is not locally constant there.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar formulas and active-set switch are directly checkable, and counterexample is the correct content kind. Nevertheless, unique Lipschitz primal-dual stability is asserted rather than explicitly connected to Robinson strong regularity of the relevant KKT generalized equation. Because the container concerns failure under strong regularity, that connection requires a direct source or an authoritative cited characterization.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a continuous KKT branch, strict inactivity and positive active multipliers persist; only weakly active constraints can switch status.
assumptions_latex: p\mapsto(x(p),\mu(p))\text{ is continuous and satisfies KKT complementarity locally}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A(x(p),p)\triangle A(x(\bar p),\bar p)\subseteq\{i:g_i(x(\bar p),\bar p)=0,\ \mu_i(\bar p)=0\}\text{ locally}.
knowledge_statements.title: Only Weakly Active Indices Can Change Status on a Continuous KKT Branch

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable, Entering, Leaving, and Weak Activity Regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Along a KKT branch \((x(p),\lambda(p))\) for inequalities \(g_i(x,p)\le0\), define slack \(s_i(p)=-g_i(x(p),p)\ge0\), multiplier \(\lambda_i(p)\ge0\), and complementarity \(s_i(p)\lambda_i(p)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local classification of inequality activity along a parameterized or iterative primal-dual branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each inequality index \(i\), the strict inactive regime is \(s_i>0,\lambda_i=0\), and the strict active regime is \(s_i=0,\lambda_i>0\). The weakly active transition boundary is \(s_i=0,\lambda_i=0\). An entering transition at \(\bar p\) occurs if there are sequences \(p_k^I\to\bar p\) and \(p_k^A\to\bar p\) for which \(s_i(p_k^I)>0\) and \(s_i(p_k^A)=0\); a leaving transition is the reverse orientation along a specified parameter path. A persistent regime is a neighborhood on which the relevant strict classification is constant. For several constraints, an activity-transition regime is the product stratification generated by these per-index states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each inequality is strictly inactive, strictly active, or weakly active according to its slack and multiplier. Weakly active points form transition boundaries where nearby branches or parameter directions can place the constraint on either side of the active-set classification.
assumptions_latex: Primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity hold along the branch.
Slacks and multipliers are evaluated with one fixed inequality sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(s_i,\lambda_i)\in\{(s,0):s>0\}\cup\{(0,\lambda):\lambda>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\] defines the inactive, active, and weak transition regimes.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Strict complementarity excludes the weakly active state \((s_i,\lambda_i)=(0,0)\).
special_cases_latex: A locally persistent active set contains no entering or leaving transition.
At a degenerate solution, one or more active indices may be weakly active.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only weakly active indices can change status without violating continuity of both slack and multiplier.
Strict sign margins yield a neighborhood with constant classification.
boundary_notes: A weakly active constraint need not actually change status along every perturbation direction.
Multiple simultaneous transitions may require a finer stratification than a single entering or leaving label.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary parametric bound problem exhibiting loss of activity at a zero-multiplier reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}(x-p)^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\le0.\] Its unique solution is \(x(p)=\min\{p,0\}\). At \(p=0\), the constraint is active with multiplier zero. It is inactive for every \(p<0\) and active for every \(p>0\). Thus reference activity need not persist without strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-multiplier active constraint can become inactive under arbitrarily small parameter perturbations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active set of the unique solution is not locally constant at \(p=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Activity Need Not Persist

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of individual or complete inequality activity along a specified localized solution selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g_i(x,p)\le0\) and a specified localized feasible solution selection \(x(p)\) with \(x(\bar p)=\bar x\), an index \(i\in\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\) is locally persistently active along this selection if a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar p\) exists such that \[g_i(x(p),p)=0\qquad(p\in U).\] The complete activity pattern is locally persistent when \[\mathcal A(x(p),p)=\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\qquad(p\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is locally persistently active when it remains binding along the specified nearby solution branch; full persistence means that branch has a locally constant active set.
assumptions_latex: \(x(p)\) is a specified localized feasible solution selection with \(x(\bar p)=\bar x\).
The inequality index set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full local persistence is precisely local constancy of \(\mathcal A(x(p),p)\) along the selection.
knowledge_statements.title: Locally Persistent Activity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Complementarity Preserves Activity along a Continuous KKT Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient branchwise condition for locally constant activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x(p),\lambda(p))\) be a continuous local primal–inequality-multiplier KKT selection for continuous constraints \(g_i(x,p)\le0\). If every reference-active constraint is strictly complementary, \[i\in\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\ \Longrightarrow\ \lambda_i(\bar p)>0,\] then, after restricting the parameter neighborhood, \[\mathcal A(x(p),p)=\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a continuous KKT branch, positive reference multipliers keep active constraints binding, while continuity preserves the strict slack of inactive constraints.
assumptions_latex: The inequality index set is finite.
Primal feasibility, dual nonnegativity, and complementarity hold along the selection.
Strict complementarity holds for every reference-active inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full active set is locally constant along the KKT selection.

notation.meaning: inequality multiplier along the KKT selection

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Complementarity Preserves Activity along a Continuous KKT Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order diagnostic for a weakly active constraint along a differentiable one-sided feasible branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t\mapsto(x(t),p(t))\) be a differentiable feasible branch for \(g_i(x,p)\le0\), with \(g_i(x(0),p(0))=0\) and KKT multiplier \(\mu_i(0)=0\). Set \(\phi_i(t)=g_i(x(t),p(t))\). Feasibility gives \(\phi_i'(0)\le0\). If \(\phi_i'(0)<0\), then \(g_i(x(t),p(t))<0\) for every sufficiently small \(t>0\), so index \(i\) becomes inactive. Persistence of activity along the branch requires \(\phi_i'(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative directional constraint derivative makes a weakly active constraint immediately inactive; continued activity requires first-order tangency.
assumptions_latex: x(\cdot),p(\cdot),g_i\text{ are differentiable along the branch}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi_i'(0)<0\Rightarrow i\notin A(x(t),p(t))\text{ for all sufficiently small }t>0;\quad i\in A(x(t),p(t))\Rightarrow\phi_i'(0)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Exit from Weak Activity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paired feasible branches showing that zero first derivative does not decide activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=x\le0\) at \(x=0\) with reference multiplier \(\mu=0\), consider \(x_1(t)=0\) and \(x_2(t)=-t^2\), \(t\ge0\). Along the first branch the constraint remains active; along the second it is inactive for every \(t>0\). Nevertheless, \[\left.\frac{d}{dt}g(x_1(t))\right|_{0}=\left.\frac{d}{dt}g(x_2(t))\right|_{0}=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two branches have identical first-order tangency, yet one retains activity and the other exits at second order.
assumptions_latex: The reference multiplier for g(x)=x\le0 is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangential Persistence and Higher-Order Exit

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Higher-Order Exit Test at a Weakly Active Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order refinement when the first directional constraint derivative vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(t)=g_i(x(t),p(t))\) along a one-sided feasible \(C^r\) branch for \(g_i\le0\), with \(\phi(0)=0\), \(\mu_i(0)=0\), and \(\phi^{(j)}(0)=0\) for \(1\le j<r\). If \(\phi^{(r)}(0)<0\), then \(\phi(t)<0\) for all sufficiently small \(t>0\), so index \(i\) becomes inactive. If \(\phi^{(r)}(0)>0\), such a one-sided feasible branch cannot exist. If all available derivatives vanish, finite-order information need not decide persistence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first nonzero higher-order derivative decides finite-order exit; flat contact remains inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi^{(r)}(0)<0\Rightarrow\phi(t)<0\text{ locally for }t>0;\qquad \phi^{(r)}(0)>0\Rightarrow\text{one-sided feasibility is impossible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Exit Test at a Weakly Active Boundary
Weakly Active Transition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak activity identifies points where active-set constancy can fail under arbitrarily small perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT point, an inequality index \(i\) is weakly active when \(g_i(\bar x,\bar p)=0\) and \(\bar\lambda_i=0\). Such an index is not protected by multiplier positivity: arbitrarily small perturbations may produce either \(g_i(x(p),p)<0\) with \(\lambda_i(p)=0\), or \(g_i(x(p),p)=0\) with \(\lambda_i(p)>0\). Consequently, weakly active points form potential transition boundaries between neighboring active-set regimes. Weak activity alone does not force a transition, but without additional nondegeneracy or directional information it precludes any general guarantee that index \(i\) remains active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active constraint with zero multiplier may become inactive or acquire a positive multiplier under small perturbations, so weak activity marks a possible active-set transition boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No general local activity-persistence guarantee follows for index \(i\) from weak activity alone.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x(p),\lambda(p))\) satisfy KKT complementarity for \(g_i(x,p)\le0\). Set \(s_i(p)=-g_i(x(p),p)\ge0\), so \(s_i(p)\lambda_i(p)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local complementarity-based coupling between multiplier degeneracy and active-set changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The multiplier-activity bifurcation set for index \(i\) is \[\mathcal B_i:=\{p:s_i(p)=0,\ \lambda_i(p)=0\}.\] A coupled bifurcation occurs at \(\bar p\in\mathcal B_i\) if arbitrarily close parameter values realize at least two distinct complementarity faces, namely points with \((s_i,lambda_i)\in(0,infty)\times\{0\}\) and points with \((s_i,lambda_i)\in\{0\}\times(0,infty)\), or distinct local KKT branches select those faces. For an index set \(J\), the coupling object is \(\mathcal B_J=bigcap_{i\in J}\mathcal B_i\), together with the adjacent activity patterns and multiplier sign patterns. The definition records that activity changes and loss or gain of positive multipliers meet at the complementarity corner.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier-activity bifurcation occurs at a weakly active constraint whose slack and multiplier are both zero and for which nearby parameter values or nearby KKT branches occupy different complementarity faces: inactive with positive slack or active with positive multiplier.
assumptions_latex: Primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity hold.
Slack and multiplier mappings are defined on the local branch or branch family under study.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bar p\in\mathcal B_i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s_i(\bar p)=\lambda_i(\bar p)=0,\] with bifurcation requiring adjacent realizable complementarity faces.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The bifurcation set is the preimage of the complementarity corner \((0,0)\) under \(p\mapsto(s_i(p),\lambda_i(p))\).
special_cases_latex: Strict complementarity implies \(\bar p\notin\mathcal B_i\) for every inequality.
Several weakly active indices can produce simultaneous activity-pattern bifurcation.
immediate_consequences_latex: A strictly active or strictly inactive constraint cannot bifurcate under sufficiently small continuous perturbations.
At \(\mathcal B_i\), classical smooth sensitivity based on a fixed active set may cease to apply.
boundary_notes: Membership in \(\mathcal B_i\) alone does not guarantee that both adjacent faces are attainable.
The exact named coupling taxonomy was not located in the inspected sources.

children.title: Multiplier Bifurcation
children.top_down_role: Local branching or abrupt changes in admissible multiplier selections.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LICQ Excludes Distinct Limiting Multiplier Branches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exclusion of distinct multiplier limits along convergent parametric KKT points near an LICQ reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a smooth finite-dimensional parametric NLP and KKT points \((p_k,x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\) with \((p_k,x_k)\to(\bar p,\bar x)\), extending inequality multipliers by zero outside their active sets. If LICQ holds at \((\bar p,\bar x)\), then the nearby multipliers are bounded and every multiplier cluster point is the unique KKT multiplier \((\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) at the limit. Consequently, distinct limiting multiplier branches cannot occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ at the limiting primal point forces every nearby convergent KKT branch to approach the same unique reference multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint gradients are continuous in \((p,x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\lambda_k,\mu_k)\to(\bar\lambda,\bar\mu).
knowledge_statements.title: LICQ Excludes Distinct Limiting Multiplier Branches
Multiplier Bifurcation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local branching definition for multipliers of a parametric finite-dimensional KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a parametric nonlinear program with parameter \(p\in P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\), and let \(S_{\mathrm{KKT}}(p)\) denote its set of primal-dual KKT triples \((x,\lambda,\mu)\). A multiplier bifurcation occurs at \((p_0,x_0)\) if there are sequences \(p_k\to p_0\) and KKT triples \((x_k^r,\lambda_k^r,\mu_k^r)\in S_{\mathrm{KKT}}(p_k)\), for \(r\in\{1,2\}\), such that \(x_k^r\to x_0\), both multiplier sequences converge, and \[(\lambda_k^1,\mu_k^1)\to(\bar\lambda^1,\bar\mu^1)\ne(\bar\lambda^2,\bar\mu^2)\leftarrow(\lambda_k^2,\mu_k^2).\] Thus the multiplier component of the localized KKT solution mapping has at least two limiting branches over the same primal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier bifurcation occurs when nearby KKT solutions approach the same primal solution through distinct limiting multiplier branches.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) and the primal-dual variables are finite-dimensional.
The displayed triples satisfy the KKT system at their respective parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((p_0,x_0)\) is a multiplier-bifurcation point of the localized KKT solution mapping.

notation.meaning: Set of primal-dual KKT triples at parameter p.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits the leaf, and the sequential statement is coherent, but “multiplier bifurcation” is being given a project-local definition without cited support. A source is needed to determine whether bifurcation should require distinct multiplier limits, local branches at common parameters, or failure of a stronger regularity property.

children.title: Activity-Pattern Bifurcation
children.top_down_role: Local branching or switching among feasible activity patterns.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Activity-Pattern Bifurcation at Weak Activity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar parametric problem with two activity patterns accumulating at one stationary solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}(x-p)^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\le0,\] the unique stationary solution is \(x(p)=\min\{p,0\}\). At \(p=0\) the active set is \(\{1\}\) and the multiplier is zero. Along \(p_k^-<0\) with \(p_k^-\to0\), the active set is empty; along \(p_k^+>0\) with \(p_k^+\to0\), it is \(\{1\}\). Hence \((0,0)\) is an activity-pattern bifurcation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solution of a scalar upper-bound problem approaches the same weakly active reference point through inactive and active parameter regimes.
assumptions_latex: Stationarity is understood in the KKT sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Two distinct activity patterns, \(\varnothing\) and \(\{1\}\), accumulate at \((x,p)=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Activity-Pattern Bifurcation at Weak Activity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential branching of active sets among localized parametric stationary solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the finitely many continuous inequalities be \(g_i(x,p)\le0\), and write \(\mathcal A(x,p)=\{i:g_i(x,p)=0\}\). A stationary solution \((\bar x,\bar p)\) is an activity-pattern bifurcation point if there are two sequences of feasible stationary solutions \((x_k^r,p_k^r)\to(\bar x,\bar p)\), \(r=1,2\), and distinct sets \(A_1\ne A_2\) such that \[\mathcal A(x_k^r,p_k^r)=A_r\] for all sufficiently large \(k\). Continuity implies \(A_1\cup A_2\subseteq\mathcal A(\bar x,\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activity-pattern bifurcation occurs when a stationary solution is approached by nearby stationary solutions having two distinct persistent active sets.
assumptions_latex: The inequality index set is finite.
Each \(g_i\) is continuous near \((\bar x,\bar p)\).
Both sequences consist of feasible stationary solutions under one specified stationarity concept.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At least two distinct activity patterns accumulate at \((\bar x,\bar p)\), and each is contained in the limiting active set.

notation.meaning: distinct eventually constant branch activity patterns

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Pattern Bifurcation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous Strictly Complementary KKT Branch Excludes Activity-Pattern Bifurcation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local stability condition ruling out activity-pattern branching along a localized KKT solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every nearby stationary solution in a localization belongs to one continuous KKT selection \((x(p),\lambda(p))\), the constraints are continuous, and strict complementarity holds at \((\bar x,\bar p)\). Then the active set is locally constant along the localization, so \((\bar x,\bar p)\) is not an activity-pattern bifurcation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique continuous strictly complementary KKT branch has a constant nearby active set and therefore cannot bifurcate by activity pattern.
assumptions_latex: All localized stationary solutions are represented by one continuous primal–dual KKT selection.
Every reference-active multiplier is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No two distinct persistent activity patterns occur in the localization.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Strictly Complementary KKT Branch Excludes Activity-Pattern Bifurcation

children.title: Coupled Bifurcation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where multiplier branching coincides with activity-pattern changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Bifurcation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous activity-pattern and multiplier branching in a parametric KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parametric KKT point \((p_0,x_0)\) lies in a coupled bifurcation regime if two sequences of KKT triples \((x_k^r,\lambda_k^r,\mu_k^r)\in S_{\mathrm{KKT}}(p_k^r)\), \(r\in\{1,2\}\), converge in their primal-parameter components to \((x_0,p_0)\), while their eventual active sets satisfy \(A_1\ne A_2\) and their multipliers satisfy \[(\lambda_k^r,\mu_k^r)\to(\bar\lambda^r,\bar\mu^r),\qquad (\bar\lambda^1,\bar\mu^1)\ne(\bar\lambda^2,\bar\mu^2).\] Hence the local KKT branches differ in both combinatorial activity and limiting dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled regime has nearby KKT branches that differ simultaneously in active-set pattern and limiting multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The inequality index set and all primal-dual spaces are finite-dimensional.
Each branch consists of KKT triples converging to the same primal-parameter point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point exhibits coupled activity-pattern and multiplier bifurcation.

notation.meaning: KKT solution set at parameter p.
Eventual active set on branch r.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), let \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\) be the true active set at a target solution. Let \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\) be an estimator or the active set of a subproblem, and let \(\mathcal W_k\) be the algorithmic working set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local identification by iterative constrained optimization methods; true, estimated, and algorithmic sets remain distinct.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence of estimated sets finitely identifies the true active set if \[\exists K<\infty\ \forall k\ge K:\qquad \widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*.\] A working-set method finitely identifies activity if the same condition holds with \(\mathcal W_k\), possibly after excluding equality indices that are included by convention. Identification is asymptotic rather than finite if every active index eventually has vanishing residual and every inactive index remains separated, but no finite \(K\) gives exact set equality. Identification of strongly active constraints means eventual equality only with \(\mathcal A_+^*=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\lambda_i^*>0\}\); it is weaker than full identification when weakly active constraints exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite active-set identification means that after some finite iteration, the estimated or working set equals the constraints truly active at the target solution and never changes again. Identifying only positive-multiplier constraints is weaker when weakly active constraints are present.
assumptions_latex: A target solution \(x^*\) and its true active set are fixed.
The estimated and working sets use the same constraint indexing and sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\quad \widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\] is finite identification.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Finite identification is eventual constancy of the set sequence at \(\mathcal A^*\).
special_cases_latex: Under LICQ, strict complementarity, and second-order sufficiency, a sufficiently local SQP subproblem can have the same active set as the NLP solution.
For bound constraints, identification fixes the variables at their eventual lower or upper bounds.
immediate_consequences_latex: After full identification, a method may use a fixed equality-constrained local model.
Failure to classify weakly active indices prevents full set equality even when strongly active indices are identified.
boundary_notes: Convergence of \(x_k\to x^*\) alone does not imply finite identification.
A correct subproblem active set and the method's retained working set need not coincide without an explicit update rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: True, Estimated, and Algorithmic Activity Sets
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a feasible point \(x\) of an NLP with equality index set \(\mathcal E\) and inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), let \(\mathcal I\) be the inequality index set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set taxonomy for feasible NLP points and active-set algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The true active set is \[\mathcal A(x)=\mathcal E\cup\{i\in\mathcal I:g_i(x)=0\}.\] An estimated active set is any data-dependent set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}(x,\eta)\) intended to approximate \(\mathcal A(x^*)\); a standard residual estimate is \[\widehat{\mathcal A}_\eta(x)=\mathcal E\cup\{i\in\mathcal I:-\eta\le g_i(x)\le0\}\] for feasible \(x\) and tolerance \(\eta\ge0\). An algorithmic working set \(\mathcal W_k\) is the subset that iteration \(k\) actually imposes as equalities in its local subproblem. Consequently, \(\mathcal W_k\), \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\), and \(\mathcal A(x_k)\) are different objects; an algorithm may require \(\mathcal W_k\subseteq\mathcal A(x_k)\) while allowing a proper subset to preserve linear independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The true active set consists of equalities and inequalities binding at a feasible point. An estimated set is produced by a residual or multiplier test. The working set is the subset actually imposed as equalities by an algorithm, and it need not equal either of the other sets.
assumptions_latex: The point \(x\) is feasible for the displayed residual estimator.
All equality constraints are included by convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal A(x),\qquad\widehat{\mathcal A}_\eta(x),\qquad\mathcal W_k\] are respectively geometric, inferential, and algorithmic activity objects.
special_cases_latex: At tolerance \(\eta=0\), the residual estimator equals the true active set at a feasible point.
A working set may be a linearly independent proper subset of the active set.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact identification requires eventual equality with the true set, not merely internal consistency of the working set.
Multiple blocking constraints may become active while only one is added to the working set.
boundary_notes: The residual estimator is one standard family, not a universal algorithmic rule.
At infeasible iterates, a two-sided residual estimator requires a modified definition.

notation.meaning: constraints imposed as equalities at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: True Active Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact inequality-constraint activity at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) and \(I\) be finite disjoint index sets, and let \(h_j:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(j\in E\) and \(g_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(i\in I\). Define the feasible set \[\mathcal F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h_j(x)=0\ (j\in E),\ g_i(x)\le 0\ (i\in I)\}.\] For \(x\in\mathcal F\), the true active set of inequality constraints is \[\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in I:g_i(x)=0\}.\] Every equality constraint is binding by definition and may be recorded separately as \(E\); the inactive inequality set is \(I\setminus\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in I:g_i(x)<0\}\). At a designated feasible solution \(x^*\), write \(\mathcal A^*=\mathcal A(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The true active set contains exactly the inequality constraints whose values equal zero at the feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(I\) are finite disjoint index sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in I:g_i(x)=0\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible point \(x\), define \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I\mid c_i(x)=0\}\). For each index set \(\mathcal S\), define \(\mathcal F_{\mathcal S}=\{x\in\mathcal C\mid\mathcal A(x)=\mathcal S\}\); the nonempty classes \(\mathcal F_{\mathcal S}\) partition \(\mathcal C\). knowledge_statements.title: Algorithmic Working Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint subset enforced as equalities in an active-set subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite index set and let differentiable functions \(g_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) define inequalities \(g_i(x)\le 0\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Working-set active-set strategy and its combinatorial limitation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic template for inequality-constrained nonlinear programs. Acceptance after a KKT check is the method description in the extract, not a general theorem that KKT conditions alone suffice for local optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inequality-constrained nonlinear program with finite inequality index set \(\mathcal I\), an active-set strategy selects a working set \(\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal I\), imposes the constraints in \(\mathcal W\) as equalities, temporarily ignores those outside \(\mathcal W\), and solves the resulting equality-constrained subproblem. It then checks whether multipliers can be chosen so that the computed point satisfies the KKT conditions of the full problem; if the check fails, it changes \(\mathcal W\). The family of possible working sets is the power set of \(\mathcal I\), containing \(2^{|\mathcal I|}\) subsets, so a strategy that exhaustively examines all working sets faces an exponentially growing search space and is not practical in general. The KKT check is an algorithmic acceptance rule here; without additional sufficient conditions, KKT satisfaction alone does not establish local optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active-set strategy guesses a working set, imposes those inequalities as equalities, temporarily ignores the others, and solves the resulting equality-constrained problem. It checks the full KKT conditions and changes the working set if the check fails. With m inequalities there are 2^m possible subsets, so exhaustive working-set enumeration has an exponentially growing search space. The KKT check is an acceptance rule, not by itself a general sufficiency theorem for local optimality.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal I\text{ is a finite index set for the inequality constraints.}
\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal I\text{ is the current working set.}
x^*\text{ is obtained by solving the equality-constrained subproblem defined by }\mathcal W.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \#\{\mathcal W:\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal I\}=2^{|\mathcal I|};\quad\text{hence exhaustive working-set enumeration has an exponentially growing search space.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column and variable partition maintained by an active-set method for a linearly constrained problem with equality constraints and simple bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and suppose the current working set contains the \(m\) equality rows and \(r\) active bound rows. With variables suitably ordered, an active-set representation partitions \[A=(B\;S\;N),\] where \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular, \(N\) contains the \(r\) columns associated with nonbasic variables fixed at bounds, and \(S\) contains the \(n-m-r\) columns associated with superbasic variables. The working-set equations are \[\begin{pmatrix}B&S&N\\0&0&I_r\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x_B\\x_S\\x_N\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}b\\b_N\end{pmatrix},\] where each component of \(b_N\) is the binding lower or upper bound. Thus the working-set feasible degrees of freedom number \(n-m-r\). In the LP basic-feasible case, \(r=n-m\) and \(S\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an active-set iteration with m equality constraints and r selected active bounds, the variables can be partitioned into m basic variables associated with a nonsingular basis B, r bound-fixed nonbasic variables, and n−m−r superbasic variables. The superbasic count equals the remaining working-set degrees of freedom. In the LP basic-feasible case, no superbasic variables remain.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inactive affine inequalities that jointly determine a truncated maximal feasible step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be finite and let affine inequalities \(g_i(x)=a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\le 0\) be given, where \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is feasible. Let \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(a_i^{\mathsf T}d\le 0\) for every currently binding inequality. Define \(D(x,d)=\{i\in I:g_i(x)<0,\ a_i^{\mathsf T}d>0\}\) and, for \(i\in D(x,d)\), define \(\alpha_i=-g_i(x)/(a_i^{\mathsf T}d)\). With the convention \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\), set \[\alpha_*=\min\left\{1,\min_{i\in D(x,d)}\alpha_i\right\}.\] The blocking set for the candidate full step is \[\mathcal K(x,d)=\{i\in D(x,d):\alpha_i=\alpha_*<1\}.\] Its members are precisely the inactive inequalities first reached before completion of the normalized full step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The blocking set consists of the inactive affine inequalities that tie for the shortest feasible step and truncate the normalized full step; it is empty when no constraint is reached before step length one.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i^{\mathsf T}d\le 0\) for every inequality binding at \(x\).
The candidate full-step length is normalized to \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(i\in\mathcal K(x,d)\), \(g_i(x+\alpha_*d)=0\), and no step with length greater than \(\alpha_*\) is feasible along \(d\).

notation.meaning: Inactive inequalities whose values increase along d and can block the step.

If \(\alpha_*<1\), then \(\alpha_*=\bar\alpha\) is the maximal feasible step length along the affine ray and every \(\alpha>\alpha_*\) violates at least one blocking inequality. If \(\alpha_*=1\), the capped ratio test certifies feasibility only through the proposed full step: it does not imply that every \(\alpha>1\) is infeasible. Thus uncapped ray maximality and maximality within the trial interval \([0,1]\) must be distinguished.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the affine setting of the blocking-set definition, suppose \(0<\alpha_*<1\) and set \(x^+=x+\alpha_*d\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Identification guarantee family for an active-set estimator
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\ge 0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\), with finite \(\mathcal I\). Let \(x_k\to x^*\), let \(\mathcal A^*:=\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), and let an estimator produce either a set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal I\) or scores \(p_k\in[0,1]^{\mathcal I}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic smooth nonlinear programming; the definition classifies guarantees rather than asserting that a particular algorithm possesses one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An identification guarantee is a quantified predicate \(G((x_k,z_k),\mathcal A^*)\) relating an algorithmic state sequence \(z_k\), its active-set output, and the target \(\mathcal A^*\). The canonical guarantee family consists of: finite exact identification, \(\exists K<\infty\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\); asymptotic score identification, \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|p_k-\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A^*}\|=0\); one-sided identification, \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\mathcal A^*\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\) or \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal A^*\); and identification in probability, \(\mathbb P(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*)\to1\), when the estimator is random. A guarantee family is a collection of such predicates indexed by the admissible problem class, estimator, convergence mode, and target set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convergent nonlinear-programming iteration, an identification guarantee is a quantified relation between the algorithmic state, the estimated active set or activity scores, and the true active set at the limit. The principal families are eventual exact equality, convergence of continuous activity scores to the target incidence vector, eventual one-sided inclusion, and—when randomness is present—probability of exact classification tending to one. A family records the problem class, estimator, target, and convergence mode for which the predicate is asserted.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I\) is finite and \(c_i(x^*)\ge0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal I\).
Each output \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\) is a subset of \(\mathcal I\), or each score satisfies \(p_k\in[0,1]^{\mathcal I}\).
The target is fixed as \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), unless an explicitly stated identifiable subset replaces it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) belongs to the identification-guarantee family precisely when it specifies, with explicit quantifiers, how \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\) or \(p_k\) approaches the designated target active set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Finite exact identification is equivalent to \(\mathbf 1_{\widehat{\mathcal A}_k}=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A^*}\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
For finite \(\mathcal I\), asymptotic score identification is equivalent to componentwise convergence \(p_{k,i}\to1\) on \(\mathcal A^*\) and \(p_{k,i}\to0\) on \(\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal A^*\).
special_cases_latex: A deterministic set-valued estimator uses the finite-exact or one-sided predicates.
A randomized estimator may use almost-sure, in-probability, or mean score convergence, provided the mode is stated explicitly.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(p_k\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal A^*}\), then thresholding at any fixed \(\theta\in(0,1)\) yields \(\{i:p_{k,i}\ge\theta\}=\mathcal A^*\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
boundary_notes: Convergence of iterates alone is not an identification guarantee.
A working set used internally by an algorithm need not equal the estimator output or the geometrically active set.

notation.meaning: estimated active set at iteration k
incidence vector of the target active set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual equality between an algorithmic estimate and the solution active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\) be iterates for an inequality-constrained problem, let \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\), and let \(A_k\subseteq I\) be the active-set estimate or working set produced at iteration \(k\). The sequence has the finite exact identification property at \(x^*\) if there exists a finite index \(K\) such that \[A_k=\mathcal A^*\qquad\text{for every }k\ge K.\] The property concerns stabilization of the discrete constraint pattern; it does not assert that \(x_K=x^*\) or that the continuous primal iterates terminate finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite exact identification means that after some finite iteration the estimated or working set equals the solution’s true active set forever.
assumptions_latex: The inequality index set \(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K<\infty\;\forall k\ge K:\ A_k=\mathcal A^*\).

notation.meaning: Estimated active set or working set at iteration k.
True active inequality set at the limit solution.
