knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\) be iterates for a nonlinear program with finite inequality index set \(\mathcal I\). Define \(\mathcal A^*=\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), and let \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal I\) be the active set estimated from the state available at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional identification of a fixed, finite target set; no rate of convergence of the primal iterates is built into the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The estimator finitely and exactly identifies \(\mathcal A^*\) along the sequence if there exists an integer \(K<\infty\) such that \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\) for every \(k\ge K\). Uniform finite exact identification on a class \(\mathscr S\) of admissible sequences means \(\exists K<\infty\ \forall (x_k,z_k)\in\mathscr S\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\). Sequencewise finite identification instead permits \(K\) to depend on the sequence and problem instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An estimator has finite exact identification when, after some finite iteration, its estimated active set equals the target active set at every subsequent iteration. The quantifier order distinguishes a uniform guarantee, which uses one identification index for an entire sequence class, from a sequencewise guarantee, whose identification index may depend on the particular problem and run.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I\) and hence \(\mathcal A^*\) are finite.
A target point \(x^*\) and target set \(\mathcal A^*\) are fixed.
The estimator output \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\) is defined for every sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K<\infty\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\triangle\mathcal A^*=\varnothing\).
\(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\mathbf1_{\widehat{\mathcal A}_k}=\mathbf1_{\mathcal A^*}\).
Finite exact identification is the conjunction of eventual no-false-positive and no-false-negative conditions.
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal A^*=\varnothing\), the condition becomes \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\varnothing\) eventually.
If an algorithm's working set \(\mathcal W_k\) is the estimator, replace \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\) by \(\mathcal W_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every set-valued statistic depending only on \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\) is constant at its target value for \(k\ge K\).
Finite exact identification implies eventual stabilization, but stabilization at an incorrect set does not imply identification.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require \(x_K=x^*\).
Repeated equality along a subsequence is insufficient; equality must hold at every iteration after \(K\).
For an infinite constraint index set, the same formula requires additional set-topological conventions.
review_flags: The definition is mathematically explicit, but no supplied source was inspected and verified to use this exact quantifier formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite exact active-set identification
Asymptotic Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit-level separation of active and inactive constraints without finite pattern stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\), let \(A_k\subseteq I\) be estimated active sets, and let \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). The sequence asymptotically identifies activity if \[\max_{i\in A_k}|g_i(x_k)|\to0\] with the maximum over the empty set defined as zero, and every truly inactive constraint is eventually excluded: \[\forall i\notin\mathcal A^*\;\exists K_i\;\forall k\ge K_i:\ i\notin A_k.\] This notion allows some truly active indices to enter and leave \(A_k\) indefinitely, so it is weaker than finite exact identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asymptotic identification excludes truly inactive constraints eventually and selects only constraints whose residuals approach zero, without requiring exact finite stabilization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected constraints are asymptotically binding, and every index outside \(\mathcal A^*\) is eventually absent.

notation.meaning: Estimated active set at iteration k.
True active set at the limit point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed notion is uncited and is substantially weaker than common identification guarantees: the permanently empty estimate satisfies it, and with finite I and continuous constraints the residual condition largely duplicates eventual exclusion of inactive indices. A source is required to establish that this is an intended meaning of “asymptotic identification” rather than merely asymptotic correctness of selected indices.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal I\) be a finite inequality index set, \(x_k\to x^*\), and \(\mathcal A^*=\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x^*)=0\}\). An estimator assigns scores \(p_k=(p_{k,i})_{i\in\mathcal I}\in[0,1]^{\mathcal I}\), where larger values represent stronger evidence of activity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic score-based asymptotic identification. Continuous scores are used so that the notion is weaker than eventual equality of finite sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The score estimator asymptotically identifies \(\mathcal A^*\) if \(p_k\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal A^*}\), equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \(K_\varepsilon\) such that \(k\ge K_\varepsilon\) implies \(p_{k,i}\ge1-\varepsilon\) for every \(i\in\mathcal A^*\) and \(p_{k,i}\le\varepsilon\) for every \(i\notin\mathcal A^*\). More generally, a real-valued diagnostic \(d_k\ge0\) asymptotically identifies the target when \(d_k\to0\) and \(d_k=0\) represents exact target classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asymptotic identification means that continuous activity scores converge to the incidence vector of the true active set. Thus scores of active constraints tend to one and scores of inactive constraints tend to zero. The accuracy index may depend on the requested tolerance, so the definition does not itself require a finite iteration at which unthresholded scores become exactly zero or one.
assumptions_latex: Each score vector belongs to \([0,1]^{\mathcal I}\).
The score orientation is fixed: one denotes activity and zero denotes inactivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|p_k-\mathbf1_{\mathcal A^*}\|=0\) for any norm on \(\mathbb R^{|\mathcal I|}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(p_{k,i}\to1\) for all \(i\in\mathcal A^*\) and \(p_{k,i}\to0\) for all \(i\in\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal A^*\).
\(\max_{i\in\mathcal A^*}(1-p_{k,i})\to0\) and \(\max_{i\notin\mathcal A^*}p_{k,i}\to0\), with the maximum over an empty set taken as zero.
special_cases_latex: For probabilistic scores \(p_{k,i}=\mathbb P(i\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_k)\), the definition specifies convergence of marginal classification probabilities.
A scalar error diagnostic can be chosen as \(d_k=\|p_k-\mathbf1_{\mathcal A^*}\|_\infty\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For every fixed \(\theta\in(0,1)\), \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k(\theta):=\{i:p_{k,i}\ge\theta\}\) equals \(\mathcal A^*\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
boundary_notes: For binary set outputs over finite \(\mathcal I\), convergence in symmetric-difference cardinality already forces eventual exact equality; that discrete formulation is therefore not a distinct weaker regime.
The definition does not specify a convergence rate.

notation.meaning: activity score for constraint i at iteration k

review_flags: A precise source supporting score-based asymptotic identification, rather than a different set-convergence convention, is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic identification by activity scores

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix a class \(\mathscr S\) of admissible convergent algorithmic sequences, a finite target set \(\mathcal A^*\subseteq\mathcal I\), estimated sets \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\), and optional activity scores \(p_k\in[0,1]^{\mathcal I}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A logical hierarchy for guarantees defined on the same problem class, target, estimator output, and convergence mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For guarantee predicates \(G_1\) and \(G_2\), write \(G_1\succeq_{\mathscr S}G_2\) when \(\forall s\in\mathscr S:\ G_1(s)\Rightarrow G_2(s)\). Write \(G_1\succ_{\mathscr S}G_2\) when \(G_1\succeq_{\mathscr S}G_2\) and there exists \(s\in\mathscr S\) satisfying \(G_2\) but not \(G_1\). Under compatible outputs, finite exact identification dominates eventual one-sided inclusion and vanishing classification error. Almost-sure finite exact identification dominates identification in probability. Uniform finite identification dominates sequencewise finite identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The identification hierarchy orders guarantees by logical implication on one fixed admissible sequence class. A guarantee is at least as strong as another when every sequence satisfying the first also satisfies the second. Strict dominance additionally requires an admissible sequence on which only the weaker predicate holds. Typical comparisons place uniform finite exact identification above sequencewise finite identification, exact equality above either one-sided inclusion, and almost-sure exact identification above convergence in probability.
assumptions_latex: Both predicates are evaluated on the same sequence class \(\mathscr S\).
The target set and the meaning of estimator output are identical in both predicates.
Any comparison involving randomness uses a common probability space and explicitly matched convergence modes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_1\succeq_{\mathscr S}G_2\iff\forall s\in\mathscr S\,[G_1(s)\Rightarrow G_2(s)]\), and strict hierarchy is defined by the additional existence of a separating sequence.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Guarantees equivalent on \(\mathscr S\) satisfy both \(G_1\succeq_{\mathscr S}G_2\) and \(G_2\succeq_{\mathscr S}G_1\).
After quotienting by logical equivalence, \(\succeq_{\mathscr S}\) is a partial order.
special_cases_latex: For false-positive and false-negative counts, finite exact identification implies both counts are eventually zero.
Uniform identification has quantifiers \(\exists K\forall s\forall k\ge K\), whereas sequencewise identification has \(\forall s\exists K_s\forall k\ge K_s\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing \(\mathscr S\), the target, or the convergence mode can change or destroy a hierarchy relation.
Two guarantees may be incomparable when one controls false positives and the other controls false negatives.
boundary_notes: A hierarchy arrow must not compare predicates with silently different targets.
Asymptotic score convergence and finite exact set identification require an explicit link between scores and sets before they can be ordered.

notation.meaning: logical-strength preorder on the sequence class

review_flags: No inspected source was established to present this precise logical ordering and its quantifier-sensitive variants.

children.title: Partial Identification
children.top_down_role: Guarantees recovering only a designated portion of the relevant activity structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual correct classification of prescribed subsets of active and inactive indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\), let \(A_k\subseteq I\) be activity estimates, and write \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). Given a target active subset \(J^+\subseteq\mathcal A^*\) and a target inactive subset \(J^-\subseteq I\setminus\mathcal A^*\), the sequence partially identifies \((J^+,J^-)\) if there exists \(K<\infty\) such that \[J^+\subseteq A_k\quad\text{and}\quad A_k\cap J^-=\varnothing\qquad(k\ge K).\] No classification guarantee is imposed on \(I\setminus(J^+\cup J^-)\). Exact identification is the special case \(J^+=\mathcal A^*\) and \(J^-=I\setminus\mathcal A^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial identification eventually includes specified truly active constraints and excludes specified truly inactive ones, leaving all other indices unresolved.
assumptions_latex: The inequality index set \(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ J^+\subseteq A_k\subseteq I\setminus J^-\).

notation.meaning: Target subset of truly active indices to include.
Target subset of truly inactive indices to exclude.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is internally coherent and the definition role fits the leaf, but “partial identification” is parameterized here by arbitrary target subsets without cited support. A source is needed to establish whether the intended concept is this two-sided eventual classification, identification of only a subset of active constraints, or a sufficient-set guarantee.

children.title: Sufficient-Set Identification
children.top_down_role: Guarantees recovering a constraint set sufficient for a downstream local task.

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient-Set Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual identification of all strongly active constraints while excluding inactive constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider inequalities \(g_i(x)\le 0\), indexed by \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and a KKT pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\). Define \(A^*=\{i\in I:g_i(x^*)=0\}\) and \(A_+^*=\{i\in A^*:\lambda_i^*>0\}\). A sequence of estimated sets \((E_k)\) has the sufficient-set identification property at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) if there exists \(K\) such that
\[
A_+^*\subseteq E_k\subseteq A^*\qquad\text{for every }k\ge K.
\]
Thus every constraint needed by the selected positive-multiplier KKT representation is eventually retained, although weakly active constraints may remain unidentified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eventually the estimate contains every positive-multiplier active constraint, contains no inactive constraint, and may include or omit zero-multiplier active constraints.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a KKT pair for finitely many smooth inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ A_+^*\subseteq E_k\subseteq A^*\).

notation.meaning: active constraint set at the reference solution
active constraints having positive reference multipliers

children.title: Identification-Guarantee Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Coverage differences between partial, sufficient-set, exact, plus asymptotic guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Identification-Guarantee Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implication hierarchy among exact, sufficient-set, and positive-multiplier identification guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_+^*\subseteq A^*\subseteq I\), and let \((E_k)\) be estimated active sets. Exact identification, defined by eventual equality \(E_k=A^*\), implies sufficient-set identification \(A_+^*\subseteq E_k\subseteq A^*\), which implies eventual identification of every member of \(A_+^*\). If \(A_+^*=A^*\), the exact and sufficient-set guarantees coincide. If \(A_+^*\subsetneq A^*\), neither positive-multiplier identification nor sufficient-set identification forces eventual inclusion of every weakly active constraint in \(A^*\setminus A_+^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact identification implies sufficient-set identification, which identifies all positive-multiplier constraints; strict complementarity makes exact and sufficient-set guarantees equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_k=A^*\text{ eventually}\Rightarrow A_+^*\subseteq E_k\subseteq A^*\text{ eventually}\Rightarrow A_+^*\subseteq E_k\text{ eventually}.\)

source_refs.locator: Chapter 9 The Theory of Constrained Optimization p. 195

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 9 The Theory of Constrained Optimization p. 195

assumptions_latex: \(A_+^*\subseteq A^*\subseteq I\), and the displayed estimates are used for every sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_+^*\subsetneq A^*\Rightarrow (E_k=A_+^*)\text{ is sufficient-set but not exact};\qquad I\setminus A^*\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow(E_k=I)\text{ identifies }A_+^*\text{ but is not sufficient-set}.

notation.meaning: Positive-multiplier subset of the reference active set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic witnesses showing that both converses in the identification-guarantee hierarchy fail in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The implication hierarchy is generally strict. If \(A_+^*\subsetneq A^*\), the constant estimate \(E_k=A_+^*\) satisfies \(A_+^*\subseteq E_k\subseteq A^*\) but never equals \(A^*\), so sufficient-set identification need not be exact. If \(I\setminus A^*\ne\varnothing\), the constant estimate \(E_k=I\) contains \(A_+^*\) but also contains inactive indices, so positive-support identification need not be sufficient-set identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient-set identification can omit weakly active constraints, and positive-support identification can retain inactive constraints; therefore neither converse implication holds in general.
knowledge_statements.title: Strictness of the Identification Hierarchy

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth nonlinear program with inequality indices \(\mathcal I\), let \(z_k\in\mathcal Z\) denote the information available at iteration \(k\), potentially including \(x_k\), multipliers \(\lambda_k\), a trial step \(d_k\), residuals, and tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic estimator interface; randomized estimators arise by allowing an additional random argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An active-set estimator is a map \(E_k:\mathcal Z\to2^{\mathcal I}\), with output \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=E_k(z_k)\). A parameterized estimator family is \(\{E_{\eta}:\eta\in\mathcal H\}\), where \(\eta\) specifies thresholds, norms, scaling, and available state variables. It is proximity-based when membership is determined from current constraint slack; multiplier-aware when membership jointly uses primal slack and multiplier information; and linearized-model-based when membership is determined from a local model \(c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Td\). The definition of a family must state its state domain, parameter domain, membership rule, and target active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active-set estimator maps the information at an iteration to a subset of inequality constraints. A family collects such maps over explicit parameters such as tolerances and scalings. The main families are distinguished by the information used: current primal slack, primal and multiplier data together, or predicted activity in a linearized local model. Merely calling a subset a working set does not determine which estimator family generated it.
assumptions_latex: The state space \(\mathcal Z\) and parameter set \(\mathcal H\) are specified.
For every admissible state and parameter, \(E_\eta(z)\subseteq\mathcal I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_\eta:\mathcal Z\to2^{\mathcal I}\) is an active-set estimator family exactly when its parameterized membership rule returns a well-defined candidate active set from the declared algorithmic state.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Every set-valued estimator can be represented by binary scores \(q_i(z;\eta)\in\{0,1\}\) through \(E_\eta(z)=\{i:q_i(z;\eta)=1\}\).
A continuous score family \(s_i(z;\eta)\) induces estimators by thresholding \(E_{\eta,\theta}(z)=\{i:s_i(z;\eta)\ge\theta\}\).
special_cases_latex: A feasibility-only estimator has state \(z=x\).
A primal-dual estimator has state \(z=(x,\lambda)\).
A model estimator has state \(z=(x,d)\) or \(z=(x,d,\lambda)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Two estimators using the same tolerance but different state variables belong to different informational families.
An identification guarantee attaches to the composite sequence \(E_{\eta_k}(z_k)\), not to the family name alone.
boundary_notes: An algorithmic working set may include constraints for globalization or safeguarding and therefore need not be an active-set estimator.
Equality constraints are normally always present and are not classified by this inequality-active-set map.

notation.meaning: power set of the inequality index set

knowledge_statements.title: Family of active-set estimators

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider inequality constraints \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\), and a point \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), which need not be feasible. Let \(s_i(x):=\max\{c_i(x),0\}\) be the nonnegative interior slack and let \(v_i(x):=\max\{-c_i(x),0\}\) be violation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal, pointwise estimator using only constraint values and explicit nonnegative tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given scales \(\sigma_i(x)>0\) and a tolerance \(\tau\ge0\), the scaled proximity estimator is \(E^{\mathrm{prox}}_{\tau,\sigma}(x):=\{i\in\mathcal I:s_i(x)/\sigma_i(x)\le\tau\}\). For feasible \(x\), this is \(\{i:c_i(x)\le\tau\sigma_i(x)\}\). A two-tolerance variant separates candidate activity from excessive infeasibility by \(E^{\mathrm{prox}}_{\tau,\rho}(x):=\{i:-\rho_i\le c_i(x)\le\tau_i\}\), where \(\tau_i,\rho_i\ge0\). The family consists of these maps over declared choices of scales and tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximity-based estimator declares an inequality potentially active when its current interior slack is no larger than a prescribed scaled tolerance. If infeasible iterates are allowed, a two-sided band can exclude constraints whose violation exceeds a separate allowance. The scale and tolerance are part of the estimator and must be stated; otherwise proximity has no invariant numerical meaning.
assumptions_latex: The activity and infeasibility tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in E^{\mathrm{prox}}_{\tau,\sigma}(x)\iff \max\{c_i(x),0\}\le\tau\sigma_i(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For feasible \(x\), \(i\in E^{\mathrm{prox}}_{\tau,\sigma}(x)\iff0\le c_i(x)\le\tau\sigma_i(x)\).
With score \(p_i(x)=\max\{0,1-s_i(x)/(\tau\sigma_i(x))\}\) for \(\tau>0\), the set is \(\{i:p_i(x)>0\}\).
special_cases_latex: Unscaled proximity uses \(\sigma_i(x)=1\).
Exact primal activity uses \(\tau=0\) at feasible points.
Iteration-dependent estimators use \(\tau=\tau_k\) and \(\sigma_i=\sigma_{k,i}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For fixed positive scales, increasing \(\tau\) can only enlarge the estimated set.
At a feasible point, the zero-tolerance estimator equals the exact active set.
boundary_notes: Small slack alone contains no dual information and may include nearly active constraints having zero limiting multiplier.
For infeasible points, using \(c_i(x)\le\tau\) without a lower violation bound can classify severely violated constraints as active.
review_flags: No inspected source was verified to support the scaled and infeasible-iterate variants at a precise locator.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-proximity active-set estimator

children.title: Slack-Based Estimators
children.top_down_role: Active-set estimators organized by primal slack information.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Based Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Near-activity estimator obtained by thresholding inequality slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le 0\), define the nonnegative feasible-side slack by \(s_i(x)=\max\{0,-g_i(x)\}\). Given a tolerance \(\tau\ge 0\), the slack-based active-set estimator is
\[
E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;\tau)=\{i\in I:s_i(x)\le\tau\}.
\]
At a feasible point this is equivalently \(E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;\tau)=\{i:g_i(x)\ge-\tau\}\). For any sequence \(x_k\to x^*\) and \(\tau_k\downarrow0\), every inactive constraint is eventually excluded; an active constraint is included whenever \(-g_i(x_k)\le\tau_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is estimated active when its feasible-side slack does not exceed a chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuous for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;\tau)=\{i\in I:\max(0,-g_i(x))\le\tau\}.\)

notation.meaning: nonnegative feasible-side slack of constraint i

source_refs.locator: 3.4.1 Active set of constraints p. 91

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.1 Active set of constraints p. 91

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-Scaling Dependence of Uniform Slack Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation dependence of a common absolute slack tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde g_i=c_i g_i\) with \(c_i>0\). At a feasible point, the uniformly thresholded estimate based on \(\widetilde g_i\) is \[\widetilde E(x;\tau)=\{i:-c_i g_i(x)\le\tau\}=\{i:-g_i(x)\le\tau/c_i\}.\] Hence a fixed common absolute tolerance is generally not invariant under positive rescaling of individual constraint functions. With individual thresholds, compatible scaling \(\widetilde\tau_i=c_i\tau_i\) preserves classification because \(-\widetilde g_i(x)\le\widetilde\tau_i\iff-g_i(x)\le\tau_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common absolute slack tolerance depends on constraint scaling; scaling each individual threshold with its constraint preserves classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde E(x;\tau)=\{i:-g_i(x)\le\tau/c_i\}\), while \(-c_i g_i(x)\le c_i\tau_i\iff-g_i(x)\le\tau_i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Scaling Dependence of Uniform Slack Thresholds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order properties of the feasible-point slack-threshold estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be feasible for \(g_i(x)\le0\), and define \(E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;\tau)=\{i:-g_i(x)\le\tau\}\). If \(0\le\tau_1\le\tau_2\), then \[\mathcal A(x)=E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;0)\subseteq E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;\tau_1)\subseteq E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;\tau_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, slack estimates are nested as tolerance increases, and zero tolerance gives exactly the true active inequality set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(x)=E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;0)\subseteq E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;\tau_1)\subseteq E_{\mathrm{sl}}(x;\tau_2)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Nesting and Zero-Tolerance Exactness

children.title: Distance-Based Estimators
children.top_down_role: Active-set estimators organized by distance to constraint boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reference-set identification from boundary-distance margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*\) be a reference active set and \(B_i=\{x:g_i(x)=0\}\). If \(\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)\le\delta\) for every \(i\in A^*\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)>\delta\) for every \(i\notin A^*\), then \(\{i:\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)\le\delta\}=A^*\). Along \(x^k\to x^*\), a finite constraint family and positive boundary separation for inactive constraints permit such thresholds once \(\delta_k\) also dominates every active-boundary distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distance estimate is exact when its threshold lies between the active and inactive boundary-distance margins.
assumptions_latex: The constraint index set is finite.
The displayed active and inactive distance margins hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{i:\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)\le\delta\}=A^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Distance-Separation Identification Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Distance Equivalence Fails at a Degenerate Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of linear residual-distance comparison without boundary regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=x^2\) and \(B=\{0\}\), \(|g(x)|=x^2\) while \(\operatorname{dist}(x,B)=|x|\). Hence no \(\alpha>0\) satisfies \(\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,B)\le|g(x)|\) throughout any neighborhood of zero. Residual and distance thresholds therefore have different local scaling at this degenerate boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero-gradient boundary, residual magnitude can decay quadratically while distance decays linearly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\ne0,\,x\to0}\frac{|g(x)|}{\operatorname{dist}(x,B)}=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Distance Equivalence Fails at a Degenerate Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Equivalence of Boundary Distance and Residual Magnitude
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular-boundary comparison supporting distance-based activity thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\) be continuously differentiable near \(x^*\), with \(g(x^*)=0\) and \(\nabla g(x^*)\ne0\), and let \(B=\{x:g(x)=0\}\). Then there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) and constants \(0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty\) such that \[\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,B)\le|g(x)|\le\beta\operatorname{dist}(x,B)\qquad(x\in U).\] Thus distance and absolute-residual thresholds are locally equivalent after rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular constraint boundary, distance and absolute residual bound one another up to positive constants.
assumptions_latex: g is continuously differentiable near x^*.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,B)\le|g(x)|\le\beta\operatorname{dist}(x,B)\quad(x\in U).

notation.meaning: zero boundary of the constraint function

knowledge_statements.title: Local Equivalence of Boundary Distance and Residual Magnitude

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance under changes of constraint representation that preserve the zero boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i\) and \(\widetilde g_i\) have the same zero set \(B_i=\{x:g_i(x)=0\}=\{x:\widetilde g_i(x)=0\}\). Using the same norm and threshold, \[\operatorname{dist}(x,\{g_i=0\})=\operatorname{dist}(x,\{\widetilde g_i=0\}),\] so the distance-threshold classification of index \(i\) is unchanged. Distance-based activity therefore depends on the geometric boundary and chosen norm, not on the scaling of a defining function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint functions with the same zero boundary give the same distance classification when the norm and threshold are fixed.
assumptions_latex: The same norm and threshold are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(x,\{g_i=0\})=\operatorname{dist}(x,\{\widetilde g_i=0\}).

notation.meaning: common zero boundary of the two constraint representations

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Representation Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of changing the ambient norm used for boundary distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For norms \(\|\cdot\|_a\) and \(\|\cdot\|_b\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), there exist \(m,M>0\) such that every nonempty \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \[m\operatorname{dist}_a(x,B)\le\operatorname{dist}_b(x,B)\le M\operatorname{dist}_a(x,B).\] Thus changing norms preserves near-boundary classification after threshold rescaling, although equal numerical thresholds need not produce equal estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-dimensional norms give comparable boundary distances after rescaling the threshold.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is finite dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m\operatorname{dist}_a(x,B)\le\operatorname{dist}_b(x,B)\le M\operatorname{dist}_a(x,B).

notation.meaning: set distances induced by the two norms

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Norm Robustness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form boundary distance for affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i(x)=a_i^\top x-b_i\) with \(a_i\ne0\), let \(B_i=\{x:a_i^\top x=b_i\}\), and let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm with dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\). Then \[\operatorname{dist}_{\|\cdot\|}(x,B_i)=\frac{|a_i^\top x-b_i|}{\|a_i\|_*}.\] Hence \(\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)\le\delta\) is equivalent to \(|a_i^\top x-b_i|\le\delta\|a_i\|_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine constraint, boundary distance equals absolute residual divided by the dual norm of its normal.
assumptions_latex: Distance is induced by \(\|\cdot\|\), whose dual norm is \(\|\cdot\|_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}_{\|\cdot\|}(x,B_i)=\frac{|a_i^\top x-b_i|}{\|a_i\|_*}.

notation.meaning: dual norm of the affine constraint normal

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Boundary Distance Formula

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Near-activity estimator based on distance to each inequality's zero boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inequality \(g_i(x)\le0\), fix an ambient norm and let \(B_i=\{y:g_i(y)=0\}\). With the convention \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\varnothing)=+\infty\), define for \(\delta\ge0\) \[E_{\mathrm{dist}}(x;\delta)=\{i:\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)\le\delta\},\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)=\inf_{y\in B_i}\|x-y\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select an inequality when the current point lies within the chosen norm-distance tolerance of that constraint's zero boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_{\mathrm{dist}}(x;\delta)=\{i:\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)\le\delta\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Distance Active-Set Estimate
Distance-Based Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Near-activity estimator based on distance to individual constraint boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each inequality \(g_i(x)\le0\), let \(B_i=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(y)=0\}\). Given \(\delta\ge0\), define
\[
E_{\mathrm{dist}}(x;\delta)=\{i\in I:\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)\le\delta\},
\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)=\inf_{y\in B_i}\|x-y\|.
\]
If \(B_i\) is empty, its distance is \(+\infty\). Near a point \(x^*\in B_i\) where \(g_i\) is continuously differentiable and \(\nabla g_i(x^*)\ne0\), local error bounds make boundary distance and \(|g_i(x)|\) equivalent up to positive constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is estimated active when the current point lies within a prescribed distance of that constraint’s boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{dist}}(x;\delta)=\{i\in I:\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)\le\delta\}.\)

notation.meaning: boundary of the i-th inequality constraint

children.title: Hybrid Proximity Estimators
children.top_down_role: Estimator families combining slack information with geometric proximity.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Proximity Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimator combining residual and geometric proximity tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\) with boundaries \(B_i=\{y:g_i(y)=0\}\), let \(a_i,b_i>0\) be scaling constants. The conjunctive hybrid proximity estimator with tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is
\[
E_{\mathrm{hyb}}(x;\varepsilon)=\left\{i\in I:\max\left(\frac{\max\{0,-g_i(x)\}}{a_i},\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)}{b_i}\right)\le\varepsilon\right\}.
\]
It retains a constraint only when both normalized slack and boundary distance are small. An alternative disjunctive hybrid is obtained by replacing the maximum with the minimum; the combining rule must therefore be declared as part of the estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid estimator combines normalized slack and boundary-distance tests, with its conjunction or disjunction rule stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in E_{\mathrm{hyb}}(x;\varepsilon)\iff \max\{\max(0,-g_i(x))/a_i,\operatorname{dist}(x,B_i)/b_i\}\le\varepsilon.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conjunctive formula is internally coherent and the definition kind fits the leaf, but the specific normalized maximum construction and the proposed minimum-based alternative have no cited source. A specialized source must establish that these are recognized hybrid proximity estimators or clearly motivate the adopted convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Multiplier Set Identification by Vanishing Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual identification of the strongly active subset from convergent primal-dual estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^k,\widehat\lambda^k)\to(x^*,\lambda^*)\), let \(A_+^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0,\lambda_i^*>0\}\), and define \[E_k=\{i:g_i(x^k)\ge-\tau_k,\ \widehat\lambda_i^k\ge\eta_k\}.\] If \(\tau_k,\eta_k\downarrow0\), every index in \(A_+^*\) eventually passes both thresholds, and every index outside \(A_+^*\) eventually fails at least one threshold, then \(E_k=A_+^*\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). Sufficient margins are \(\max_{i\in A_+^*}|g_i(x^k)|\le\tau_k\), \(\eta_k<\frac12\min_{i\in A_+^*}\lambda_i^*\), and eventual primal or dual exclusion of every remaining index.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-dual thresholding eventually identifies the positive-multiplier set when both inclusion and exclusion margins separate.
assumptions_latex: The stated inclusion and exclusion margins hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_k=A_+^*\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }k.

notation.meaning: positive-multiplier active set at the reference KKT pair

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Multiplier Set Identification by Vanishing Thresholds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set monotonicity in the primal-proximity tolerance and multiplier cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(E(\tau,\eta)=\{i:g_i(x)\ge-\tau,\ \widehat\lambda_i\ge\eta\}\), if \(0\le\tau_1\le\tau_2\) and \(0<\eta_2\le\eta_1\), then \[E(\tau_1,\eta_1)\subseteq E(\tau_2,\eta_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing the primal tolerance or decreasing the multiplier cutoff can only enlarge the estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E(\tau_1,\eta_1)\subseteq E(\tau_2,\eta_2).
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Monotonicity of Multiplier-Aware Estimates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set estimator combining primal near-activity with positive estimated-multiplier significance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), a point \(x\), and a nonnegative multiplier estimate \(\widehat\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), choose \(\tau\ge0\) and \(\eta>0\), and define \[E_{\mathrm{mult}}(x,\widehat\lambda;\tau,\eta)=\{i:g_i(x)\ge-\tau\ \text{and}\ \widehat\lambda_i\ge\eta\}.\] This estimate targets constraints that are simultaneously close to their feasible-side boundary and supported by a significant positive multiplier estimate; it targets the positive-multiplier active set rather than every weakly active constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select an inequality when it is nearly active and its nonnegative estimated multiplier exceeds a positive cutoff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_{\mathrm{mult}}(x,\widehat\lambda;\tau,\eta)=\{i:g_i(x)\ge-\tau,\ \widehat\lambda_i\ge\eta\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjunctive Multiplier-Aware Active-Set Estimate
Multiplier-Aware Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set estimator combining primal near-activity with estimated multiplier significance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), a point \(x\), and a nonnegative multiplier estimate \(\widehat\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), choose \(\tau\ge0\) and \(\eta>0\). Define
\[
E_{\mathrm{mult}}(x,\widehat\lambda;\tau,\eta)=\{i\in I:g_i(x)\ge-\tau\ \text{and}\ \widehat\lambda_i\ge\eta\}.
\]
The primal test rejects constraints separated from their boundaries, while the dual test selects constraints supported by significant multiplier estimates. This estimator targets the positive-multiplier active set rather than all weakly active constraints; exact active-set identification consequently requires an additional condition such as strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is selected when it is nearly active and its estimated multiplier exceeds a positive significance threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{mult}}=\{i:g_i(x)\ge-\tau,\ \widehat\lambda_i\ge\eta\}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Nonuniqueness Makes Strong Activity Multiplier-Relative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed boundary concerning multiplier-dependent classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a feasible point admits KKT multipliers \(\lambda^a\) and \(\lambda^b\) with \(\lambda_i^a>0\) and \(\lambda_i^b=0\) at an active index, its positive-multiplier classification depends on the chosen multiplier.

assumptions_latex: The reference point admits KKT multipliers with different components at an active index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_+(x^*,\lambda^a)\ne A_+(x^*,\lambda^b).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For differentiable inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\), let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) be a trial or model step, and define the affine prediction \(\ell_i(x;d):=c_i(x)+\nabla c_i(x)^Td\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order model-based estimator; it classifies predicted constraint activity for a declared trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given positive scales \(\sigma_i(x,d)>0\), activity tolerances \(\tau_i\ge0\), and violation allowances \(\rho_i\ge0\), the linearized-model estimator is \(E^{\mathrm{lin}}_{\tau,\rho,\sigma}(x,d):=\{i\in\mathcal I:-\rho_i\sigma_i(x,d)\le\ell_i(x;d)\le\tau_i\sigma_i(x,d)\}\). If the model step is linearly feasible, so \(\ell_i(x;d)\ge0\), this reduces to \(\{i:\ell_i(x;d)/\sigma_i(x,d)\le\tau_i\}\). The estimator family is indexed by the rule producing \(d\), the scaling, and the tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearized-model estimator predicts which inequalities will be active after a trial step by evaluating each affine first-order constraint model. A constraint is selected when its predicted value lies in a declared band around zero. If the step satisfies the linearized inequalities, only the upper activity threshold is needed. The step-generation rule is part of the family because different trial steps can yield different estimated sets at the same point.
assumptions_latex: The trial step \(d\) and all scales and tolerances are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in E^{\mathrm{lin}}_{\tau,\rho,\sigma}(x,d)\iff-\rho_i\sigma_i(x,d)\le c_i(x)+\nabla c_i(x)^Td\le\tau_i\sigma_i(x,d)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a linearly feasible step, membership is equivalent to normalized predicted slack not exceeding \(\tau_i\).
If \(d=0\), the linearized-model estimator reduces to a proximity estimator based on \(c_i(x)\).
special_cases_latex: An active constraint of a quadratic-programming subproblem corresponds to \(\ell_i(x;d)=0\).
A common-tolerance unscaled family uses \(\tau_i=\tau\), \(\rho_i=\rho\), and \(\sigma_i=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The estimator can select a currently inactive constraint when the model predicts contact after the trial step.
Changing only \(d\) may change the estimated set even when \(x\) is fixed.
boundary_notes: The affine prediction need not equal \(c_i(x+d)\); second-order model error is outside the definition.
A model working set may additionally contain constraints imposed for numerical or globalization reasons.

notation.meaning: affine first-order prediction of constraint i

review_flags: A precise inspected source for this estimator-band definition and its scope was not available.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearization-Based Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicted active set obtained from affine constraint linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(x\) be the current point, and let \(d\) be a trial step. The affine predicted residual is \(\ell_i(x;d)=g_i(x)+\nabla g_i(x)^\top d\). For \(\tau\ge0\), define
\[
E_{\mathrm{lin}}(x,d;\tau)=\{i\in I:\ell_i(x;d)\ge-\tau\}.
\]
When the linearized subproblem enforces \(\ell_i(x;d)\le0\), this selects constraints whose predicted slacks are at most \(\tau\). The estimate concerns activity at the trial point \(x+d\), not necessarily at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is predicted active when its affine residual at the trial step is within tolerance of zero.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i\) is differentiable at \(x\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{lin}}(x,d;\tau)=\{i:g_i(x)+\nabla g_i(x)^\top d\ge-\tau\}.\)

notation.meaning: affine model of the i-th constraint residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Identification by a Linearized Margin
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for equality between the linearized estimate and a reference active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). If \(\ell_i(x;d)\ge-\tau\) for every \(i\in A^*\) and \(\ell_i(x;d)<-\tau\) for every \(i\notin A^*\), then \(E_{\mathrm{lin}}(x,d;\tau)=A^*\). In particular, if \(x+d=x^*\) and \(|g_i(x+d)-\ell_i(x;d)|\le q_i\), it suffices that \(q_i\le\tau\) for \(i\in A^*\) and \(g_i(x^*)+q_i<-	au\) for \(i\notin A^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The estimate is exact when the tolerance dominates active-model error while remaining below every inactive modeled slack.
assumptions_latex: The prediction-error bounds q_i are valid.
A^* is the reference active set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_{\mathrm{lin}}(x,d;\tau)=A^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Identification by a Linearized Margin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation between affine predicted residuals and actual residuals at the trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\nabla g_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz on the segment \([x,x+d]\), then \[|g_i(x+d)-\ell_i(x;d)|\le\frac{L_i}{2}\|d\|^2.\] Consequently, \(\ell_i(x;d)<-\tau-(L_i/2)\|d\|^2\) certifies \(g_i(x+d)<-\tau\), while \(g_i(x+d)=0\) implies \(\ell_i(x;d)\ge-(L_i/2)\|d\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz-gradient remainder bound transfers affine-model margins to actual trial-point residual guarantees.
assumptions_latex: g_i is continuously differentiable on the segment from x to x+d.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |g_i(x+d)-g_i(x)-\nabla g_i(x)^\top d|\le(L_i/2)\|d\|^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Linearization Prediction-Error Transfer

children.title: Model-Based Estimators
children.top_down_role: Activity estimators derived from local optimization models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy condition transferring modeled thresholds to actual trial-point residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(|m_i(x;d)-g_i(x+d)|\le\kappa_i\Delta^{q_i}\) whenever \(\|d\|\le\Delta\). Then \(m_i(x;d)<-\tau-\kappa_i\Delta^{q_i}\) certifies \(g_i(x+d)<-\tau\), while \(g_i(x+d)=0\) implies \(m_i(x;d)\ge-\kappa_i\Delta^{q_i}\). Thus the activity threshold must be calibrated to the model-error order and validity radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modeled activity margin is reliable only when it exceeds the model error on the valid step region.
assumptions_latex: The displayed model-error bound holds on the validity region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |m_i(x;d)-g_i(x+d)|\le\kappa_i\Delta^{q_i}.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Error Activity Transfer

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interpolation Alone Does Not Ensure Predictive Activity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when only zero-step interpolation is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=x\) at \(x=0\), both \(m_1(0;d)=d\) and \(m_2(0;d)=-d\) satisfy \(m_j(0;0)=g(0)=0\). For any \(d>0\) and \(0\le\tau<d\), the estimator based on \(m_1\) selects the constraint, while that based on \(m_2\) does not. Thus interpolation at \(d=0\) alone supplies no activity-prediction guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two interpolating models can make opposite activity predictions, so zero-step interpolation is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_1(0;0)=m_2(0;0)=g(0)\quad\text{but their threshold classifications disagree}.
knowledge_statements.title: Interpolation Alone Does Not Ensure Predictive Activity
Model-Based Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicted active set defined by general local constraint models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a point \(x\), let \(m_i(x;d)\) be a local model of the residual \(g_i(x+d)\), with \(m_i(x;0)=g_i(x)\). Given a trial step \(d\) and \(\tau\ge0\), the model-based estimator is
\[
E_{\mathrm{mod}}(x,d;\tau)=\{i\in I:m_i(x;d)\ge-\tau\}.
\]
If the model subproblem enforces \(m_i(x;d)\le0\), membership means that the predicted constraint slack is at most \(\tau\). Affine, quadratic, or surrogate constraint models yield distinct instances, so the model and its accuracy region are part of the estimator specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model-based estimator selects constraints whose modeled residuals at a trial step are close to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{mod}}(x,d;\tau)=\{i:m_i(x;d)\ge-\tau\}.\)

notation.meaning: local model of the i-th constraint residual

children.title: Estimator-Agreement Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where linearization-based estimates coincide with model-based estimates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic error-versus-margin criterion for agreement of residual, affine, and model estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), let \(E_a=\{i:a_i\ge-\tau\}\), \(E_b=\{i:b_i\ge-\tau\}\), and \(E_c=\{i:c_i\ge-\tau\}\). If \[|a_i-b_i|<|a_i+\tau|\quad\text{and}\quad |a_i-c_i|<|a_i+\tau|\quad\forall i,\] then \(E_a=E_b=E_c\). Conversely, \(i\in E_a\triangle E_b\) implies \(|a_i-b_i|\ge|a_i+\tau|\), and analogously for \(c_i\). Taking \(a_i=g_i(x+d)\), \(b_i=g_i(x)+\nabla g_i(x)^\top d\), and \(c_i=m_i(x;d)\) gives the slack, affine, and model estimator certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The estimators agree whenever each surrogate error is smaller than the exact residual's distance from the shared threshold; disagreement requires an error at least that large.
assumptions_latex: All estimators use the same sign convention and threshold \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{|a_i-b_i|,|a_i-c_i|\}<|a_i+\tau|\ \forall i\Rightarrow E_a=E_b=E_c\).

notation.meaning: symmetric difference of estimated active sets
reference residual's distance from the threshold

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Tolerance Estimator Agreement Certificate
Estimator-Agreement Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which residual, affine, and model-based estimates eventually coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k=x_k+d_k\to x^*\), and suppose models satisfy
\[
\max_{i\in I}|m_i(x_k;d_k)-g_i(z_k)|=o(\tau_k),\qquad
\max_{i\in I}|g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^\top d_k-g_i(z_k)|=o(\tau_k),
\]
where \(\tau_k\downarrow0\). Assume also that every \(i\in A(x^*)\) satisfies \(g_i(z_k)\ge-(1-o(1))\tau_k\). Then, for all sufficiently large \(k\), the slack estimator at \(z_k\), affine estimator, and model estimator with tolerance \(\tau_k\) all equal \(A(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The three estimators eventually agree when model errors are negligible relative to tolerance and active residuals remain inside that tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Affine and model residual errors are \(o(\tau_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{sl}}(z_k;\tau_k)=E_{\mathrm{lin}}(x_k,d_k;\tau_k)=E_{\mathrm{mod}}(x_k,d_k;\tau_k)=A(x^*)\) eventually.

notation.meaning: active set at the limit point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for this specialized eventual-agreement claim. Moreover, g_i(z_k)>=-(1-o(1))tau_k does not provide a margin that necessarily dominates the independent o(tau_k) affine and model errors, so those errors can still move a modeled active residual below -tau_k. A direct source and a quantitatively sufficient shared-margin hypothesis are required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp deterministic condition for agreement of residual, affine, and model threshold estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a common threshold \(\tau>0\), define \(E_a=\{i:a_i\ge-\tau\}\), \(E_b=\{i:b_i\ge-\tau\}\), and \(E_c=\{i:c_i\ge-\tau\}\). If, for every \(i\), \[|a_i-b_i|<|a_i+\tau|\quad\text{and}\quad |a_i-c_i|<|a_i+\tau|,\] then \(E_a=E_b=E_c\). More generally, disagreement for index \(i\) can occur only if at least one approximation error reaches the reference residual's distance from the threshold: \[i\in E_a\triangle E_b\Rightarrow |a_i-b_i|\ge|a_i+\tau|.\] Taking \(a_i=g_i(x+d)\), \(b_i=g_i(x)+\nabla g_i(x)^\top d\), and \(c_i=m_i(x;d)\) gives the corresponding slack, linearization, and model-estimator criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold estimators agree whenever every affine and model error is smaller than the exact residual's distance from the shared activity threshold.
assumptions_latex: All three estimators use the same sign convention and threshold \(\tau>0\).
No reference residual lies exactly on the threshold under the strict-margin conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{|a_i-b_i|,|a_i-c_i|\}<|a_i+\tau|\ \forall i\Rightarrow E_a=E_b=E_c.\)

notation.meaning: symmetric difference of two estimated active sets
distance of the reference residual from the activity threshold

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Identification regime for constrained nonlinear programming
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathscr P\) be a class of nonlinear programs, \(\mathscr S(P)\) a class of algorithmic sequences converging to a stationary point \(x^*\) of \(P\), \(E\) an estimator, and \(T(P,x^*,\Lambda^*)\subseteq\mathcal I\) a designated target.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A regime is a specification of structural hypotheses and identification semantics, not an identification result by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An identification regime is a tuple \(\mathfrak R=(\mathscr P,\mathscr S,E,T,\mathcal Q,\mathcal M)\), where \(\mathcal Q\) is a list of local regularity and degeneracy conditions and \(\mathcal M\) is a convergence mode. The associated guarantee has the quantified form \(\forall P\in\mathscr P\ \forall s\in\mathscr S(P)\), if \(\mathcal Q(P,s,x^*)\) holds, then \(E(s_k)\) identifies \(T(P,x^*,\Lambda^*)\) in mode \(\mathcal M\). Regimes are distinguished by strict complementarity, multiplier degeneracy, constraint geometry, target choice, and finite, asymptotic, deterministic, or probabilistic mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An identification regime packages the precise problem class, admissible convergent sequences, estimator, target set, structural conditions, and convergence mode used by an identification statement. Strict-complementarity, degenerate-multiplier, and geometry-based settings are different regimes because their hypotheses or identifiable targets differ. Naming a regime does not itself assert that identification occurs.
assumptions_latex: The problem, sequence, estimator, target, structural conditions, and convergence mode are explicitly declared.
The target \(T\) is a subset of the inequality index set.
Multiplier-dependent targets use a stated multiplier or multiplier set \(\Lambda^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak R=(\mathscr P,\mathscr S,E,T,\mathcal Q,\mathcal M)\) uniquely specifies the domain and semantics of an identification claim.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A regime can be represented as the domain of validity of the conditional predicate \(\mathcal Q\Rightarrow G_{E,T,\mathcal M}\).
Two regime descriptions are equivalent when they generate the same admissible instances, target, estimator output, and guarantee predicate.
special_cases_latex: A strict-complementarity regime includes positivity of all active multipliers in \(\mathcal Q\).
A geometry regime may target a minimal face or active manifold rather than every active constraint label.
immediate_consequences_latex: Identification guarantees from different regimes cannot be compared solely by their convergence mode.
Changing the target from the full active set to a strongly active subset changes the regime.
boundary_notes: Constraint qualifications and strict complementarity are distinct conditions and must not be conflated.
The tuple does not prescribe an algorithm or establish that its conditional guarantee is valid.
review_flags: The regime-tuple formalization is unsourced within the supplied material and requires an exact supporting reference.
knowledge_statements.title: Identification regime for constrained nonlinear programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact identification by a combined primal-dual threshold estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a strictly complementary KKT pair for finitely many locally Lipschitz inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\). Let \(x_k\to x^*\), \(\widehat\lambda_k\to\lambda^*\), and \(\tau_k,\eta_k\downarrow0\), with \(\|x_k-x^*\|=o(\tau_k)\). Define \(E_k=\{i:g_i(x_k)\ge-\tau_k,\ \widehat\lambda_{k,i}\ge\eta_k\}\). Then \(E_k=A(x^*)\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity, primal threshold accuracy, and multiplier convergence make the combined estimator equal the true active set eventually.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many locally Lipschitz inequalities.
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a strictly complementary KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ E_k=A(x^*).

notation.meaning: active inequality set at the KKT point

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Complementarity Threshold Identification
Strict-Complementarity Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact identification by a multiplier-aware estimator under strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(g_i(x)\le0\) and a KKT pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfying strict complementarity: \(g_i(x^*)=0\) implies \(\lambda_i^*>0\), while \(g_i(x^*)<0\) implies \(\lambda_i^*=0\). Let \(x_k\to x^*\), \(\widehat\lambda_k\to\lambda^*\), \(\tau_k\downarrow0\), and \(\eta_k\downarrow0\), with \(\|x_k-x^*\|=o(\tau_k)\) and \(\|\widehat\lambda_k-\lambda^*\|_\infty=o(\eta_k)\). Then
\[
E_k=\{i:g_i(x_k)\ge-\tau_k,\ \widehat\lambda_{k,i}\ge\eta_k\}
\]
equals \(A(x^*)\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict complementarity and suitably scaled primal-dual errors, the multiplier-aware estimate equals the true active set after finitely many iterations.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a strictly complementary KKT pair and each \(g_i\) is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ E_k=A(x^*)\).

notation.meaning: true active set at the KKT point

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\), let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions with \(\lambda_i^*\ge0\), \(\lambda_i^*c_i(x^*)=0\), and \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\). Let \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal I\) be an estimator output.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local primal-dual identification regime at a KKT point with a specified multiplier satisfying strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is strictly complementary when \(c_i(x^*)+\lambda_i^*>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal I\); equivalently, \(\lambda_i^*>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal A^*\) and \(c_i(x^*)>0\) for every \(i\notin\mathcal A^*\). Strict-complementarity identification is identification of the full set \(\mathcal A^*\) by an estimator along a sequence converging to such a pair, with the guarantee mode stated separately, for example \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict-complementarity identification concerns a primal-dual KKT limit where every active inequality has a positive multiplier and every inactive inequality has positive slack. In this regime, the identification target is the full active set. The phrase must still be paired with a mode such as finite exact or asymptotic identification; strict complementarity alone is a property of the limit pair, not an estimator guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity.
The multiplier \(\lambda^*\) used in the strict-complementarity condition is specified.
The estimator sequence and its convergence mode are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime condition is \(\min_{i\in\mathcal A^*}\lambda_i^*>0\) together with \(\min_{i\notin\mathcal A^*}c_i(x^*)>0\), using \(+\infty\) for a minimum over an empty set, and its identification target is \(\mathcal A^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under complementarity, strict complementarity is equivalent to \(c_i(x^*)+\lambda_i^*>0\) for all \(i\in\mathcal I\).
For finite \(\mathcal I\), it is equivalent to a positive separation margin \(\delta^*:=\min_i(c_i(x^*)+\lambda_i^*)>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal A^*=\varnothing\), strict complementarity reduces to strict inactivity of all inequalities.
With a unique KKT multiplier, the regime is independent of multiplier selection.
immediate_consequences_latex: The active set equals \(\{i:\lambda_i^*>0\}\).
Positive primal-dual separation permits threshold-based classification at the limit.
boundary_notes: When multipliers are nonunique, strict complementarity may mean existence of a strictly complementary multiplier or positivity of a designated multiplier; the convention must be stated.
Strict complementarity does not itself imply finite identification for an arbitrary estimator.
review_flags: Strict complementarity is standard, but no inspected locator was established for this exact identification-regime formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-complementarity identification regime
Identification without Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier thresholding cannot generally identify weakly active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Strict complementarity cannot be omitted from exact identification by positive multiplier thresholding. Consider
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R} x^2\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad -x\le0.
\]
At the unique solution \(x^*=0\), the constraint is active, but the unique KKT multiplier is \(\lambda^*=0\). Hence for every \(\eta>0\), the multiplier-aware rule \(E_{\mathrm{mult}}(x^*,\lambda^*;\tau,\eta)\) excludes the active constraint, for every \(\tau\ge0\). Thus convergence of primal points and multipliers alone does not guarantee exact identification when an active constraint has zero multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-multiplier active constraint can be missed forever by any estimator requiring a strictly positive multiplier threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(x^*)=\{1\}\) but \(E_{\mathrm{mult}}(x^*,\lambda^*;\tau,\eta)=\varnothing\) for every \(\tau\ge0\) and \(\eta>0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair for inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\). Define \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), \(\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\lambda_i^*>0\}\), and \(\mathcal A^0(\lambda^*)=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\lambda_i^*=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local identification when at least one active inequality is weakly active; full-set and partial-set targets are explicitly distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Identification without strict complementarity is an identification regime satisfying \(\mathcal A^0(\lambda^*)\ne\varnothing\). A full identification claim targets \(\mathcal A^*\), whereas a strong-active identification claim targets only \(\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)\). For an estimator \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\), finite full identification means \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal A^*\); finite strong-active identification means \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal A^*\). The latter leaves classification of zero-multiplier active constraints unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without strict complementarity, at least one active inequality has zero multiplier. Identification statements must then say whether the target is the entire active set or only the positively multiplied constraints. A common partial target requires all strongly active constraints to be selected and forbids inactive constraints, while allowing weakly active constraints to be either selected or omitted.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier selection is fixed when multipliers are nonunique.
The estimator and finite or asymptotic mode are explicitly stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is characterized by failure of strict complementarity and by an explicit choice between target \(\mathcal A^*\) and the partial target interval \(\{S:\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)\subseteq S\subseteq\mathcal A^*\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Failure of strict complementarity at the specified pair is equivalent to \(\min_{i\in\mathcal A^*}\lambda_i^*=0\) when \(\mathcal A^*\ne\varnothing\).
The partial finite condition is equivalent to eventual absence of false positives and eventual inclusion of every positive-multiplier index.
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)=\varnothing\), the partial condition requires only \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\subseteq\mathcal A^*\) eventually.
Additional geometric information may support full identification despite zero multipliers.
immediate_consequences_latex: A guarantee for \(\mathcal A^+(\lambda^*)\) is not automatically a guarantee for \(\mathcal A^*\).
Zero multiplier does not imply that an active constraint is geometrically redundant.
boundary_notes: The regime does not assert that full identification is impossible.
Multiplier-dependent partitions can vary with multiplier choice when the multiplier set is not a singleton.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point and let \(\Lambda(x^*)\) be its nonempty set of KKT multipliers for inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\). Define \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification regimes with possibly nonunique multipliers; the definitions separate multiplier-invariant and multiplier-dependent targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the uniformly strongly active set \(\mathcal A^{++}:=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)}\lambda_i>0\}\), the potentially strongly active set \(\mathcal A^{+}:=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)}\lambda_i>0\}\), and the uniformly zero-multiplier set \(\mathcal A^{00}:=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\lambda_i=0\ \forall\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)\}\). A multiplier-degenerate identification regime is one in which \(\mathcal A^{++}\ne\mathcal A^*\), or multiplier selection changes the positive-multiplier support. Its target must be declared as \(\mathcal A^*\), \(\mathcal A^{++}\), \(\mathcal A^{+}\), or the support of a selected multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When KKT multipliers are nonunique or contain zeros on active constraints, identification targets based on multiplier support can differ. Constraints may have multipliers bounded positively away from zero for every multiplier, positive for at least one multiplier, or zero for all multipliers. A multiplier-degenerate regime states which of these sets is the target and whether the estimator depends on a selected multiplier sequence.
assumptions_latex: All multipliers use the same constraint orientation and normalization.
The infimum and supremum are taken over the complete declared multiplier set or a specified normalized subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A^{++}\subseteq\mathcal A^{+}\subseteq\mathcal A^*\), \(\mathcal A^{00}=\mathcal A^*\setminus\mathcal A^{+}\), and a multiplier-degenerate identification statement must name one of these distinct targets or a selected-multiplier support.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(i\in\mathcal A^{00}\iff\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)}\lambda_i=0\), since inequality multipliers are nonnegative.
Multiplier-support invariance holds when \(\{i:\lambda_i>0\}\) is identical for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\Lambda(x^*)\) is a singleton \(\{\lambda^*\}\), then \(\mathcal A^{++}=\mathcal A^{+}=\{i\in\mathcal A^*:\lambda_i^*>0\}\).
If a strictly complementary multiplier exists, then \(\mathcal A^{+}=\mathcal A^*\), although \(\mathcal A^{++}\) may still be smaller.
immediate_consequences_latex: Identification of \(\mathcal A^{++}\) is invariant under multiplier selection.
Identification of a selected multiplier's support may change when the algorithm converges to a different multiplier.
boundary_notes: The condition \(\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)}\lambda_i>0\) can be too strong when the multiplier set is not compact; the declared multiplier set must make the infimum meaningful.
Primal activity \(\mathcal A^*\) remains defined independently of multiplier degeneracy.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at the target point

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Identification Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification guarantees when weak activity or multiplier degeneracy is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair with \(A_+^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0,\lambda_i^*>0\}\subsetneq A^*=A(x^*)\). Suppose \(x_k\to x^*\) and \(\widehat\lambda_k\to\lambda^*\). A multiplier-significance estimator can stably identify \(A_+^*\) when its positive threshold vanishes more slowly than multiplier-estimation error, but these assumptions do not determine membership of \(A^*\setminus A_+^*\). Consequently, without an independent primal, geometric, or algorithmic separation condition, the generally supportable guarantee is sufficient-set identification rather than exact identification of \(A^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero-multiplier active constraints, multiplier information can identify the positive-multiplier subset but does not generally determine the full active set.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a KKT pair with \(A_+^*\subsetneq A^*\).
The multiplier threshold dominates \(\|\widehat\lambda_k-\lambda^*\|_\infty\) and tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_+^*\) may be identified finitely, whereas exact identification of \(A^*\) requires additional separation information.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique-Multiplier Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes geometric activity from the support associated with a selected KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le 0\), and let \(x^*\) be a KKT point with nonempty multiplier set \(M(x^*)\). Define \(A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\), \(A^+=\{i:\lambda_i>0\text{ for some }\lambda\in M(x^*)\}\), and \(A^{++}=\{i:\lambda_i>0\text{ for every }\lambda\in M(x^*)\}\). Then \(A^{++}\subseteq A^+\subseteq A^*\). If multipliers are nonunique, the support \(\{i:\lambda_i>0\}\) may depend on the selected multiplier; hence convergence to one multiplier can identify its support without identifying every member of \(A^+\) or all geometrically active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With nonunique KKT multipliers, different multiplier limits may have different positive supports. Identifying one support therefore need not identify every potentially positive or geometrically active constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{++}\subseteq A^+\subseteq A^*\), while multiplier-support identification may depend on the selected element of \(M(x^*)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal fixed-primal example with representative-dependent positive support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x\) subject to \(-x\le0\) and \(-x\le0\). The unique minimizer is \(x^*=0\), and \(M(0)=\{(t,1-t):0\le t\le1\}\). The multipliers \((1,0)\), \((0,1)\), and \((1/2,1/2)\) have positive supports \(\{1\}\), \(\{2\}\), and \(\{1,2\}\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating an active inequality gives multiplier representatives with different positive supports at the same primal solution.
assumptions_latex: The duplicate inequalities remain distinct indexed constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{supp}_+(\lambda)\text{ is not constant on }M(0).

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicated-Constraint Selection Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold stability for a chosen multiplier limit and the exact boundary for representative sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda^k\to\bar\lambda\in M(x^*)\), let \(\tau_k\downarrow0\), and define \(D_k=\{i:\lambda_i^k>\tau_k\}\). If \(\max_{i:\bar\lambda_i=0}(\lambda_i^k)_+=o(\tau_k)\), then \(D_k=\operatorname{supp}_+(\bar\lambda)\) eventually. Consequently, among admissible multiplier limits, eventual thresholded support is selection-invariant exactly when \(\operatorname{supp}_+(\lambda)\) is constant on the set of admissible limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholding eventually recovers the positive support of the selected multiplier limit; classifications are invariant exactly when all admissible limits have the same positive support.
assumptions_latex: Positive errors on zero limit components are \(o(\tau_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_k=\operatorname{supp}_+(\bar\lambda)\text{ eventually}.
knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Support Stability and Selection Invariance
Multiplier-Selection Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies support stability under selection from a non-singleton KKT multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(x^*)\) be the KKT multiplier set and let a selection rule produce \(\lambda^k\to\bar\lambda\in M(x^*)\). For a threshold sequence \(\tau_k\downarrow0\), define \(D_k=\{i:\lambda_i^k>\tau_k\}\). If \(\min_{i:\bar\lambda_i>0}\bar\lambda_i>0\) and \(\|\lambda^k-\bar\lambda\|_\infty=o(1)\), then \(D_k=\operatorname{supp}_+(\bar\lambda)\) eventually whenever \(\tau_k\) is eventually smaller than half that minimum and exceeds the errors on zero components. Different limits in \(M(x^*)\) can yield different eventual sets, so identification is selection-sensitive precisely when positive supports vary over \(M(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier threshold identifies the support of its selected multiplier limit. Different limits cause different classifications exactly when their positive supports differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_k=\operatorname{supp}_+(\bar\lambda)\) eventually; this set may change with the selected \(\bar\lambda\in M(x^*)\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x:c_i(x)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\ c_i(x)\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I)\}\), let \(x^*\in\Omega\), and let \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\). Assume the active constraints are differentiable at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local geometric identification based on tangent and normal objects; it distinguishes geometric structure from a particular constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linearized tangent cone is \(T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*):=\{d:\nabla c_i(x^*)^Td=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\ \nabla c_i(x^*)^Td\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal A^*)\}\), and its polar is the linearized normal cone \(N_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*):=T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)^\circ\). A constraint-geometry identification regime declares as its target a representation-invariant local object—such as \(T_\Omega(x^*)\), \(N_\Omega(x^*)\), a minimal face, or an active manifold—and defines identification by eventual equality or convergence of estimated geometric objects to that target. Label identification is a separate, representation-dependent target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint-geometry regime identifies local feasible geometry rather than merely a list of constraint labels. Its target can be the tangent cone, normal cone, minimal face, or active manifold at the limit point. The corresponding estimator must output a geometric object of the same type and the equality or convergence notion must be stated. Different constraint lists can describe the same geometry, so geometric identification and label identification are not equivalent without additional assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(\Omega\) and target point \(x^*\) are fixed.
The chosen geometric target and topology or equality criterion are explicitly declared.
If \(T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)\) is identified with \(T_\Omega(x^*)\), an appropriate constraint qualification is separately assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A geometry-based estimator identifies the target \(G^*\) when \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\widehat G_k=G^*\), or when \(\operatorname{dist}_{\mathfrak G}(\widehat G_k,G^*)\to0\) in a declared metric on geometric objects.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a polyhedral feasible set, identifying the minimal face containing \(x^*\) in its relative interior is a representation-invariant face-identification target.
Under an exact tangent-cone constraint qualification, \(T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=T_\Omega(x^*)\).
special_cases_latex: For affine inequalities, \(T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)\) equals the feasible tangent cone.
Redundant active constraints may change \(\mathcal A^*\) without changing the tangent cone or minimal face.
immediate_consequences_latex: Geometric identification can remain meaningful under redundant or duplicated constraints.
Exact label recovery requires representational information beyond equality of tangent or normal cones.
boundary_notes: The polar convention must be fixed; here \(C^\circ=\{v:v^Td\le0\ \forall d\in C\}\).
Nonpolyhedral sets may lack a locally constant face structure, so an active-manifold target needs separate regularity.
review_flags: Standard cone definitions are used, but no inspected source supports the complete identification-regime formulation and listed target objects.
