knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonunique Equality Multipliers with Opposite Tangent Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth example showing that multiplier-dependent curvature conflicts are nonempty when constraint regularity fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{(x_1,x_2)} f(x)=x_1+x_2^2\) subject to \(h_1(x)=x_1=0\) and \(h_2(x)=x_1+x_2^2=0\). At \(x^*=(0,0)\), the KKT multipliers satisfy \(
u_1+
u_2=-1\), and the linearized tangent cone is \(C=\{d:d_1=0\}\). For \(m^a=(-1,0)\), \(d^T
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,m^a)d=2d_2^2>0\) for nonzero \(d\in C\). For \(m^b=(1,-2)\), the same quantity is \(-2d_2^2<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent equality gradients allow two valid multipliers to assign opposite curvature signs to the same tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,m^a)d>0>d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,m^b)d\quad\forall d\in C\setminus\{0\}.

notation.meaning: linearized tangent cone at the feasible point

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Equality Multipliers with Opposite Tangent Curvature

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflicting curvature assessments from different KKT multipliers on one geometrically fixed critical direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M(x^*)\) be the KKT multiplier set at \(x^*\), and let \(C(x^*)\) be a critical cone defined from the primal first-order geometry. For \(m=(\nu,\lambda)\in\mathcal M(x^*)\), set \(H(m)=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,m)\). A multiplier-dependent curvature conflict occurs when there exist \(m^a,m^b\in\mathcal M(x^*)\) and \(d\in C(x^*)\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(d^TH(m^a)d>0\) and \(d^TH(m^b)d\le0\). Consequently, any multiplier-independent curvature assertion must state whether its multiplier quantifier is existential, universal, or direction-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two KKT multipliers conflict when their Lagrangian Hessians give positive and nonpositive curvature on the same fixed critical direction.
assumptions_latex: The problem data are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
\(\mathcal M(x^*)\) contains at least two KKT multipliers.
\(C(x^*)\) is defined independently of the selected multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists m^a,m^b\in\mathcal M(x^*),\ d\in C(x^*)\setminus\{0\}:d^TH(m^a)d>0\ge d^TH(m^b)d.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Cone Multiplier-Dependent Curvature Conflict
Multiplier-Dependent Curvature Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflicting second-order assessments caused by nonunique KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(x^*\) has two KKT multiplier pairs \(m^a=(
u^a,\lambda^a)\) and \(m^b=(
u^b,\lambda^b)\). Let \(H_r=
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,m^r)\) and let \(C_r\) be the corresponding critical cone for \(r\in\{a,b\}\). A multiplier-dependent curvature conflict occurs when there is a nonzero common direction \(d\in C_a\cap C_b\) such that
\[d^TH_ad>0\qquad	ext{and}\qquad d^TH_bd\le0.\]
Thus the same primal point and direction pass strict curvature under one admissible multiplier but fail it under another; any multiplier-independent second-order claim must specify the required quantifier over the multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonunique multipliers conflict when their Lagrangian Hessians give positive and nonpositive curvature along the same admissible direction.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraints are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists d\in(C_a\cap C_b)\setminus\{0\}:d^TH_ad>0\ge d^TH_bd\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let c(\bar x\) be a KKT point of a twice continuously differentiable NLP with non-singleton multiplier set c(\Lambda(\bar x)\). For c(\eta=(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\), define c(H_\eta=\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\eta)\) and the corresponding critical cone c(C_\eta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional NLP with nonunique KKT multipliers; curvature is compared at the same primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplier-dependent curvature conflict occurs at c(\bar x\) if there exist multipliers c(\eta_1,\eta_2\in\Lambda(\bar x)\) and a nonzero direction c(d\in C_{\eta_1}\cap C_{\eta_2}\) such that the quadratic Lagrangian curvatures give different classifications, for example c(d^TH_{\eta_1}d>0\) while c(d^TH_{\eta_2}d\le0\). A strict sign conflict has c(d^TH_{\eta_1}d>0>d^TH_{\eta_2}d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier-dependent curvature conflict exists when two valid KKT multipliers at the same primal point assign incompatible second-order curvature to a common critical direction—positive under one multiplier and nonpositive under another.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(\exists\eta_1,\eta_2\in\Lambda(\bar x),\ \exists d\in(C_{\eta_1}\cap C_{\eta_2})\setminus\{0\}:\ d^TH_{\eta_1}d>0\ge d^TH_{\eta_2}d.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a fixed common direction c(d\), the scalar map c(\eta\mapsto d^TH_\eta d\) crosses or reaches zero on the multiplier set.
A strict conflict occurs when c(\inf_{\eta\in\Lambda_d}d^TH_\eta d<0<\sup_{\eta\in\Lambda_d}d^TH_\eta d\), where c(\Lambda_d=\{\eta\in\Lambda(\bar x):d\in C_\eta\}\).

If every active constraint is affine, c(H_\eta=\nabla^2f(\bar x)\) is independent of the multiplier, so only critical-cone dependence can remain.

Multiplier-quantified conditions using a supremum or maximum can differ from conditions imposed for every multiplier.
boundary_notes: Different curvatures on directions that are not critical for both multipliers do not satisfy this definition.
Nonuniqueness of multipliers does not by itself imply a curvature conflict.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let c(\{x_k\}\) be iterates for an inequality-constrained NLP, let c(W_k\subseteq\mathcal I\) be the algorithm's working-set estimate, and suppose c(x_k\to\bar x\). Let c(A(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\), with constraints written as c(g_i\le0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An active-set identification failure occurs if either misclassification or instability holds. Misclassification means that c(W_k\) is eventually constant, say c(W_k=W_\infty\), but c(W_\infty\ne A(\bar x)\) or differs from the intended identifiable set c(A^+(\bar\mu)\). Instability means that c(W_k\) is not eventually constant: c(\forall K\;\exists k,\ell\ge K\) with c(W_k\ne W_\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active-set failure occurs when the estimated working set either stabilizes to the wrong limiting set or continues changing arbitrarily late even though the primal iterates converge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c([\exists W_\infty\ \exists K\ \forall k\ge K:W_k=W_\infty\ne A_{\rm target}]\ \lor\ [\forall K\ \exists k,\ell\ge K:W_k\ne W_\ell].

Misclassification can be measured by a nonempty eventual symmetric difference c(W_\infty\triangle A_{\rm target}\).
special_cases_latex: Under strict complementarity and a valid local identification result, the natural target is the full active set.
With weakly active constraints, the target may be the strongly active set rather than every geometrically active inequality.
immediate_consequences_latex: The algorithm cannot permanently reduce the problem to the correct equality-constrained active manifold.
Repeated changes alter the reduced subproblem and may prevent the local fast-convergence regime from being entered.
boundary_notes: Temporary working-set changes before eventual correct identification are not failures.
The definition separates identification from primal convergence; c(x_k\to\bar x\) may still hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Chattering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite local switching of estimated active sets along a convergent iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x_k)_{k\ge0}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be iterates of an active-set method with \(x_k\to x^*\), and let \(W_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be the working set at iteration \(k\). Active-set chattering occurs at \(x^*\) when
\[\#\{k\ge0:W_{k+1}\ne W_k\}=\infty.\]
Equivalently, there are no \(K\ge0\) and no fixed set \(W\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) such that \(W_k=W\) for every \(k\ge K\). This is a failure of finite working-set identification along the convergent iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-set chattering means that the working set changes infinitely often along convergent iterates instead of becoming fixed after finitely many iterations.
assumptions_latex: \((x_k)_{k\ge0}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is an infinite sequence generated by an active-set method.
Each iteration has a working set \(W_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are no \(K\ge0\) and \(W\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) such that \(W_k=W\) for all \(k\ge K\).

notation.meaning: algorithmic working set at iteration k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear Activity Strata Need Not Be Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry boundary for extending face terminology to general nonlinear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:x_1^2+x_2^2\le 1\}\) and \(g(x)=x_1^2+x_2^2-1\). The active-pattern stratum \(S=\{x\in F:g(x)=0\}\) is the unit circle. Since \(S\) is not convex, it is not a face of the convex set \(F\). Thus alternating active-index patterns for general nonlinear inequalities describes movement between activity strata, not necessarily movement between convex-geometric faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit circle is the active stratum of the unit-disk inequality but is not a face, so nonlinear activity patterns cannot generally be called faces.
assumptions_latex: Every face of a convex set is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\{x:x_1^2+x_2^2=1\}\text{ is not a face of }F.\)

notation.meaning: stratum where the nonlinear inequality is active

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Activity Strata Need Not Be Faces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite bidirectional movement between two distinct minimal polyhedral faces near a common limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polyhedron, and let \(M(x)\) denote the unique face of \(P\) whose relative interior contains \(x\). A feasible sequence \(x_k\to x^*\) zigzags between two distinct faces \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) when both transition sets are infinite:
\[\#\{k:M(x_k)=F_1,\ M(x_{k+1})=F_2\}=\infty,\qquad \#\{k:M(x_k)=F_2,\ M(x_{k+1})=F_1\}=\infty.\]
Consequently, the minimal-face sequence is not eventually constant. This geometric property concerns the faces containing the primal iterates and need not coincide with switching of an algorithmic working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedron, zigzagging between faces means that the minimal faces containing consecutive feasible iterates make infinitely many transitions in both directions between two distinct faces.
assumptions_latex: \(M(x)\) is the unique face whose relative interior contains \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(x_k)\text{ has infinitely many }F_1\to F_2\text{ and }F_2\to F_1\text{ transitions and is not eventually constant.}\)

notation.meaning: unique minimal face whose relative interior contains x
two distinct polyhedral faces visited in alternating transitions

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Face Zigzagging
Zigzagging between Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternation between distinct constraint faces near a common limit point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the feasible set be \(F=\{x:g(x)\le0\}\), and associate with an index set \(J\) the relative face
\[F_J=\{x\in F:g_i(x)=0\ \text{for}\ i\in J,\ g_i(x)<0\ \text{for}\ i\notin J\}.\]
A feasible sequence \(x_k\to x^*\) zigzags between faces if there exist distinct sets \(J_1,J_2\) and infinitely many indices \(k\) such that \(x_k\in F_{J_1}\) and \(x_{k+1}\in F_{J_2}\), with the reverse transition also occurring infinitely often. The sequence therefore approaches \(x^*\) without remaining on one locally identified face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zigzagging occurs when convergent feasible iterates alternate infinitely often between two distinct active-constraint faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\) makes infinitely many transitions in both directions between \(F_{J_1}\) and \(F_{J_2}\).

notation.meaning: relative face determined by active index set J

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of eventual active-set identification in inequality-constrained methods, with face-switching and possible convergence deterioration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A^*\) be the active set at a local solution and \(\mathcal A^{(k)}\) the active set at iterate \(x^{(k)}\). Zigzagging occurs when the sets \(\mathcal A^{(k)}\) do not settle to \(\mathcal A^*\), but instead oscillate among different constraint subsets. For linear constraints this corresponds to movement among different faces or linear manifolds of the feasible region. If \(\mathcal A^{(k)}=\mathcal A^*\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), the convergence order becomes that of the corresponding equality-constrained method, usually superlinear for good methods. With zigzagging, the order may degenerate to linear with a rate constant that is not small, and convergence may fail in some cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zigzagging is persistent oscillation of the iterate active sets instead of eventual identification of the solution active set. For linear constraints it appears as switching among feasible faces. Identification recovers the equality-constrained local convergence regime, whereas zigzagging can cause slow linear convergence or failure to converge.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) is a local solution with active set \(\mathcal A^*\).
The method generates iterates \(x^{(k)}\) with active sets \(\mathcal A^{(k)}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Zigzagging means }\neg\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\mathcal A^{(k)}=\mathcal A^*;\text{ it may degrade or prevent convergence.}

children.title: Premature Constraint Release
children.top_down_role: Cases where a constraint leaves the working set before its active role is reliably resolved.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Premature Release Relative to an Identification Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Release that contradicts an explicitly stated local retention or identification guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J^*\) be the set of constraints that an identification result requires every sufficiently late working set to retain: under hypotheses \(H\), there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) and \(K\) such that \(x_k\in U\) and \(k\ge K\) imply \(J^*\subseteq W_k\). A transition releasing \(j\), with \(j\in W_k\setminus W_{k+1}\), is premature relative to this regime when \(H\) holds, \(x_k,x_{k+1}\in U\), \(k\ge K\), and \(j\in J^*\). Immediate readmission, constraint violation, and membership of \(j\) in the full active set \(I(x^*)\) are not necessary parts of this definition. Without a specified target set and retention regime, a release cannot be classified as premature merely because the constraint is active at the limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A release is premature only relative to a stated local identification guarantee: it removes a constraint that the guarantee requires late working sets to retain. Immediate readmission or infeasibility is unnecessary, while activity at the limit alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: Under hypotheses \(H\), \(x_k\in U\) and \(k\ge K\) imply \(J^*\subseteq W_k\).
\(j\in W_k\setminus W_{k+1}\), \(j\in J^*\), \(x_k,x_{k+1}\in U\), and \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The release of }j\text{ contradicts the stated local retention guarantee.}\)

notation.meaning: constraint set that the applicable identification result requires late working sets to retain
neighborhood in which the local retention guarantee applies
hypotheses of the applicable identification or retention result

knowledge_statements.title: Premature Release Relative to an Identification Regime
Premature Constraint Release
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Release of a truly active constraint before its local activity is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_k\to x^*\), let \(W_k\) be the working set, and suppose \(j\in I(x^*)\). A release of constraint \(j\) at iteration \(k\), meaning \(j\in W_k\) but \(j\notin W_{k+1}\), is premature if the accepted step does not establish local inactivity and the constraint must immediately be restored:
\[g_j(x_{k+1})=0\quad\text{and}\quad j\in W_{k+2}.\]
A more severe premature release produces \(g_j(x_{k+1})>0\), so the accepted point violates feasibility. Repeated premature releases prevent finite identification of the limiting active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is released prematurely when it is active at the limit and must promptly be restored, or its release causes violation.
assumptions_latex: \(W_k\) is the working set and \(j\in W_k\setminus W_{k+1}\).

notation.meaning: true active set at the limit point

children.title: Persistent False Activity
children.top_down_role: Cases where an inactive constraint remains incorrectly retained.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent False Activity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual retention of a constraint that is inactive at the limiting solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_k\to x^*\) be iterates with working sets \(W_k\). Constraint \(j\) exhibits persistent false activity when it is strictly inactive at the limit but is retained indefinitely by the algorithm:
\[g_j(x^*)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad \exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ j\in W_k.\]
Because continuity gives \(g_j(x_k)<0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), the working-set membership does not represent actual activity. If the algorithm imposes the working constraint as an equality in its subproblem, the false membership may unnecessarily restrict steps and distort multiplier estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent false activity means an inequality strictly inactive at the limit remains in every sufficiently late working set.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration has a working set \(W_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_j(x^*)<0\) and \(j\in W_k\) eventually.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing-Slack Threshold Excludes Persistent False Activity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exclusion of false retention for a strictly inactive limiting constraint under a consistent slack test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_j(x^*)<0\), \(x_k\to x^*\), and \(\tau_k\to0\). Suppose \(j\in W_k\) only if \(-g_j(x_k)\le\tau_k\). Continuity gives \(\delta>0\) such that \(-g_j(x_k)\ge\delta\) for every sufficiently large \(k\), while eventually \(\tau_k<\delta\). Hence \(j\notin W_k\) for every sufficiently large \(k\), so persistent false activity is impossible under this rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous constraint with positive limiting slack cannot remain selected by a slack threshold tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ j\notin W_k.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Slack Threshold Excludes Persistent False Activity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp exclusion of false retention for a strictly inactive limiting constraint under a consistent slack test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_j(x^*)<0\), \(x_k\to x^*\), and let \(\tau_k\downarrow0\). Suppose membership requires \(-g_j(x_k)\le\tau_k\). By continuity, there exist \(\delta>0\) and \(K_1\) such that \(-g_j(x_k)\ge\delta\) for all \(k\ge K_1\); since \(\tau_k\to0\), eventually \(\tau_k<\delta\). Hence \(j\notin W_k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), so persistent false activity is impossible under this rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous constraint with positive limiting slack cannot remain selected by a slack threshold that tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ j\notin W_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Slack-Threshold Excludes Persistent False Activity

children.title: Release–Readmission Oscillation
children.top_down_role: Repeated transitions caused by unstable activity classification near a working-set boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Release–Readmission Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite toggling of one constraint's working-set membership near a limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_k\to x^*\) and let \(W_k\) be the working set. Constraint \(j\) undergoes release–readmission oscillation when both transition sets are infinite:
\[\#\{k:j\in W_k,\ j\notin W_{k+1}\}=\infty,\qquad
\#\{k:j\notin W_k,\ j\in W_{k+1}\}=\infty.\]
Thus the binary membership sequence \(\mathbf 1_{\{j\in W_k\}}\) is not eventually constant and contains infinitely many changes in each direction. This is a constraint-specific form of active-set chattering and constitutes failure of finite classification of constraint \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Release–readmission oscillation means one constraint is removed and subsequently restored infinitely many times along a convergent iteration.
assumptions_latex: \((x_k)\) is an infinite sequence with \(x_k\to x^*\).
Each iteration has a working set \(W_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf 1_{\{j\in W_k\}}\) has infinitely many \(1\to0\) and \(0\to1\) transitions.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For c(m\) inequality constraints, a working set is any subset c(W\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Hence the unrestricted working-set state space is c(\mathfrak W=2^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}\) with c(|\mathfrak W|=2^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite working-set search processes for constrained optimization; the definition concerns discrete complexity rather than curvature or numerical error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A working-set procedure exhibits combinatorial failure on a problem family if its accepted or examined working sets cannot be confined to a subexponential family: there exist c(\alpha>0\) and instances with c(m\to\infty\) for which the number c(N_m\) of distinct working sets examined before termination satisfies c(N_m\ge2^{\alpha m}\). On a fixed instance, a nonterminating combinatorial failure also occurs when the procedure revisits working-set states indefinitely without reaching an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working-set method has a combinatorial failure when it must examine exponentially many distinct subsets of the inequality indices on a growing problem family, or when repeated working-set states cause nontermination on a fixed instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c([\exists\alpha>0\ \exists m_j\to\infty:N_{m_j}\ge2^{\alpha m_j}]\ \lor\ [\text{working-set states recur indefinitely without termination}].
equivalent_formulations_latex: Unrestricted enumeration has worst-case state count c(2^m\).
A deterministic recurrence of the complete algorithmic state is the cycling specialization of fixed-instance combinatorial failure.
special_cases_latex: Testing every candidate working set has c(N_m=2^m\).
Adding or dropping only one index per iteration traverses edges of the c(m\)-dimensional Boolean hypercube but does not alone preclude exponential paths.
immediate_consequences_latex: The discrete identification effort can dominate the continuous reduced-subproblem solves.
Local progress rules that do not impose an acyclic ordering may revisit previous subsets.
boundary_notes: A large polynomial number of working sets is not exponential failure under this definition.
The existence of c(2^m\) possible sets alone is combinatorial difficulty; failure additionally requires exponential exploration or recurrence.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-state cycling in a deterministic active-set method, distinct from merely slow progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an active-set algorithm generate states \(s_k=(x_k,W_k,\eta_k)\), where \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(W_k\) is the working set, and \(\eta_k\) contains all additional data used by its deterministic transition rule. The run cycles if there exist integers \(p<q\) such that \(s_p=s_q\), neither state satisfies the algorithm's termination test, and every transition from a given state is uniquely determined. Consequently, \(s_{p+j}=s_{q+j}\) for every integer \(j\geq 0\), so the algorithm follows a nonterminating periodic orbit and cannot reach a state outside that orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycling occurs when a deterministic active-set algorithm revisits the same complete nonterminal state, forcing all subsequent states to repeat periodically.
assumptions_latex: The transition rule is deterministic and depends only on \(s_k\).
Equality of states includes every variable affecting tie-breaking or constraint selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The repeated state generates a nonterminating periodic orbit.

notation.meaning: additional algorithmic state and tie-breaking data

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Working-Set Recurrence Is Not Complete-State Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that recurrence of a working-set component does not certify cycling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k=1/(k+1)\), and let \(W_k=\{1\}\) for even \(k\) and \(W_k=\{2\}\) for odd \(k\). Each working set recurs infinitely often and \(W_k\) changes at every iteration, but the complete states \(s_k=(x_k,W_k)\) are pairwise distinct because \(x_k\) is strictly decreasing. Thus componentwise working-set chattering does not imply complete-state cycling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating working sets do not prove cycling when another transition-relevant state component changes and no complete state repeats.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall p<q,\ s_p\ne s_q,\quad\text{although }W_k\text{ changes infinitely often}.\)

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let c(s_k\) denote the complete state of a deterministic active-set method, including the primal iterate, working set or basis, and any tie-breaking data that affect the next update. Write the update as c(s_{k+1}=T(s_k)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The method cycles if there exist c(k_0\ge0\) and a period c(p\ge1\) such that c(s_{k_0+p}=s_{k_0}\), none of c(s_{k_0},\ldots,s_{k_0+p-1}\) is a terminating state, and the deterministic rule therefore gives c(s_{k+p}=s_k\) for every c(k\ge k_0\). In simplex terminology, this commonly follows a sequence of degenerate steps that returns to an earlier basis without objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycling occurs when a deterministic method returns to exactly the same nonterminal algorithmic state after finitely many updates; it then repeats the same states forever and does not terminate.

Any state-dependent scalar quantity is periodic along the cycle; in degenerate simplex cycling the primal point and objective may remain unchanged.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Stalling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic failure boundary for active-set runs whose combinatorial transitions do not produce primal progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an active-set sequence \((x_k,W_k)\) for a constrained problem with a termination predicate \(T(x_k,W_k)\). Working-set stalling occurs if there exist an index \(K\) and a point \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \(x_k=\bar x\) for every integer \(k\geq K\), while \(T(\bar x,W_k)\) is false and the method continues adding, deleting, or reconsidering constraints. Thus continued working-set activity alone does not constitute progress when it produces neither an accepted primal displacement nor a terminal certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active-set method stalls when it keeps changing or reconsidering constraints while the primal point remains fixed and no termination certificate is obtained.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm records accepted primal iterates \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and working sets \(W_k\).
The termination predicate distinguishes a certified terminal state from an unresolved state.
The stalling condition is stated in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run makes no primal progress despite continued working-set transitions.

notation.meaning: fixed primal point at which the run stalls

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Deterministic Stalling Implies Eventual Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial consequence of indefinite stalling when all transition-relevant discrete state is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x_k=\bar x\) for every \(k\ge K\), no state reached after \(K\) is terminal, and the complete state has the form \(s_k=(\bar x,\eta_k)\), where \(\eta_k\) belongs to a finite set \(E\) and \(s_{k+1}=T(s_k)\) is deterministic. Then there exist \(K\le p<q\) with \(s_p=s_q\). Consequently, \(s_{p+j}=s_{q+j}\) for every \(j\ge0\), so the stalled run is eventually periodic and cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinitely stalled deterministic run with finitely many complete discrete states must eventually cycle.
assumptions_latex: No state reached after \(K\) satisfies the termination test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists p<q\text{ such that }s_p=s_q,\quad\text{and the run is eventually periodic}.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Length Working-Set Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate active-set transition that changes the working set at a fixed feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be feasible, let \(d_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be a trial direction, and suppose the accepted update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k\) with \(\alpha_k\geq 0\). A zero-length working-set change is a transition for which \(\alpha_k=0\) and \(W_{k+1}\neq W_k\). Such a transition changes the combinatorial state while satisfying \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Repeated zero-length changes can therefore contribute to working-set stalling or cycling, although a single such change does not by itself imply either failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-length working-set change alters the working set with an accepted step length of zero, leaving the primal iterate unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The accepted update has the form \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k\).
Working sets are explicitly updated after step selection or multiplier inspection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\alpha_k=0\) and \(W_{k+1}\neq W_k\), then \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) despite a combinatorial transition.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Transition Events
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguous or zero-displacement working-set transitions caused by simultaneous blocking or degenerate multiplier information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an active-set state \((x,W)\), a degenerate transition event occurs when either the prescribed add-or-delete rule has more than one equally admissible outcome or an admissible working-set change has zero primal displacement. The first case can arise when distinct inactive constraints attain the same minimum blocking step or when distinct active inequalities tie under the method's deletion criterion; the second includes an accepted update with \(x_{+}=x\) and \(W_{+}\neq W\). If the first case occurs and no deterministic tie-breaking rule is specified, the next working set is not uniquely determined by the current state and first-order data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate transition event is either an ambiguous working-set update, such as a tie among blockers or deletion candidates, or an admissible working-set change with zero primal displacement.
assumptions_latex: The active-set rule adds blocking constraints or deletes active inequalities using a stated multiplier criterion.
Ties are interpreted in exact arithmetic; a finite-precision implementation requires an explicit tolerance and tie convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A tied transition is nonunique without tie-breaking, while a zero-displacement transition changes the working set without moving the primal point.

notation.meaning: accepted primal point after the transition

knowledge_statements.title: Anti-Cycling Safeguard Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial safeguards for deterministic active-set transitions; no claim of global NLP convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active-set method, an anti-cycling safeguard may augment ambiguous add-or-delete transitions with an ordering device, such as lexicographic pivoting, a fixed priority rule, or symbolic perturbation. To exclude an infinite sequence of zero-displacement transitions, the safeguard must provide a signature \(\phi(W,\eta)\) in a set equipped with a well-founded strict order \(\prec\) such that every zero-displacement transition satisfies \(\phi(W_{k+1},\eta_{k+1})\prec\phi(W_k,\eta_k)\). No infinite strictly descending chain, and hence no recurrence of a complete zero-displacement state, is then possible. This principle excludes combinatorial cycling in the covered transitions but does not by itself guarantee descent, feasibility restoration, or convergence of the underlying nonlinear iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anti-cycling rule excludes an infinite sequence of zero-displacement working-set changes when every such change strictly decreases a signature in a well-founded order.
assumptions_latex: The signature \(\phi(W,\eta)\) is defined for every augmented discrete state covered by the safeguard.
Every covered zero-displacement transition strictly decreases the signature under the well-founded order \(\prec\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No infinite sequence of covered zero-displacement transitions and no recurrence of a covered augmented state are possible.

notation.meaning: ranking signature for augmented working-set states
well-founded strict order used by the ranking argument

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent priority encodings for resolving covered degenerate active-set transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every ambiguous transition has finitely many eligible updates, each assigned a fixed-length comparison vector \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_r)\). A lexicographic safeguard selects an eligible update with lexicographically minimal vector. The same hierarchy can be encoded formally by comparing \(\sum_{i=1}^r v_i\varepsilon^{i-1}\) for a positive infinitesimal \(\varepsilon\). If every covered zero-displacement update strictly decreases the resulting signature and only finitely many signatures are attainable, the covered degenerate-transition phase terminates after finitely many updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic comparison and hierarchical symbolic perturbation encode the same priority ordering; strict decrease over finitely many signatures terminates the covered degenerate phase.
assumptions_latex: Each ambiguous transition has finitely many eligible updates.
Comparison vectors have fixed finite dimension and a fixed component ordering.
Every covered zero-displacement update strictly decreases the signature.
Only finitely many signatures are attainable during the covered phase.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The covered zero-displacement phase contains finitely many transitions.}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deterministic Tie-Breaking Alone Does Not Prevent Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between uniquely resolving a transition and proving an anti-cycling property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic priority rule need not be anti-cycling. On two distinct nonterminal states \(a,b\), the deterministic transition map \(T(a)=b\) and \(T(b)=a\) uniquely resolves every successor but produces the periodic orbit \(a,b,a,b,\ldots\). Thus determinism alone is insufficient; absence of cycling requires a strictly monotone ranking, a no-revisit invariant, or another structural argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed deterministic choice removes ambiguity but does not by itself prevent a periodic cycle.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a deterministic transition map on nonterminal states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Determinism does not imply absence of cycling.}\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite combinatorial working-set or basis methods; a safeguard may be a tie-breaking, perturbation, or state-memory rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An anti-cycling safeguard is a rule selecting c(T_{\rm ac}(s)\in\mathcal T(s)\) such that no generated nonterminal trajectory contains a repeated complete state. A family c(\{T_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\) is anti-cycling if every admissible parameter c(\theta\) has this property. A standard sufficient form is the existence of a strict order or potential c(\Phi\) for which every safeguarded degenerate transition satisfies c(\Phi(T_\theta(s))\prec\Phi(s)\); on a finite state space this excludes cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anti-cycling safeguard resolves otherwise ambiguous working-set transitions so that no nonterminal complete state can recur. A safeguard family has this property for each admissible choice of its parameter or ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(\forall\theta\in\Theta\ \forall\text{ generated nonterminal trajectories }\{s_k\}:\ k\ne\ell\Rightarrow s_k\ne s_\ell.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical Reliability Failure in KKT and Activity Computations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let c(D\) denote exact problem data and c(\widehat y\) a floating-point output representing a step, multiplier, rank decision, or activity classification. Let c(F(D,y)=0\) denote the exact defining equations and let c(u\) be unit roundoff.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision constrained optimization; the definition covers inaccurate solves and unstable discrete classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A numerical reliability failure occurs if either backward reliability or decision stability fails. Backward reliability fails when no perturbation c(\Delta D\) within the prescribed relative tolerance c(\tau\) makes the computed output exact: c(\nexists\Delta D\) with c(\|\Delta D\|\le\tau\|D\|\) and c(F(D+\Delta D,\widehat y)=0\). Decision stability fails when two admissible perturbations c(\Delta D_1,\Delta D_2\) of that size produce different exact rank, sign, or activity decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained computation is numerically unreliable when its result cannot be interpreted as the exact result for nearby data of the allowed size, or when admissibly small data perturbations change the rank, multiplier-sign, or activity decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c([\nexists\Delta D:\|\Delta D\|\le\tau\|D\|,\ F(D+\Delta D,\widehat y)=0]\ \lor\ [\exists\Delta D_1,\Delta D_2:\operatorname{dec}(D+\Delta D_1)\ne\operatorname{dec}(D+\Delta D_2)]).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a linear solve c(Ky=b\), normwise backward failure is a residual c(r=b-K\widehat y\) too large to be explained by allowed perturbations of c(K\) and c(b\).
A rank or activity decision is unreliable when the distance of the data to the corresponding decision boundary is no larger than the admitted perturbation scale.
special_cases_latex: A computed negative pivot caused only by roundoff in a theoretically semidefinite factorization is a reliability failure.
A multiplier whose magnitude is comparable to its error bound has an unreliable sign classification.
immediate_consequences_latex: The computed active set or KKT step lacks a certified nearby exact interpretation.
Repeating the computation under scaling or an equivalent formulation may change the reported discrete outcome.
boundary_notes: A forward error may be large while backward reliability still holds for an ill-conditioned problem.
This definition requires a stated norm and tolerance; exact mathematical degeneracy is a separate issue.

notation.meaning: Discrete rank, sign, or activity decision.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity boundary for equality-constrained or fixed-working-set Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed working set, let the computed step and multiplier solve the KKT system \(Kz=b\), where \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\). If \(K\) is nonsingular and the right-hand side is perturbed by \(r\), then the solution perturbation is \(\Delta z=K^{-1}r\) and satisfies \(\|\Delta z\|_2\leq\|r\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(K)\). Hence a small \(\sigma_{\min}(K)\), equivalently a large condition number when \(\|K\|_2\) is controlled, can strongly amplify residuals and roundoff, making steps and multipliers numerically unreliable even when the linear residual is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearly singular KKT matrix amplifies right-hand-side errors and roundoff, so computed steps and multipliers may be unreliable despite a small residual.
assumptions_latex: Sensitivity is measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The error amplification factor is at most \(1/\sigma_{\min}(K)\) for right-hand-side perturbations.

notation.meaning: Hessian or Hessian approximation on the current subproblem
smallest singular value of the KKT matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Kz=b\) and \((K+E)(z+\Delta z)=b+r\), where \(K\) is nonsingular. If \(\|K^{-1}E\|_2<1\), then \(K+E\) is nonsingular and \[\|\Delta z\|_2\leq \frac{\|K^{-1}\|_2}{1-\|K^{-1}E\|_2}\left(\|r\|_2+\|E\|_2\|z\|_2\right).\] Thus perturbations of the Hessian, active Jacobian, or residual can produce large primal-dual errors when \(K\) is ill-conditioned; the guarantee disappears as \(\|K^{-1}E\|_2\) approaches one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ill-conditioned KKT matrix amplifies both right-hand-side errors and perturbations of its Hessian or Jacobian blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Coefficient-Perturbation Amplification

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the saddle-point system c(Kz=b\) with c(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), where c(H\) is a Lagrangian or quadratic-model Hessian and c(A\) is the Jacobian of equality or working-set constraints. Let c(\|\cdot\|\) be a subordinate matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingular finite-dimensional KKT matrices; singular systems are treated as the limiting failure case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular c(K\), its normwise condition number is c(\kappa(K)=\|K\|\,\|K^{-1}\|\). Relative to a specified threshold c(\kappa_{\max}\), the KKT system is ill-conditioned when c(\kappa(K)\ge\kappa_{\max}\). In floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff c(u\), the practically critical regime is c(\kappa(K)u\not\ll1\), because small relative perturbations or backward errors may then be amplified into large relative solution errors. A singular KKT matrix has c(\kappa(K)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular KKT system is ill-conditioned when the product of the norm of its matrix and inverse exceeds a declared threshold. Numerically, danger arises when its condition number times unit roundoff is not small; a singular KKT matrix has infinite condition number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(\kappa(K)=\|K\|\|K^{-1}\|\ge\kappa_{\max},\quad\text{with critical finite-precision regime }\kappa(K)u\not\ll1.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the spectral norm for symmetric nonsingular c(K\), c(\kappa_2(K)=\sigma_{\max}(K)/\sigma_{\min}(K)\).
Ill-conditioning is proximity to singularity after the selected scaling and norm are fixed.
special_cases_latex: If c(A\) loses row rank or the reduced Hessian loses positive definiteness, the standard KKT nonsingularity conditions fail.
Primal-dual interior-point KKT systems can become ill-conditioned as some diagonal complementarity weights diverge while others approach zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small residual does not alone guarantee a small forward error in the computed primal-dual step.
Scaling, stable symmetric-indefinite factorization, or regularization may be needed to obtain reliable steps.
boundary_notes: Every KKT matrix with at least one constraint is indefinite; indefiniteness alone is not ill-conditioning.
Condition numbers depend on variable scaling, the chosen norm, and the formulation of the KKT equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Numerical Rank Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-rank decisions near the singular-value cutoff are not robust to scaling or perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let numerical rank be declared by \(r_\tau(A)=\#\{j:\sigma_j(A)>\tau\}\) for a fixed absolute threshold \(\tau\) satisfying \(0<\tau<1\). For \(A_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\) with \(0<\varepsilon\leq\tau\), this rule returns rank one although \(A_\varepsilon\) has exact rank two. After the positive row rescaling \(D=\operatorname{diag}(1,c)\), it returns rank two whenever \(c\varepsilon>\tau\). More generally, if a singular value lies near the threshold, sufficiently small data perturbations or changes in constraint scaling can change the declared rank and thereby alter working-set independence decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a singular value is near a fixed absolute cutoff, perturbations or equivalent constraint rescaling can change the declared numerical rank and active-set independence decisions.
assumptions_latex: Numerical rank uses a fixed absolute singular-value threshold \(\tau\) with \(0<\tau<1\).
Positive row scaling represents an equivalent rescaling of constraint equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The declared numerical rank is not invariant under equivalent positive row scaling near the threshold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unstable Numerical Rank Decision at a Prescribed Tolerance
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(q=\min\{m,n\}\), and write its singular values as \(\sigma_1(A)\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_q(A)\geq0\). Fix an absolute rank threshold \(\tau\geq0\), a spectral-norm uncertainty radius \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and the admissible perturbation set \(\mathcal U_\varepsilon(A)=\{A+E:\|E\|_2\leq\varepsilon\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional numerical rank classification under norm-bounded matrix perturbations. The definition concerns the reliability of a threshold decision, not the exact algebraic rank of an unperturbed matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The threshold numerical rank of \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is \[r_\tau(B)=\#\{j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}:\sigma_j(B)>\tau\}.\] The numerical rank decision for \(A\) is \((\tau,\varepsilon)\)-unstable when it is not constant on the uncertainty set, namely when \[\bigl|\{r_\tau(B):B\in\mathcal U_\varepsilon(A)\}\bigr|>1.\] Equivalently, there exist perturbations \(E_1,E_2\) satisfying \(\|E_1\|_2,\|E_2\|_2\leq\varepsilon\) for which \(r_\tau(A+E_1)\neq r_\tau(A+E_2)\). Its instability radius is \[\rho_\tau(A)=\inf\{\|E\|_2:r_\tau(A+E)\neq r_\tau(A)\},\] with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). Thus the decision is unstable whenever \(\rho_\tau(A)\leq\varepsilon\) and an admissible perturbation realizes a different rank; it is stable when every admissible perturbation preserves \(r_\tau(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a real matrix, count as numerically nonzero exactly those singular values strictly larger than a prescribed threshold. The resulting numerical-rank decision is unstable at perturbation level \(\varepsilon\) if two matrices within spectral-norm distance \(\varepsilon\) of the reported matrix can receive different threshold ranks. The instability radius is the smallest spectral-norm perturbation that changes this rank classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) has an unstable numerical rank decision at \((\tau,\varepsilon)\) exactly when the map \(B\mapsto r_\tau(B)\) is nonconstant on \(\mathcal U_\varepsilon(A)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\exists E_1,E_2\) with \(\|E_1\|_2,\|E_2\|_2\leq\varepsilon\) such that \(r_\tau(A+E_1)\neq r_\tau(A+E_2)\).
Defining \(\mathcal R_{\tau,\varepsilon}(A)=\{r_\tau(A+E):\|E\|_2\leq\varepsilon\}\), instability is the condition \(|\mathcal R_{\tau,\varepsilon}(A)|\geq2\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\tau=0\), \(r_0(A)\) is the exact algebraic rank, but its numerical reliability still depends on the allowed perturbations.
A relative threshold can be represented by replacing \(\tau\) with \(\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\sigma_1(B)\); this is a distinct, scale-relative decision rule.
immediate_consequences_latex: Since \(|\sigma_j(A+E)-\sigma_j(A)|\leq\|E\|_2\), the sufficient separation condition \(\min_j|\sigma_j(A)-\tau|>\varepsilon\) makes the threshold rank invariant throughout \(\mathcal U_\varepsilon(A)\).

When a working-set Jacobian has singular values near \(\tau\), admissible numerical errors may cause different constraints to be classified as linearly independent, changing the working-set dimension.
boundary_notes: This definition does not prescribe how \(\tau\) or \(\varepsilon\) should be selected.
Ill-conditioning and rank-decision instability are related but not identical: a matrix may be ill-conditioned while a particular threshold decision remains stable.
The strict comparison \(\sigma_j(B)>\tau\) is part of the convention; using \(\geq\) changes behavior at the threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Sensitive Activity Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of absolute residual tests under equivalent positive rescaling of inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an inequality is written as \(g_i(x)\leq0\) and declared numerically active when \(|g_i(x)|\leq\tau\), with a fixed absolute tolerance \(\tau>0\). Replacing it by the equivalent constraint \(\widetilde g_i(x)=s_i g_i(x)\leq0\), where \(s_i>0\), changes the test to \(s_i|g_i(x)|\leq\tau\). Thus any point with \(0<|g_i(x)|<\tau\) can be classified inactive after choosing \(s_i>\tau/|g_i(x)|\), while a point failing the original test can be classified active by sufficiently small \(s_i\). Absolute activity tests are therefore not representation invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed absolute constraint-residual tolerance can label the same point differently after positive rescaling of an equivalent inequality.
assumptions_latex: Equivalent constraint representations may use arbitrary positive scale factors \(s_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The activity classification is not invariant under positive constraint scaling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-invariant residual activity classification under positive constraint rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inequality \(g_i(x)\leq0\), let \(q_i(x)>0\) be a residual scale and declare \(i\) estimated active when \(|g_i(x)|/q_i(x)\leq\tau\). If replacing \(g_i\) by \(\widetilde g_i=s_i g_i\), \(s_i>0\), also replaces \(q_i\) by \(\widetilde q_i=s_iq_i\), then \[\frac{|\widetilde g_i(x)|}{\widetilde q_i(x)}=\frac{|g_i(x)|}{q_i(x)},\] so the activity decision is invariant under positive rescaling. Without an invariant normalized ratio, no general representation-invariance guarantee follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual activity test is invariant under positive constraint scaling when its normalization transforms by the same factor as the constraint.
assumptions_latex: Under \(\widetilde g_i=s_i g_i\), the scale satisfies \(\widetilde q_i=s_iq_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widetilde g_i(x)|/\widetilde q_i(x)=|g_i(x)|/q_i(x)\), so the classification is representation invariant.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Covariant Activity Tolerances

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider constraints \(c_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), indexed by \(i\in\mathcal I\), and a point \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Let \(\tau_i>0\) be absolute residual tolerances. For positive scale factors \(\omega_i>0\), the equivalent constraint representation is \(\widetilde c_i=\omega_i c_i\); its exact zero set is identical to that of \(c_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality constraints and inequality constraints tested for proximity to their active boundary. The definition addresses absolute residual tests and positive rescalings of individual constraint functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The absolute-tolerance activity test is \[\mathcal A_\tau(x;c)=\{i\in\mathcal I:|c_i(x)|\leq\tau_i\}.\] It is scaling-sensitive at \(x\) over a class \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R_{++}^{|\mathcal I|}\) of admissible positive scalings if there exists \(\omega\in\Omega\) such that \[\mathcal A_\tau(x;c)\neq\mathcal A_\tau(x;\operatorname{diag}(\omega)c).\] Componentwise, sensitivity occurs exactly when some \(i\) and admissible \(\omega_i\) make the truth values of \(|c_i(x)|\leq\tau_i\) and \(\omega_i|c_i(x)|\leq\tau_i\) differ. A family of activity tests is scaling-equivariant when the tolerances transform with the residuals: \[\widetilde\tau_i=\omega_i\tau_i,\qquad \mathcal A_{\widetilde\tau}(x;\operatorname{diag}(\omega)c)=\mathcal A_\tau(x;c)\quad\text{for every }x\text{ and }\omega>0.\] Consequently, an absolute activity test that leaves \(\tau_i\) fixed under arbitrary positive rescaling is scaling-sensitive at every point having \(0<|c_i(x)|<\infty\) for at least one tested constraint, because a scale factor can move that residual across the fixed threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absolute numerical activity test declares constraint \(i\) active when the magnitude of its residual does not exceed \(\tau_i\). The test is scaling-sensitive if multiplying an equivalent constraint by a positive constant, while leaving its tolerance fixed, can change the declared active set. It is scaling-equivariant if each tolerance is multiplied by the same factor as its constraint, which preserves every activity decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling sensitivity is the existence of \(x\), an admissible positive scaling \(\omega\), and an index \(i\) for which the activity classifications of \(c_i\) and \(\omega_i c_i\) differ despite their identical exact active boundaries.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a fixed \(x\), sensitivity is equivalent to the existence of \(i\) and \(\omega_i>0\) such that exactly one of \(|c_i(x)|\leq\tau_i\) and \(|c_i(x)|\leq\tau_i/\omega_i\) holds.
A test is invariant under all positive diagonal constraint scalings precisely when its decision depends on a dimensionless residual or its residual tolerance is transformed covariantly.
special_cases_latex: For an inequality written as \(c_i(x)\geq0\), a one-sided test may use \(c_i(x)\leq\tau_i\); the same scaling criterion applies after replacing \(|c_i(x)|\) by the chosen one-sided residual.
Normalizing by a positive scale \(s_i\) gives the dimensionless rule \(|c_i(x)|/s_i\leq\widehat\tau_i\), which is invariant when both \(c_i\) and \(s_i\) are multiplied by \(\omega_i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: With a fixed common tolerance \(\tau\), two algebraically equivalent formulations can produce different numerical working sets.
If \(\widetilde\tau_i=\omega_i\tau_i\), positive rescaling alone cannot change the activity classification.
For nonlinear constraints, attainable residual accuracies may differ by constraint, so a single unscaled absolute threshold need not represent comparable numerical proximity to each boundary.
boundary_notes: Exact activity, defined by \(c_i(x)=0\), is invariant under every nonzero scaling and is not the failure described here.
Only positive scaling is included, so an inequality's orientation is preserved.
Variable scaling and objective scaling can also alter numerical behavior, but they are outside this definition unless they change the tested constraint residuals or their tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Multiplier Estimates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-sign decisions become unreliable when stationarity data are noisy or the active Jacobian is ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(g,e\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and define the unperturbed and perturbed multiplier estimates by \(\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mu\in\mathbb{R}^m}\|A^{\mathsf T}\mu+g\|_2\) and \(\widehat\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mu\in\mathbb{R}^m}\|A^{\mathsf T}\mu+g-e\|_2\), respectively. Then \(\widehat\lambda-\lambda=(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}Ae\) and \(\|\widehat\lambda-\lambda\|_2\leq\|e\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(A)\). Consequently, this bound alone cannot certify the sign of component \(\lambda_i\) when \(|\widehat\lambda_i|\leq\|e\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(A)\). Near rank deficiency enlarges this ambiguity region and can make deletion decisions based on small multiplier estimates unstable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity-data noise is amplified by a nearly rank-deficient active Jacobian, so small least-squares multiplier estimates and their signs may be unreliable for constraint-deletion decisions.
assumptions_latex: The active-constraint Jacobian \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
Both multiplier estimates are defined by the stated Euclidean least-squares problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplier-estimate error satisfies \(\|\widehat\lambda-\lambda\|_2\leq\|e\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(A)\), so component signs within this bound are not certified by it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Jacobian Sensitivity of Multiplier Estimates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order effect of active-Jacobian and gradient-data errors on a full-row-rank least-squares multiplier estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) have full row rank, let \(\lambda\) solve \(AA^{\mathsf T}\lambda=-Ag\), and put \(\rho=A^{\mathsf T}\lambda+g\). For differentiable perturbations \(A(t)=A+t\Delta A\) and \(g(t)=g+t\Delta g\) that preserve full row rank near \(t=0\), the corresponding least-squares multiplier satisfies \[\dot\lambda(0)=-(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\left(A\Delta g+\Delta A\,\rho+A\Delta A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\right).\] Hence active-Jacobian noise as well as gradient noise can become strongly amplified near rank loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier estimates are sensitive to active-Jacobian noise as well as gradient noise, and this sensitivity can diverge near rank loss.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dot\lambda(0)=-(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}(A\Delta g+\Delta A\rho+A\Delta A^{\mathsf T}\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Jacobian Sensitivity of Multiplier Estimates

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) be a full-row-rank working-set Jacobian and let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) be an objective-gradient vector. Define the nominal first-order multiplier estimate by \(\widehat\lambda(A,g)=\arg\min_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^p}\|A^T\lambda-g\|_2\). Let admissible data errors satisfy \(\|\Delta A\|_2\leq\varepsilon_A\) and \(\|\delta g\|_2\leq\varepsilon_g\), with \(A+\Delta A\) retaining full row rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth constrained optimization using first-order least-squares multiplier estimates. Noise includes rounding, derivative error, and other bounded perturbations of the working-set Jacobian or objective gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The attainable multiplier set under the stated data uncertainty is \[\Lambda_{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_g}(A,g)=\left\{\widehat\lambda(A+\Delta A,g+\delta g):\|\Delta A\|_2\leq\varepsilon_A,\ \|\delta g\|_2\leq\varepsilon_g\right\}.\] For a prescribed reliability tolerance \(\eta\geq0\), the nominal multiplier estimate is \((\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_g,\eta)\)-noisy when \[\sup_{\mu\in\Lambda_{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_g}(A,g)}\|\mu-\widehat\lambda(A,g)\|_2>\eta.\] For a sign tolerance \(\zeta\geq0\), component \(i\) is decision-noisy when the classification map \[s_\zeta(t)=\begin{cases}-1,&t<-\zeta,\\0,&|t|\leq\zeta,\\1,&t>\zeta\end{cases}\] is nonconstant on \(\{\mu_i:\mu\in\Lambda_{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_g}(A,g)\}\). Thus admissible numerical errors can change whether the multiplier is regarded as negative, indeterminate, or positive. This componentwise condition is the relevant failure when multiplier signs control deletion or retention of working-set constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the nominal multiplier as the least-squares fit of the objective gradient by the transposed working-set Jacobian. Perturb both numerical inputs within specified error bounds and collect all resulting estimates. The estimate is noisy at tolerance \(\eta\) if some admissible result differs from the nominal estimate by more than \(\eta\). A component is decision-noisy when admissible errors change its negative, near-zero, or positive sign classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A multiplier estimate is noisy precisely when its admissible perturbation image exceeds the prescribed reliability tolerance; it is decision-noisy in component \(i\) precisely when the corresponding attainable values do not share one \(\zeta\)-sign classification.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(I_i=\{\mu_i:\mu\in\Lambda_{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_g}(A,g)\}\), component \(i\) is decision-noisy exactly when \(|s_\zeta(I_i)|\geq2\).
For \(\zeta=0\), a sufficient and directly interpretable sign-instability condition is that \(I_i\) contain both a negative and a positive value.
special_cases_latex: When \(A^T\lambda=g\) is compatible, \(\widehat\lambda(A,g)\) equals the exact working-set multiplier.
If only the gradient is noisy, take \(\varepsilon_A=0\); if only the Jacobian is noisy, take \(\varepsilon_g=0\).
At a nonstationary point, \(A^T\lambda=g\) need not be compatible, but the least-squares estimate remains defined when \(A\) has full row rank.
immediate_consequences_latex: If an attainable component interval crosses the deletion threshold, multiplier sign alone cannot robustly determine whether its constraint should leave the working set.
Near-linear dependence of working-set rows can amplify small input perturbations and enlarge \(\Lambda_{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_g}(A,g)\).
A small computed negative multiplier need not certify a genuinely negative multiplier when its admissible perturbation set also contains zero or positive values.
boundary_notes: This definition concerns uncertainty of a specified estimator; it does not assert that every least-squares estimate is statistically biased.
If \(A\) loses full row rank under admissible perturbations, multiplier nonuniqueness must be modeled separately, for example by a chosen generalized-inverse convention.
Near-zero exact multipliers can make sign decisions intrinsically ambiguous even when arithmetic errors are small.
